Sprinkle with sesame seeds to finish.
tips: Add 1 sliced Cheongyang chili pepper for a spicy flavor.
Adding 1 tsp (about 7g) of oligosaccharide at the end gives it a nice shine.

french-toast.desc: Toast coated in a sweet egg wash and pan-fried.
french-toast.name: French Toast
steps: In a wide dish, smoothly beat egg 2, milk 100ml, sugar 1 tbsp, and salt 1 pinch.
Dip sandwich bread into the egg wash for 20 seconds on each side to soak through to the center. Be careful not to leave it in too long or it will tear.
Heat a pan over medium-low heat, grease it with cooking oil 1/2 tbsp, place 2 slices of sandwich bread, and cook for 2 minutes on each side until golden.
Cook the remaining sandwich bread using the same method with the remaining oil.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with sugar 1 tsp (about 4g) or oligosaccharide before eating.
tips: Sandwich bread that is a day old absorbs the egg wash better, which is great.
Melting butter 5g in the pan makes the flavor much better.

gaeseong-pyeonsu.desc: Gaeseong-style square summer dumplings stuffed with Korean zucchini and beef.
gaeseong-pyeonsu.name: Gaeseong Pyonsu
steps: Make a dough with 2 cup flour, 1/4 tsp salt, and 100 ml water, and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Cut the Korean zucchini into thin strips, salt it to squeeze out moisture, mince the beef, stir-fry with 1 tbsp soy sauce and sesame oil, and mix with tofu to make the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut into squares, place the filling, and pinch the four corners together.
Cook in boiling water or a steamer for 10 minutes and dip in soy sauce mixed with 1 tbsp vinegar to eat.
tips: Floating them in cold broth makes a great summer delicacy.
The thinner you roll the dumpling wrapper, the more delicious it tastes.

gajami-jorim.desc: Braised flounder cooked on a bed of Korean radish in a seasoned sauce.
gajami-jorim.name: Braised Flounder (Gajami-jorim)
steps: Prep the flounder and make score marks, cut the Korean radish thickly, and cut the onion into thin strips.
Place Korean radish and onion on the bottom of a pot, pour in 200 ml of water, and boil for 5 minutes.
Place the sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, and minced garlic on the flounder.
Braise over medium heat for 12 minutes while spooning the broth over it, then top with green onion.
tips: Do not flip the fish, just spoon the broth over it.
The Korean radish is so tasty it might be more popular than the flounder.

gaji-bokkeum.desc: A side dish of tenderly cooked eggplant soaked in a savory soy sauce seasoning.
gaji-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Eggplant
steps: Cut the eggplant in half lengthwise and slice into 1 cm-thick half-moons. Cut the onion into thin strips and slice thinly the green onion.
Heat a pan over medium heat, add 2 tbsp of cooking oil, add the eggplant, and stir-fry for 4 minutes until wilted.
Add the onion, minced garlic, and green onion, and stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Drizzle in 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of oligosaccharide syrup, stir-fry for 1 minute, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Eggplant absorbs oil quickly, so add it all at the beginning and do not add more in the middle.
Salting for 5 minutes and squeezing out the moisture makes it less chewy.

gaji-jeon.name: Pan-fried Eggplant (Gaji-jeon)
steps: Cut the eggplant diagonally 7mm thick, sprinkle with salt 1/4 tsp, let sit for 5 minutes, and pat dry.
Coat both sides with Korean pancake mix 4 tbsp and dip in beaten egg.
Add cooking oil to a pan over medium heat and pan-fry until golden for 3 minutes on each side.
Plate and serve with soy sauce dipping sauce.
tips: Eggplants absorb a lot of oil, so cook slowly over low heat.
Dip in the soy sauce dipping sauce.

gaji-namul.desc: Light and oil-free eggplant seasoned after being steamed.
gaji-namul.name: Seasoned Steamed Eggplant
steps: Remove the stem of the eggplant, cut into 4 lengthwise pieces, and cut into 5 cm lengths.
Boil 300 ml of water in a pot, place the eggplant in a steamer, cover with a lid, and steam for 5 minutes.
Take out to cool, squeeze out moisture gently, and tear along the grain by hand.
Add 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of sesame oil, minced garlic, Korean red pepper flakes, and slice thinly green onion, mix well, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Steaming too long will make it mushy. Keep it within 5 minutes.
Squeezing out the moisture firmly ensures the seasoning clings well.

galbi-jjim-pork.desc: Sweet and savory soy sauce-glazed braised pork ribs.
galbi-jjim-pork.name: Braised Pork Ribs (Galbi-jjim)
steps: Soak the pork in cold water for 30 minutes to remove blood, then blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse.
In a pot, combine the pork, soy sauce 5 tbsp, sugar 2 tbsp, minced garlic, mirin 2 tbsp, and water 500 ml, and simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes.
Cut the potato, carrot, and onion into large chunks, add them in, and braise for 20 minutes.
Turn off the heat once the broth is slightly reduced.
tips: Blanching removes gamey odors and excess fat.
Blending pear and adding it makes the meat tender.

galbitang.desc: A clear soup containing generous pieces of short ribs.
galbitang.name: Beef Short Rib Soup (Galbitang)
steps: Soak the beef in cold water for 1 hour to draw out the blood, blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes, and rinse.
Put water 2 L, beef, and Korean radish in a pot and simmer over medium-low heat for 70 minutes.
Season the broth with minced garlic, soup soy sauce 2 tbsp, and salt 1 tsp, add soaked glass noodles, and boil for 5 minutes.
Top with green onion and black pepper.
tips: Chilling it and removing the fat makes it clean.
Adding large-cut Korean radish makes it refreshing.

galchi-gui.desc: Crispy pan-fried hairtail seasoned simply with salt.
galchi-gui.name: Pan-Fried Hairtail (Galchi-gui)
steps: Wash the hairtail, pat it dry thoroughly with a paper towel, sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of salt, and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Coat a pan with 2 tbsp of cooking oil and fry one side of the hairtail over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Flip and fry for another 4 minutes until golden brown.
Transfer to a plate and serve with lemon on the side.
tips: Patting the fish dry prevents the skin from sticking to the pan.
Avoid moving the fish around too much while frying.

galchi-jorim.desc: Hairtail fish braised with a bed of Korean radish in a savory seasoning.
galchi-jorim.name: Braised Hairtail (Galchi Jorim)
steps: Cut the hairtail into pieces, wash, and pat dry. Cut the Korean radish thick and the onion into large pieces.
Place the Korean radish and onion at the bottom of a pot, pour 300 ml water, and boil for 5 minutes.
Mix 2 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp minced garlic, and 1 tbsp sugar to make the sauce.
Place the hairtail on top, drizzle the sauce over it, braise over medium heat for 15 minutes, and top with green onion.
tips: Cook the Korean radish first so it absorbs the seasoning and the hairtail doesn't break apart.
Spoon the broth over the fish as it braises.

gambas.desc: An appetizer where shrimp is cooked in garlic oil and dipped in bread.
gambas.name: Shrimp Gambas (Saewu Gambas)
steps: Soak frozen shrimp in cold water for 10 minutes to thaw and thoroughly wipe away moisture with a paper towel. Season with 1/3 tsp salt and black pepper.
Slice thinly Cheongyang chili, cut sandwich bread into bite-sized pieces, and toast in a dry pan for 1 minute each.
In a small pan, add 4 tbsp cooking oil, minced garlic, and Cheongyang chili, and heat over low heat for 3 minutes to bring out the garlic aroma.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes on each side. They are done when they turn pink and curl into a circle.
Turn off the heat and dip the toasted sandwich bread into the oil.
tips: Make sure to dry the shrimp thoroughly to prevent oil from splattering.
Stir-frying boiled noodles in the remaining oil makes aglio e olio.

gamja-chae-jeon.desc: Crispy Korean pancake made with thin potato strips.
gamja-chae-jeon.name: Pan-Fried Shredded Potato Jeon (Gamja-chae-jeon)
steps: Peel the potato, cut into thin strips, soak in cold water for 5 minutes to remove starch, drain in a sieve, and squeeze out the moisture.
Toss the potato with 1/3 tsp of salt and 2 tbsp of Korean pancake mix.
Heat 3 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, and spread the potato thinly.
Pan-fry until golden brown, pressing down for 4 minutes on each side.
tips: Squeezing out the moisture makes it crispy.
Fry it thin so the inside cooks through.

gamja-jorim.desc: Sweet and salty braised potatoes cooked in a soy sauce glaze.
gamja-jorim.name: Braised Potatoes (Gamja-jorim)
steps: Peel the potato, cut into 2.5cm cubes, soak in cold water for 5 minutes to remove starch, and pat dry.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan (or pot) over medium heat and sauté the potato for 3 minutes until the surface is slightly translucent.
Add 200ml of water, 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, and minced garlic, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce to medium-low heat, cover with a lid, and braise for 10 minutes.
When a chopstick easily pierces the potato, open the lid, add 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, and braise for 3 to 4 minutes until almost no broth is left.
Add 1 tsp of sesame oil and sesame seeds, mix, and turn off the heat.
tips: Stirring too often while braising will break the potato, so stir only occasionally.
Adding 1 Cheongyang chili makes it sweet and spicy.

gamja-ongsimi.desc: Chewy potato dumplings made from freshly grated potatoes.
gamja-ongsimi.name: Potato Dumpling Soup (Gamja Ongsimi)
steps: Peel the potato, grate it on a grater, wrap it in cheesecloth to squeeze out the water, and save the settled starch.
Mix the squeezed potato and the starch, add a little salt, and shape into bite-sized round balls.
Boil the anchovy and kombu in water 1L for 10 minutes, remove them, and season the broth with soup soy sauce 2 tbsp.
Add the potato dumpling and Korean zucchini to the broth, and when they float to the top, boil for 3 more minutes.
tips: You must save and add the starch together to make them chewy.
Adding perilla seeds makes the potato dumpling soup nutty and savory.

gamja-sujebi.desc: A warm soup with chewy hand-torn wheat flour dough pieces.
gamja-sujebi.name: Potato Hand-Pulled Dough Soup (Gamja Sujebi)
steps: In a bowl, combine flour 100g, salt 1/4 tsp, water 60 ml, and cooking oil 1 tsp, knead for 5 minutes to make a dough. Wrap in plastic and let rest in the refrigerator for 20 minutes.
Put water 900 ml and anchovy in a pot, boil for 7 minutes after it comes to a boil, then remove the anchovy.
Cut the potato into half-moons 0.5cm thick, cut the Korean zucchini and onion into thin strips, slice the green onion thinly, and add the potato first to boil for 5 minutes.
Flatten the dough thinly with your hands and tear it into the pot, add the onion and Korean zucchini, and boil for another 5 minutes. When the sujebi floats to the top, it is cooked.
Season with soy sauce 1 and 1/2 tbsp, minced garlic, and salt 1/4 tsp, add the green onion, and boil for 1 minute.
tips: Resting the dough makes it chewy.
The thinner you tear the sujebi, the faster it cooks and the better the texture.

gamja-tteok.desc: Chewy potato dumplings stuffed with sweet red bean paste.
gamja-tteok.name: Gangwon-do Potato Rice Cake (Gamja-tteok)
steps: Grate the potato on a grater, squeeze out the liquid in a cotton cloth, and collect the settled starch.
Mash the boiled red bean and mix with 2 tbsp of sugar to make the filling.
Mix the squeezed potato with 4 tbsp of starch and 1/3 tsp of salt to make a dough, then shape into balls filled with the red bean.
Steam for 20 minutes in a steamer with rising steam.
tips: Leave them for 3 minutes because they can burst if touched right after steaming.
They won't stick together if you brush them with sesame oil.

ganjang-bibim-guksu.desc: Soy sauce mixed noodles with a great sesame oil aroma.
ganjang-bibim-guksu.name: Soy Sauce Mixed Noodles (Ganjang Bibim-guksu)
steps: Put thin wheat noodles in boiling water, boil for 3 minutes, rub and rinse in cold water, and drain.
Mix soy sauce 1.5 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tsp, and sesame oil 1 tbsp in a bowl.
Add the thin wheat noodles, mix well, and top with the egg, crushed roasted seaweed, and sesame seeds.
Serve in a bowl and mix to eat right away.
tips: Rub and wash the thin wheat noodles vigorously in cold water to make them chewy.
Topping with plenty of roasted seaweed makes it taste great.

garlic-bread-simple.desc: Crispy garlic bread baked in an air fryer or pan.
garlic-bread-simple.name: Garlic Bread
steps: Leave butter at room temperature to soften, and mix with 1 tbsp of minced garlic and 1 tbsp of sugar.
Spread the garlic butter evenly on one side of the sandwich bread.
Toast golden brown in a pan or air fryer at 160 degrees for 4-5 minutes.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and serve.
tips: Melting the butter in a double boiler helps spread it evenly on the bread.
Add parsley if you have some.

gemmatsal-egg-roll.desc: Sweet and savory lunchbox side dish made with imitation crab.
gemmatsal-egg-roll.name: Imitation Crab Rolled Omelette (Gemmatsal-egg-roll)
steps: Tear the imitation crab lengthwise or cut into thirds. Mince the green onion finely.
Beat 3 eggs with the green onion and 1/4 tsp of salt.
Lightly coat a pan with cooking oil over low heat, pour half of the egg wash, and when the edges are cooked, place the imitation crab on top and roll it up.
Roll one more time with the remaining egg wash, let it cool down slightly, and slice it.
tips: You should divide the egg wash into two parts so the thickness is even.
If you place the imitation crab in a single line down the center, the cross-section looks pretty.

gemmatsal-oi-muchim.desc: A sweet, tangy, and crunchy summer side dish.
gemmatsal-oi-muchim.name: Imitation Crab and Cucumber Salad (Gemmatsal Oi Muchim)
steps: Cut the cucumber in half lengthwise, slice thinly on an angle, marinate with salt 1/3 tsp for 5 minutes, and squeeze out the excess moisture firmly.
Tear the imitation crab into long strips.
Mix vinegar 1 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, and mayonnaise 1 tbsp in a bowl.
Add the cucumber and imitation crab, toss together, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Be sure to squeeze the cucumber firmly after marinating so it stays crunchy.
Leaving out the mayonnaise makes it even more refreshing.

geonsaeu-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Dried Shrimp (Geonsaeu Bokkeum)
steps: Stir-fry the dried shrimp in a dry pan over low heat for 2 minutes to remove the fishy smell.
Add cooking oil 1 tsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, and oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp into the pan and bring to a boil.
Add the dried shrimp, toss for 1 minute and 30 seconds, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Let it cool and store in an airtight container.
tips: Stir-fry over low heat so they do not burn.
Mixing in nuts turns this into a calcium-rich snack.

geonsaeu-hobak-guk.desc: A clear, refreshing Korean zucchini soup simmered with dried shrimp.
geonsaeu-hobak-guk.name: Dried Shrimp and Korean Zucchini Soup (Geonsaeu Hobak-guk)
steps: Toast the dried shrimp in a dry pan to get rid of the fishy smell. Cut the Korean zucchini into half-moons and cut the onion into thin strips.
Put 600 ml of water and dried shrimp in a pot and boil for 5 minutes to make the broth.
Add the Korean zucchini, onion, and minced garlic, and boil for 5 minutes.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce and top with the green onion.
tips: Toasting the dried shrimp makes the broth much more savory.
Adding tofu makes it filling.

gochu-jeon.desc: Spicy chili peppers stuffed with a savory tofu and meat filling.
gochu-jeon.name: Stuffed Chili Peppers (Gochu Jeon)
steps: Cut the Cheongyang chili in half to remove the seeds, squeeze the excess water out of the tofu, and mash it together with the pork and 1/3 tsp of salt.
Dust the inside of the Cheongyang chili with flour, stuff it with the filling, and press down.
Coat the filling side with flour and dip into beaten egg (2 eggs).
Heat a pan over medium heat, add cooking oil, and cook starting with the filling side down for 3 minutes, then flip and cook for 2 minutes.
tips: Use regular chili peppers if you prefer it less spicy.
Spread the filling thinly so it cooks all the way through.

gochujapchae.desc: Stir-fried bell pepper and pork cooked over high heat.
gochujapchae.name: Stir-Fried Pork and Bell Peppers (Gochujapchae)
steps: Cut pork into thin strips and marinate for 10 minutes with 1/2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of starch, and black pepper. Cut bell pepper and onion lengthwise into 0.5cm-wide strips.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1 tbsp of cooking oil, and stir-fry green onion and minced garlic for 20 seconds.
Add pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes to cook, then add onion and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add bell pepper, 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, the remaining 1/2 tbsp of soy sauce, and sugar, stir-fry quickly over high heat for 1 minute, and turn off the heat.
tips: Vegetables should be stir-fried briefly over high heat to stay crisp.
Serve with rice or dumplings for a complete meal.

godeungeo-gui.desc: Crispy pan-fried mackerel seasoned simply with salt.
godeungeo-gui.name: Pan-fried Mackerel (Godeungeo-gui)
steps: Pat the mackerel thoroughly dry with a paper towel and make 2 to 3 score marks on the skin.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp salt and black pepper on both sides and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, place the skin side down first, and cook for 5 minutes.
Flip and cook for 4 more minutes until cooked through to the center. It is done when the flesh flakes easily with a chopstick.
tips: Drying off the moisture prevents oil splatters and makes the skin crispy.
You can also cook it in an air fryer at 180°C for 12 minutes.

godeungeo-mu-jorim.desc: A spicy braised mackerel dish with tender Korean radish soaked in savory sauce.
godeungeo-mu-jorim.name: Braised Mackerel and Radish (Godeungeo-mu-jorim)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into thick 1.5 cm pieces, cut the onion in half and cut into thin strips, and slice the green onion diagonally. Cut the mackerel into portions and pat dry.
Place the Korean radish at the bottom of a pot, pour in 400 ml water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium heat and cook for 10 minutes.

Dissolve the sauce made of 1.5 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1 tbsp mirin, and minced ginger into the broth, then top with the mackerel and onion.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes while spooning the broth over the fish, then add the green onion and cook for 2 more minutes.
tips: Do not stir the mackerel as it will break apart; just ladle the broth over it.
Ginger helps remove the fishy smell.

goguma-jeon.desc: Pan-fried sweet potato pancake with a sweet flavor.
goguma-jeon.name: Sweet Potato Pancake (Goguma-jeon)
steps: Cut the sweet potato to 7mm thickness and blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Coat with 4 tbsp Korean pancake mix and dip in beaten egg mixed with 1/4 tsp salt.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over low heat and pan-fry for 4 minutes on each side.
Let steam escape slightly and arrange on a plate.
tips: Blanching helps the inside cook quickly.
It is also great as a kid's snack.

goguma-latte.desc: A warm latte made by blending sweet sweet potatoes.
goguma-latte.name: Sweet Potato Latte (Goguma Latte)
steps: Peel the sweet potato and boil or steam it until tender.
Combine the sweet potato, 300 ml of milk, and 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup in a blender and blend until smooth.
Transfer to a pot and heat over low heat for 3 minutes.
Pour into a cup and top with mixed nuts.
tips: Instead of adding all the milk at once, add it gradually while blending to easily adjust the thickness.
It is also delicious served cold.

goguma-matang.desc: Crispy and sweet candied sweet potatoes.
goguma-matang.name: Candied Sweet Potatoes (Goguma Matang)
steps: Cut the sweet potato with skin on into bite-sized pieces, soak in water for 10 minutes to remove starch, and pat dry.
Put cooking oil 6 tbsp in a pan and pan-fry the sweet potato over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Wipe the oil off with a paper towel, add sugar 3 tbsp and oligosaccharide syrup 2 tbsp, and melt over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add the sweet potato, toss for 1 minute to coat, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Do not stir the sugar; swirl the pan to melt it so it won't crystallize.
It hardens as it cools, so eat right away.

goguma-salad.desc: A salad made by mixing mashed sweet potato and apple with mayonnaise.
goguma-salad.name: Sweet Potato Salad (Goguma Salad)
steps: Peel the sweet potato, boil or steam it until softly cooked, and mash it while it is hot.
Dice the apple finely and chop the mixed nuts coarsely.
Mix the mashed sweet potato with 3 tbsp mayonnaise and 1/4 tsp salt.
Add the apple and mixed nuts and mix well.
tips: Mash the sweet potato while it is hot so it mashes smoothly.
It is also great served on white bread as a sandwich.

gondre-bap.desc: Gangwon-do style rice cooked with gondre thistle.
gondre-bap.name: Gondre Rice (Gondre Bap)
steps: Soak the uncooked rice for 30 minutes, rinse the gondre in water, cut into 3cm lengths, and toss in perilla oil 1/2 tbsp.
Put the uncooked rice, water 300ml, and gondre in a pot and boil over high heat.
When it comes to a boil, reduce to low heat for 15 minutes, turn off the heat, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Make a seasoned soy sauce with soy sauce 3 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes, minced garlic, slice thinly green onion, perilla oil 1/2 tbsp, and sesame seeds, then mix it in.
tips: Dried gondre needs to be boiled and soaked for a day to become tender.
Match the amount of water to the same volume as the rice.

gosari-bokkeum.desc: Stir-fried boiled fiddlehead ferns fragrant with perilla oil.
gosari-bokkeum.name: Seasoned and Stir-Fried Fiddlehead Ferns (Gosari-bokkeum)
steps: Rinse the boiled fiddlehead ferns in cold water, squeeze out the water, and cut into 5 cm lengths. Slice the green onion thinly.
Place the fiddlehead ferns in a bowl with soup soy sauce 1 tbsp and minced garlic, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat perilla oil 1 tbsp in a pan and stir-fry the fiddlehead ferns over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour in water 100 ml, cover with a lid, cook over low heat for 8 minutes, open the lid to let the moisture evaporate, and finish by adding the green onion and sesame seeds.
tips: For dried fiddlehead ferns, use ones that have been soaked overnight and boiled.
Perilla oil is sensitive to heat, so lower the flame at the very end.

greek-salad.desc: Mediterranean salad topped with olive and cheese.
greek-salad.name: Greek Salad
steps: Dice cucumber and tomato into bite-sized pieces, cut onion into thin strips, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, and drain.
Mix 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/3 tsp salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Place vegetables and black olive in a bowl, tear cheese into small pieces, and place them on top.
Drizzle with the dressing.
tips: Removing the seeds from tomato reduces excess liquid.
Toss just before eating.

gul-gukbap.desc: Clear winter rice soup made with Korean radish and oyster.
gul-gukbap.name: Oyster Rice Soup (Gul-gukbap)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into flat, thin rectangle slices, wash the oyster in saltwater, and drain in a sieve. Slice the green onion diagonally.
Coat a pot with 1 tsp of sesame oil, sauté the Korean radish over medium heat for 2 minutes, pour 700 ml of water, and boil for 10 minutes.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, 1/2 tsp of salt, and minced garlic.
Add the oyster and boil for only 2 minutes, then add the green onion, put cooked rice in a bowl, and pour the broth over it.
tips: You must boil the oyster for only the last 2 minutes to keep it plump.
It becomes spicy and refreshing if you serve it with black pepper or Cheongyang chili.

gul-jeon.desc: Winter jeon that highlights the ocean flavor of the oyster.
gul-jeon.name: Oyster Pancake (Gul-jeon)
steps: Gently rinse the oyster in saltwater, drain in a sieve, and season with 1/3 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Beat 2 eggs. Coat the oyster lightly with flour, shake off the excess, and dip into the egg wash.
Heat 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, place the oyster, and pan-fry for 1 minute 30 seconds on each side.
Serve with a dipping sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of vinegar.
tips: If you pan-fry the oyster for too long, it shrinks and becomes tough.
You must drain the oyster thoroughly so the egg coating does not peel off.

gul-sundubu.desc: Refreshing soft tofu stew with oysters.
gul-sundubu.name: Oyster Soft Tofu Stew (Gul Sundubu Jjigae)
steps: Swish the oysters in light saltwater to wash and drain them, and slice thinly the green onion.
In a pot, stir-fry 1 tbsp of cooking oil, 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, and minced garlic over low heat for 1 minute.
Pour 300 ml of water, and when it comes to a boil, add large chunks of soft tofu and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the oysters and 1 tsp of soup soy sauce, boil for just 2 minutes, and top with the green onion.
tips: Oysters shrink if boiled too long, so add them at the end.
Omit the Korean red pepper flakes to make a clear soft tofu soup.

gulbi-jorim.desc: Yellow croaker braised in a savory soy sauce seasoning.
gulbi-jorim.name: Braised Yellow Croaker (Gulbi-jorim)
steps: Make score marks on the yellow croaker and cut the Korean radish into thick pieces.
Place the Korean radish at the bottom of a pot and put the yellow croaker on top.
Mix soy sauce 3 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and water 200 ml, then pour it over.
Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes, spooning the broth over the fish, then top with Cheongyang chili and green onion.
tips: If the yellow croaker is too salty, add a little more water.
Do not flip the fish while braising.

gun-mandu.desc: The easiest way to make frozen dumplings crispy.
gun-mandu.name: Pan-Fried Dumplings (Gun-Mandu)
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, place the frozen dumpling in the pan without overlapping, and fry for 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden.
Pour 3 tbsp (45ml) of water along the edge of the pan, immediately cover with the lid, and steam over low heat for 4 minutes. You can stop when the dumpling wrapper becomes translucent.
Open the lid and fry for 1 minute longer until the moisture evaporates, making the bottom crispy.
Mix 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1/2 tbsp of vinegar, and Korean red pepper flakes to serve as a dipping sauce.
tips: Oil may splatter when pouring water, so use the lid as a shield.
They also turn out crispy when baked in an air fryer at 180 degrees for 8 minutes.

gungjung-tteokbokki.desc: Beef and vegetable gungjung tteokbokki stir-fried in a soy sauce seasoning.
gungjung-tteokbokki.name: Royal Court Rice Cake (Gungjung Tteokbokki)
steps: Blanch the rice cake in boiling water, drain, and cut the beef, onion, carrot, and mushroom into bite-sized pieces.
Mix soy sauce 3 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 1 tbsp and stir-fry the beef and vegetables over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add the rice cake and sauce, stir-fry for 3 more minutes, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching the rice cake beforehand helps the sauce absorb better.
Leaving out gochujang makes it the royal court style.

gwangjang-mayak-gimbap.desc: Mini rice rolls from Gwangjang Market dipped in mustard soy sauce.
gwangjang-mayak-gimbap.name: Gwangjang Market 'Drug' Gimbap (Mayak Gimbap)
steps: Cut carrot into thin strips and sauté in 1 tsp cooking oil with salt, then cut pickled yellow radish thinly. Mix sesame oil and salt into cooked rice.
Cut roasted seaweed in half, spread cooked rice thinly, place carrot and pickled yellow radish on top, and roll up tightly into thin cylinders.
Brush sesame oil on the outside and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Dip in a sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp soy sauce, mustard, and 1 tsp vinegar.
tips: Spread the cooked rice thinly to make slender gimbap.
Adjust the amount of mustard to your preferred spice level.

gwangjang-nokdu-bindaetteok.desc: Crispy mung bean pancakes made from ground mung beans.
gwangjang-nokdu-bindaetteok.name: Gwangjang Market Mung Bean Pancake (Nokdu Bindaetteok)
steps: Soak mung bean for 4 hours, remove the skins, and grind coarsely in a blender with 200 ml water.
Mince pork, chop kimchi finely, slice mung bean sprout and green onion thinly, and mix them into the batter with 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat a generous amount of cooking oil in a pan, spoon thick layers of the batter, and pan-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side until crispy.
Drain excess oil, place on a plate, and serve with soy sauce.
tips: Pour plenty of cooking oil to make it crispy.
Removing the skins from mung bean gives a nice color and soft texture.

gwangju-duck-tang.desc: Savory duck soup boiled with perilla seeds and dried radish greens.
gwangju-duck-tang.name: Gwangju-style Duck Soup (Gwangju Duck Tang)
steps: Blanch duck in boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and rinse, and cut dried radish greens to 3cm.
Put duck, water 1.5L, and doenjang 1 tbsp in a pot, boil on high heat, skim off the foam, and simmer on medium heat for 35 minutes.
Add dried radish greens, minced garlic, and soup soy sauce 2 tbsp, and boil for 10 minutes.
Add perilla seed powder 5 tbsp and green onion, and boil for 5 more minutes.
tips: Skim off the oil once after blanching the duck.
Add perilla seed powder at the end for a nutty flavor.

gyeongsang-beef-mu-guk.desc: Daegu and Gyeongbuk-style spicy beef soup boiled with Korean red pepper flakes and soybean sprouts.
gyeongsang-beef-mu-guk.name: Gyeongsang-style Beef and Radish Soup (Gyeongsang-sik Sogogi Mu-guk)
steps: Soak beef in cold water for 15 minutes to remove blood, cut Korean radish into flat bite-sized pieces, and cut largely green onion.
Heat sesame oil 1 tbsp in a pot, stir-fry beef over medium heat for 3 minutes, add Korean red pepper flakes 3 tbsp, and stir-fry over low heat for 1 minute.
Add Korean radish and water 1.2 L, skim off foam when it boils, and boil over medium-low heat for 30 minutes.
Add soybean sprout, minced garlic, and soup soy sauce 2 tbsp, and boil with the lid open for 7 minutes.
Add green onion and finish with salt 1/2 tsp.
tips: Stري-frying Korean red pepper flakes in oil makes the broth deep and red.
You must boil soybean sprout with the lid open so it doesn't smell fishy.

gyeongsang-hutjesa-tang.desc: A clear ancestral rite soup from Gyeongsang-do made with beef, Korean radish, and tofu.
gyeongsang-hutjesa-tang.name: Gyeongsang Ancestral Rite Soup (Gyeongsang Tangguk)
steps: Cut Korean radish flat, tofu thickly, and beef into bite-sized pieces.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and stir-fry beef and Korean radish for 3 minutes.
Add 1 L of water and kombu, boil for 20 minutes, and take out kombu.
Add tofu, green onion, 2 tbsp of soup soy sauce, and 1/2 tsp of salt, then boil for 5 minutes.
tips: It is characterized by being boiled clear with almost no seasoning.
Leftover soup from ancestral rites tastes even deeper the next day.

gyeran-ppang.desc: A street snack baked with a whole egg inside.
gyeran-ppang.name: Egg Bread (Gyeran-ppang)
steps: Mix 1 cup of flour, 1 egg, 100 ml of milk, 1 tbsp of sugar, and 1/4 tsp of salt to make the batter.
Grease a muffin tin or deep pan with butter and fill it halfway with the batter.
Crack remaining eggs one by one on top.
Bake in an oven or air fryer preheated to 180 degrees for 15 minutes and let cool slightly.
tips: Fill only halfway because the batter will overflow if you add too much.
Sprinkling a little salt and pepper will season it right.

gyudon.desc: Japanese-style rice bowl topped with sweet and salty beef and onions.
gyudon.name: Gyudon
steps: Cut onion into 0.5 cm thick strips and cut beef into bite-sized pieces. Slice thinly green onion.
In a pot, add 150ml water, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, and 1 tbsp sugar, and boil over medium heat.
When the broth boils, add onion and cook for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add beef and boil for 3 minutes until the redness disappears. Skim off any rising foam.
Place 1 serving of cooked rice (210g) in each bowl and top with beef, onion, and 3 tbsp (45ml) of broth each.
Top with a soft-boiled egg, egg yolk, or green onion.
tips: Cooking the beef too long will make it tough. Remove it as soon as the color changes.
If you are uncomfortable eating raw eggs, substitute with a 7-minute soft-boiled egg.

gyul-chicken-salad.desc: A refreshing chicken salad with sweet mandarin oranges.
gyul-chicken-salad.name: Mandarin Chicken Salad
steps: Boil the chicken breast in boiling water for 12 minutes, let cool, and tear along the grain.
Peel the mandarin orange and separate the segments. Tear the iceberg lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Mix 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/3 tsp salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Place the chicken breast and mandarin orange on top of the iceberg lettuce and drizzle with the dressing.
tips: The sweetness of the mandarin orange pairs well with the mild flavor of the chicken breast.
You can also use oranges or grapefruits.

haeju-bibimbap.desc: Hwanghae-do style bibimbap topped with chicken breast and seasoned vegetables.
haeju-bibimbap.name: Haeju Bibimbap
steps: Boil the chicken breast, shred it, and mix with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp sesame oil.
Blanch the soybean sprout and spinach, season with sesame oil and soy sauce, and cut into thin strips and stir-fry the carrot.
Make an egg garnish and cut into thin strips.
Place cooked rice, seasoned vegetables, and chicken breast in a bowl, and serve with a sauce mixed with 1 tbsp soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil to mix together.
tips: It is a clean-tasting bibimbap mixed with soy sauce seasoning instead of gochujang.
Season the vegetables lightly.

haemul-pajeon.desc: A crispy seafood pancake made with squid and shrimp.
haemul-pajeon.name: Seafood and Green Onion Pancake (Haemul Pajeon)
steps: Cut the green onion into 15cm lengths, and chop the squid and shrimp finely.
In a bowl, mix 100g of Korean pancake mix and 180ml of water to make a thin batter.
Heat a pan over medium heat, add 3 tbsp of cooking oil, lay the green onion out neatly, pour in the batter, and top with the seafood.
Beat 2 eggs, pour them over the top, and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, add the remaining 1 tbsp of cooking oil, and cook for another 4 minutes while pressing down to make it crispy.
tips: Use plenty of oil for a crispy texture.
Serve with soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

ham-cheese-toast.desc: A breakfast made with two slices of sandwich bread, ham, and cheese.
ham-cheese-toast.name: Ham and Cheese Toast
steps: Lightly grease a pan heated over medium-low heat with cooking oil 1 tsp using a paper towel, crack egg, and fry for 1 minute 30 seconds to set.
On top of one slice of sandwich bread, place ham 2 slices, cheese 1 slice, and the fried egg in order, and cover with another slice of sandwich bread.
Place in the pan, press down over medium-low heat for 1 minute 30 seconds on each side, and toast until golden. It is done when the cheese melts.
Cut in half and serve with ketchup.
tips: Spreading a thin layer of mayonnaise on the outside of the sandwich bread and toasting makes it crispier.
Adding 2 slices of cheese makes it stretch even more.

ham-egg-jeon.desc: A savory ham pancake great for lunchbox side dishes.
ham-egg-jeon.name: Pan-fried Ham and Egg (Ham Egg Jeon)
steps: Wipe the oil off the ham with a paper towel and prepare each slice. Beat 2 eggs and mix in salt 1 pinch.
Lightly coat both sides of the ham with Korean pancake mix 3 tbsp and shake off any excess.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, dip the ham into the egg wash, and place in the pan.
Pan-fry the front side for 1 minute 30 seconds and the back side for 1 minute until golden, then transfer to a paper towel to drain the oil.
tips: Since the ham is salty, add just a tiny pinch of salt to the egg wash.
Adding minced carrot and onion adds more nutrition.

ham-fried-rice.desc: A fried rice made by clearing out leftover vegetables.
ham-fried-rice.name: Ham and Vegetable Fried Rice (Ham-Yachae-Bokeumbap)
steps: Cut the ham, onion, and carrot into 5mm fine dices. Let the cooked rice cool down slightly.
In a pan heated over medium heat, add 1/2 tbsp of cooking oil, pour in the beaten egg, stir with chopsticks to make scrambled eggs, and set aside.
Add the remaining cooking oil, stir-fry the ham, carrot, and onion for 2 minutes, and once the onion becomes translucent, add the cooked rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Put the scrambled eggs back in, season with 1 tsp of soy sauce, salt, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
tips: Stir-fry quickly over high heat so the rice grains separate nicely.
Adding 1/2 tsp (about 3g) of oyster sauce gives it that restaurant taste.

ham-mustard-sandwich.desc: A simple sandwich enhanced by mustard.
ham-mustard-sandwich.name: Ham and Mustard Sandwich
steps: Spread mustard 1 tsp thinly on one piece of sandwich bread.
Place iceberg lettuce, 2 slices of ham, and 1 slice of cheese on top in order.
Cover with another piece of sandwich bread and press down gently with your hands.
Cut in half and eat.
tips: It is crunchier if you toast the sandwich bread in a dry pan first.
Adding a tomato slice is also good.

hamburg-steak.desc: A juicy grilled hamburg steak topped with sauce.
hamburg-steak.name: Hamburg Steak (Hambak Steak)
steps: Soak sandwich bread in 3 tbsp (45ml) milk for 5 minutes, mash with your hands, finely dice onion, stir-fry in a dry pan for 2 minutes, and let cool.
In a large bowl, add 300g pork, mashed sandwich bread, onion, 1 egg, 1/3 tsp salt, and black pepper, and knead for 2-3 minutes until sticky.
Divide the dough into 2 portions, toss back and forth between your hands to remove air, and shape into oval patties with a thickness of 2.5cm. Press the center slightly with your thumb.
Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over medium heat and pan-fry each side until golden for 3 minutes.
Pour 100ml water, cover with a lid, and cook over low heat for 6 minutes to cook through to the center. Pierce with a chopstick and check if clear juices come out.
Transfer to a plate, and in the same pan, add 3 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, and 3 tbsp (45ml) water, simmer for 1 minute, and pour the sauce over.
tips: Since it needs to cook through to the center, cook dough containing pork thoroughly.
Leaving the shaped patties in the refrigerator for 10 minutes keeps them from losing their shape.

hamgyeong-gamja-jeon.desc: A savory Hamgyeong-style bean paste soup with potato and Korean zucchini.
hamgyeong-gamja-jeon.name: Hamgyeong-style Potato and Doenjang Soup (Hamgyeong Gamja Makjang-guk)
steps: Cut potato, Korean zucchini, and tofu into bite-sized pieces.
Boil anchovy in water 700 ml for 5 min and remove them, dissolve doenjang 2 tbsp, add potato, and boil for 8 min.
Add Korean zucchini, minced garlic, and Korean red pepper flakes, then boil for 5 min.
Add tofu and green onion and boil for 3 min.
tips: Since the doenjang flavor is deep, add plenty of potato.
Adding Cheongyang chili pepper makes it spicy and refreshing.

hamheung-hoe-naengmyeon.desc: Hamheung-style cold noodles mixed with flounder in a sweet, sour, and spicy sauce.
hamheung-hoe-naengmyeon.name: Hamheung Spicy Raw Fish Cold Noodles (Hamheung Hoe Naengmyeon)
steps: Blanch flounder in boiling water for 2 minutes, shred the flesh thinly, and toss in 1 tbsp vinegar.
Make the sauce by mixing 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and minced garlic.
Boil naengmyeon noodles, rinse in cold water, drain, cut cucumber and Korean pear into thin strips, and boil egg to cut in half.
Toss naengmyeon noodles with the sauce, flounder, and garnishes, and mix well.
tips: Traditional recipes use skate or flounder raw, but blanch it for food safety.
Adjust the sourness with vinegar.

hobak-beombeok.desc: Chungcheong-do style pumpkin porridge made with kabocha squash, glutinous rice, and red beans.
hobak-beombeok.name: Sweet Pumpkin Porridge (Hobak-beombeok)
steps: Soak the glutinous rice for 30 minutes, peel the kabocha squash, and cut it into large pieces.
Put the kabocha squash and 600 ml of water in a pot, boil thoroughly for 12 minutes, and mash with a spatula.
Add the glutinous rice and boiled red bean, and simmer for 15 minutes while stirring over low heat.
Add 2 tbsp of sugar and 1/3 tsp of salt, and stir for another 5 minutes until thick.
tips: Stir frequently so it doesn't burn.
It thickens as it cools, so add a little extra water to adjust the consistency.

hobak-gochujang-jjigae.desc: A hearty stew featuring Korean zucchini and potato in a savory gochujang broth.
hobak-gochujang-jjigae.name: Zucchini Gochujang Stew (Hobak Gochujang Jjigae)
steps: Cut the Korean zucchini and potato into half-moons 0.7cm thick, dice the onion, cut the tofu into 2cm cubes, and slice the green onion and Cheongyang chili thinly.
Pour water 500 ml into a pot, dissolve gochujang 1 tbsp and doenjang 1/2 tbsp, and bring to a boil. If you have pork, add it now.
Add the potato first and boil over medium heat for 5 minutes. The edges of the potato should be half-cooked.
Add the onion, Korean zucchini, Korean red pepper flakes, and minced garlic, and boil for another 5 minutes.
Add the tofu, green onion, and Cheongyang chili, boil for 3 minutes, and finish.
tips: The longer gochujang boils, the sweeter it gets.
Boiling with 5 anchovies (about 5g) deepens the broth.

hobakip-ssambap.desc: Rice and ssmjang wrapped in steamed pumpkin leaves.
hobakip-ssambap.name: Pumpkin Leaf Ssambap (Hobakip-ssambap)
steps: Strip the fibers from the stems of the pumpkin leaves and wash them under running water.
Steam them in a steamer for 5 minutes, submerge them in cold water, and drain the water.
Stir-fry the anchovy in a dry pan for 2 minutes, mix it with ssamjang, and add finely chopped Cheongyang chili.
Place cooked rice and ssamjang on top of the pumpkin leaf and wrap to eat.
tips: You must peel the skin off the stems so they are not tough.
Serve alongside doenjang jjigae.

honey-butter-toast.desc: Sweet toast brushed with butter and honey.
honey-butter-toast.name: Honey Butter Toast
steps: Melt 1/2 tbsp butter in a pan and toast sandwich bread over medium-low heat for 2 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Spread the remaining butter on the toasted sandwich bread.
Drizzle honey evenly and serve.
Eat immediately while warm.
tips: Add honey after toasting so it doesn't burn.
You can also sprinkle cinnamon powder.

honey-ginger-tea.name: Honey Ginger Tea (Kkul Saenggang-cha)
steps: Peel the ginger and slice thinly.
Put ginger and water 500ml in a pot and boil on low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove the ginger and pour into a cup.
Add honey 2 tbsp, stir, and drink.
tips: Do not add honey when it is too hot; let it cool down a bit first.
Do not give honey to babies under 12 months of age.

honey-mustard-chicken-salad.desc: A chicken breast salad tossed in a sweet and tangy mustard dressing.
honey-mustard-chicken-salad.name: Chicken Breast Salad with Honey Mustard
steps: Boil 500 ml water and 1/3 tsp salt in a pot, add the chicken breast, cook over high heat for 2 minutes, turn off the heat, cover, and let sit for 12 minutes. Cool and shred along the grain.
Tear the iceberg lettuce, and cut the tomato and cucumber into bite-sized pieces.
Mix 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tbsp oligosaccharide syrup, 1 tbsp vinegar, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Arrange the vegetables and chicken breast in a bowl and drizzle with the dressing.
tips: The saltiness of mustard varies by brand, so taste and adjust accordingly.
Drizzle the dressing right before eating.

hongap-miyeok-guk.desc: Seaweed soup with a refreshing mussel broth.
hongap-miyeok-guk.name: Mussel Seaweed Soup (Hongap Miyeok Guk)
steps: Remove the beards from the mussels and scrub the shells to wash them. Soak the dried seaweed for 10 minutes and cut into 5 cm lengths.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the dried seaweed and minced garlic for 2 minutes.
Pour 700 ml of water, and when it comes to a boil, add the mussels and boil for 8 minutes until the shells open.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce.
tips: Discard any mussels that do not open their shells.
Mussels are naturally salty, so taste the soup before adjusting the soup soy sauce.

hongap-tang.desc: Clear and refreshing mussel broth, also great as a drinking snack.
hongap-tang.name: Mussel Soup (Honghap-tang)
steps: Remove the beards from the mussel and scrub the shells with a brush. Slice the green onion diagonally and slice thinly the Cheongyang chili.
Put 500 ml of water, 1 tbsp of mirin, and minced garlic in a pot and boil.
When it comes to a boil, add the mussel, cover with a lid, and boil for 5 minutes to make the shells open.
Season with 1/4 tsp of salt and add the green onion, Cheongyang chili, and black pepper to boil for 1 minute more.
tips: Discard any mussel that does not open its shell.
The broth can become salty, so add salt after tasting.

hongeo-muchim.desc: Skate salad seasoned tart and sweet with water dropwort and Korean radish.
hongeo-muchim.name: Skate Salad (Hongeo Muchim)
steps: Cut skate into bite-sized pieces and cut Korean radish into thin strips, marinate in vinegar 1 tbsp and sugar 1/2 tbsp for 5 minutes, and squeeze out the water.
Cut water dropwort to 5cm length.
Mix gochujang 2 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Add the sauce to skate, Korean radish, and water dropwort, toss well, and sprinkle sesame seeds.
tips: Toss just before eating so it does not release liquid.
Adjust the sweet and sour taste with vinegar to your liking.

hongeo-samhap.desc: A representative Jeolla-do drinking snack combining fermented skate, boiled pork slices, and aged kimchi.
hongeo-samhap.name: Fermented Skate Trios (Hongeo Samhap)
steps: Dissolve doenjang and green onion in 1 L of water, and when it boils, add pork, boil for 40 minutes, take it out, let it cool, and cut it thickly.
Slice skate thinly and lay out aged kimchi one leaf at a time to squeeze out the liquid.
Arrange skate, pork, and kimchi on a plate.
Wrap pork and skate together in kimchi and eat in one bite.
tips: If you are trying it for the first time, start with a small amount of skate.
It is also good with sesame oil dip or seasoned soybean paste.

hotdog.desc: A simple corn dog style hot dog coated in batter.
hotdog.name: Hot Dog
steps: Mix 100 g of flour, 1 egg, 80 ml of milk, and 1 tbsp of sugar in a bowl to make a thick batter.
Insert skewers into sausage, coat evenly with the batter, and roll in breadcrumbs.
Fry in 170 degree oil while rolling for 3 minutes until golden, or bake in an air fryer at 190 degrees for 8 minutes.
Serve with ketchup.
tips: If the batter is too runny, it will drip off. Make sure it is thick.
Spray cooking oil before baking in the air fryer.

hummus.desc: A smooth Middle Eastern spread made from chickpeas.
hummus.name: Hummus
steps: Drain the chickpea and squeeze the lemon juice.
Place the chickpea, 3 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, 1/3 tsp salt, and 3 tbsp water in a blender.
Blend until smooth, and if it is too thick, add 1 tbsp water at a time.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle a circle of olive oil on top, and serve.
tips: Blend for a long time to make it smooth.
Serve with bread or vegetable sticks for dipping.

hunje-oori-buchu-bokkeum.desc: A 10-minute dish stir-fried in smoked duck fat without extra oil.
hunje-oori-buchu-bokkeum.name: Smoked Duck and Garlic Chive Stir-fry (Hunje Oori Buchu Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips and cut the garlic chive into 5 cm lengths. Cut the smoked duck into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a pan without oil over medium heat, place the smoked duck on it, and stir-fry for 2 minutes to render the fat.
Add the onion and minced garlic, and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes to soften the onion.
Add soy sauce 1 tbsp and oyster sauce 1/2 tbsp, stir-fry for 30 seconds, add the garlic chive and black pepper, mix for just 20 seconds, and turn off the heat.
tips: Adding the garlic chive at the end prevents a raw grassy taste and keeps it crunchy.
Since the smoked duck is salty, taste the dish and reduce the soy sauce if needed.

hunje-oori-deopbap.desc: A rice bowl topped with smoked duck and onion stir-fried in a savory soy sauce.
hunje-oori-deopbap.name: Smoked Duck Rice Bowl (Hunje Oori Deopbap)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips, slice thinly the green onion, and cut the smoked duck into bite-sized pieces.
In a pan heated over medium heat without oil, stir-fry the smoked duck for 2 minutes to render the fat, add the onion, and stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Add 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of oligosaccharide syrup, then simmer down for 1 minute.
Place cooked rice in a bowl, top with the duck stir-fry, egg, and the green onion, then drizzle with 1 tsp of sesame oil.
tips: Breaking the egg yolk and mixing it in reduces the saltiness.
Adding sliced wild sesame leaves (perilla leaves) on top also goes well with it.

hunje-oori-fried-rice.desc: Savory fried rice stir-fried in rendered duck fat.
hunje-oori-fried-rice.name: Smoked Duck Fried Rice (Hunje Oori Fried Rice)
steps: Cut the smoked duck into 1cm pieces and mince finely the onion. Slice thinly the green onion.
In a pan heated over medium heat without oil, stir-fry the smoked duck for 2 minutes to render the fat.
Add the onion and the green onion, stir-fry for 1 minute, then crack in the egg and scramble it.
Add cooked rice, 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce, and black pepper, stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, and finish until fluffy.
tips: Since there is duck fat, cooking oil is not needed.
Using cold cooked rice makes it fluffier.

hunje-oori-kimchi-bokkeum.desc: Smoked duck and kimchi stir-fried together, great as a side dish or drinking snack.
hunje-oori-kimchi-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Smoked Duck and Kimchi (Hunje Oori Kimchi Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the kimchi into bite-sized pieces, cut the onion into thin strips, and slice the green onion thinly. Cut the smoked duck into bite-sized pieces.
Stir-fry the smoked duck in a pan heated over medium heat without oil for 2 minutes to render its fat.
Add the kimchi, onion, Korean red pepper flakes, and oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp, and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the green onion, sesame oil, and sesame seeds, mix for 30 seconds, and turn off the heat.
tips: Frying the kimchi in the smoked duck fat means you do not need extra oil.
The riper and sourer the kimchi, the better it tastes.

hunje-oori-salad.desc: A smoked duck salad served with a tangy mustard dressing.
hunje-oori-salad.name: Smoked Duck Salad (Hunje Oori Salad)
steps: Cook the smoked duck in a pan over medium heat for 1 minute on each side without oil to render out the fat.
Tear the iceberg lettuce, cut the tomato into wedges, and cut the onion into thin strips, soak them in water, then drain.
Mix 1 tbsp of mustard, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, 1 tbsp of vinegar, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Arrange the vegetables on a plate, top with the smoked duck, and drizzle with the dressing.
tips: Cooking to remove the duck fat makes it much cleaner.
Drizzle the dressing right before eating.

hunje-oori-sandwich.desc: A hearty sandwich filled with smoked duck and mustard.
hunje-oori-sandwich.name: Smoked Duck Sandwich
steps: Cook the smoked duck in a dry pan over medium heat for 1 minute on each side to drain the excess fat.
Spread mayonnaise and mustard on one slice of sandwich bread.
Layer the iceberg lettuce, tomato, and smoked duck in order.
Cover with another slice of sandwich bread and cut in half.
tips: Wiping away the duck fat with a paper towel keeps it clean.
Toasting the sandwich bread makes it crispier.

hunje-oori-ssam.desc: A meal of smoked duck and onion wrapped in leaf lettuce.
hunje-oori-ssam.name: Smoked Duck Wraps (Hunje Oori Ssam)
steps: Wash leaf lettuce and perilla leaf, shake off the water, and arrange them on a plate. Cut the onion into thin strips, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, and drain.
Mix mustard 1 tsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, and oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp to make a sauce, and toss the onion in it to make pickled onions.
Place the smoked duck in a pan without oil and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side.
Wrap by placing perilla leaf, smoked duck, pickled onion, and ssamjang on top of leaf lettuce.
tips: Pickling the onion with a tangy flavor cuts through the greasiness.
Grilling garlic to serve on the side enhances the flavor.

hutjesabap.desc: An Andong-style bibimbap where seasoned vegetables and tofu are mixed with soy sauce instead of gochujang.
hutjesabap.name: Heotjesabap (Andong-style Bibimbap)
steps: Blanch spinach and soybean sprout in boiling water, squeeze out the moisture, and toss with 1 tbsp sesame oil and salt. Stir-fry fiddlehead fern and bellflower root in 1 tbsp cooking oil.
Cut tofu into thick slices and pan-fry them in a pan until golden brown on both sides.
Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and sesame seeds to make the seasoned soy sauce.
Arrange cooked rice, vegetables, and tofu around a bowl, serve with the seasoned soy sauce, and mix well.
tips: It is characterized by mixing with soy sauce instead of gochujang.
The vegetables should be seasoned lightly to bring out their true flavor.

hwangtae-gui.desc: Daegwallyong dried pollack grilled with a spicy gochujang sauce.
hwangtae-gui.name: Grilled Dried Pollack (Hwangtae-gui)
steps: Lightly moisten the dried pollack in water for 3 minutes, take it out, squeeze out the water, and remove the bones.
Mix 2 tbsp of gochujang, Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, minced garlic, oligosaccharide syrup, and sesame oil to make the sauce.
Thoroughly coat the dried pollack with the sauce.
Add 1 tbsp of cooking oil to a pan and grill on low heat for 3 minutes on each side without burning.
tips: Just moisten them slightly because soaking them too long drains the flavor.
Keep the heat low since the sauce burns easily.

hwangtae-haejangguk.desc: A refreshing dried pollack soup boiled with Korean radish and tofu.
hwangtae-haejangguk.name: Dried Pollack Hangover Soup (Hwangtae Haejangguk)
steps: Soak the dried pollack in water for 5 minutes, squeeze out the water, cut into 3cm pieces, and cut the Korean radish into bite-sized thin rectangular pieces.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and sauté the dried pollack and Korean radish over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour 900ml of water, boil for 15 minutes, then add tofu, minced garlic, 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, and 1/3 tsp of salt, and boil for 5 minutes.
Beat the egg, drizzle it around the soup, and top with green onion.
tips: Sautéing the dried pollack in sesame oil makes the broth milky and rich.
Keep it mild and non-spicy when your stomach hurts.

janchi-noodles.desc: Noodles in a warm anchovy broth.
janchi-noodles.name: Banquet Noodles (Janchi Guksu)
steps: Put 1 L of water and 10 anchovies in a pot, boil over high heat, and when it boils, simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes and remove the anchovies.
Season the broth with 2 tbsp of soy sauce, minced garlic, and 1 pinch of salt.
Cut the Korean zucchini into thin strips and stir-fry in a pan coated with 1 tsp of cooking oil for 1 minute, beat the egg, make a thin egg garnish, and cut it into thin strips.
Boil 2 L of water in another pot, cook the thin wheat noodles for 3 to 4 minutes, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Put the thin wheat noodles in a bowl, pour the hot broth over them, and top with the Korean zucchini, egg garnish, and slice thinly green onion.
tips: Noodles will get soggy if left in the broth too long, so pour the broth right before eating.
Serving with a seasoned soy sauce mixture (1 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tsp sesame oil) makes it even tastier.

japchae.desc: A festive side dish of glass noodles and vegetables stir-fried in a savory soy sauce seasoning.
japchae.name: Glass Noodle Stir-Fry (Japchae)
steps: Soak glass noodles in cold water for 30 min. Blanch spinach in boiling water for 30 sec, rinse in cold water, squeeze out excess moisture, and cut into 5 cm lengths.
Cut carrot, onion, and mushroom into thin strips, and marinate pork with soy sauce 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and black pepper for 10 min.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan, stir-fry carrot, onion, and mushroom separately for 1 min each, transfer to a plate without adding salt, and stir-fry pork for 3 min.
Boil soaked glass noodles in boiling water for 6 min, drain, and toss with soy sauce 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, and sesame oil 1 tbsp.
Add glass noodles, vegetables, pork, and spinach to a bowl, mix together, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Season glass noodles right after boiling so they do not bloat and absorb the flavors well.
Cool stir-fried vegetables separately to keep their vibrant colors.

japchae-bap.desc: Soy sauce-seasoned japchae served on top of rice.
japchae-bap.name: Stir-Fried Glass Noodles with Rice (Japchae-bap)
steps: Marinate the pork in 1/2 tbsp of soy sauce, and cut the onion, carrot, and bell pepper into thin strips.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over high heat, stir-fry the pork for 2 minutes, then add the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper, the remaining 1.5 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, 1 tsp of sugar, and 100 ml of water, and boil for 1 minute.
Mix 1 tsp of starch with 1 tbsp of water to thicken the sauce, and drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve on top of the cooked rice.
tips: Cutting the vegetables thinly helps the sauce absorb better.
Adding a fried egg on top makes it extra smooth.

jeju-bingtteok.desc: A traditional Jeju rice cake made by rolling seasoned radish namul inside a buckwheat crepe.
jeju-bingtteok.name: Jeju Buckwheat Crepe Roll (Jeju Bingtteok)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into thin strips, blanch in boiling water, squeeze out the moisture, and toss with 1/4 tsp of salt and 1 tbsp of sesame oil.
Mix 1 cup of buckwheat flour, 1/4 tsp of salt, and 200ml of water to make a thin batter.
Coat a pan lightly with cooking oil and fry the batter into round, thin crepes.
Place the seasoned radish namul on the cooked crepe, roll it up tightly, and cut it into bite-sized pieces.
tips: The batter must be cooked thin so it rolls well.
Keeping the seasoning light is the traditional Jeju way.

jeju-carrot-rape.desc: A sweet and sour French-style carrot salad.
jeju-carrot-rape.name: Jeju Gujwa Carrot Grated Salad (Jeju Gujwa Danggeun Rape)
steps: Peel the carrot and cut into thin strips using a julienne peeler.
Add salt 1/2 tsp, pickle for 5 minutes, and squeeze out the moisture.
Mix olive oil 2 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, mustard, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Toss the carrot with the dressing and top with mixed nuts.
tips: Letting it sit in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes brings out the flavors.
It is also great as a sandwich filling.

jeju-doenjang-mulhoe.desc: A refreshing Jeju-style cold raw fish soup with a doenjang base.
jeju-doenjang-mulhoe.name: Jeju-style Soybean Paste Cold Raw Fish Soup (Jeju-sik Doenjang Mulhoe)
steps: Blanch the squid in boiling water for 2 minutes, cut into bite-sized pieces, and cut the cucumber, onion, and perilla leaf into thin strips.
Dissolve 2 tbsp of doenjang, 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of sugar, minced garlic, and sesame oil in 300ml of cold water to make the broth, then chill it.
Place the squid and vegetables in a bowl.
Pour the chilled broth right before eating and top with ice cubes.
tips: Doenjang mulhoe is tangy and savory.
Adding somen noodles makes it a complete meal.

jeju-dwaeji-duruchigi.desc: Jeju-style stir-fried pork made with kimchi and vegetables.
jeju-dwaeji-duruchigi.name: Jeju-Style Stir-Fried Pork (Jeju-sik Dwaeji Duruchigi)
steps: Marinate the pork with 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, minced garlic, and 1 tsp of sugar for 15 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips, cut the kimchi into bite-sized pieces, and cut the green onion diagonally.
Place the pork, onion, and kimchi in a pan and stir-fry over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the green onion and 1 tbsp of sesame oil, and stir-fry for 1 more minute.
tips: Adding plenty of onion brings out a sweet flavor.
It is also great to serve over rice as a rice bowl dish.

jeju-galchi-guk.desc: Clear Jeju-style hairtail soup with napa cabbage and pumpkin.
jeju-galchi-guk.name: Jeju Hairtail Soup (Jeju Galchi-guk)
steps: Cut hairtail into pieces and wash them, cut napa cabbage into bite-sized pieces, cut Korean zucchini into half-moons, and slice green onion and Cheongyang chili diagonally.
Put 800 ml of water, napa cabbage, and Korean zucchini in a pot and boil for 8 minutes.
Add hairtail and minced garlic, and boil for 8 minutes. Skim off any foam.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce and 1/3 tsp of salt, and top with green onion and Cheongyang chili.
tips: Do not stir the hairtail as it falls apart easily.
In Jeju, aged pumpkin is added to bring out the natural sweetness.

jeju-gamgyul-yogurt-bowl.desc: A refreshing yogurt bowl topped with mandarin oranges.
jeju-gamgyul-yogurt-bowl.name: Jeju Mandarin Yogurt Bowl (Jeju Gamgyul Yogurt Bowl)
steps: Peel the mandarin orange and separate it into individual segments.
Put yogurt in a bowl and sprinkle oatmeal on top.
Top with mandarin orange and mixed nuts.
Drizzle 1 tsp of honey around and serve.
tips: Removing the white pith from the mandarin orange peel reduces bitterness.
You can top it with mandarin orange marmalade instead of honey.

jeju-godeungeo-ssambap.desc: Wrap grilled mackerel with leaf lettuce and ssamjang.
jeju-godeungeo-ssambap.name: Jeju Mackerel Ssambap (Jeju Godeungeo Ssambap)
steps: Cut the mackerel in half, wipe off the moisture, sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt, and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side.
Wash the leaf lettuce and perilla leaf and drain the water.
Place cooked rice, mackerel flesh, and ssamjang on the leaf lettuce and wrap to eat.
tips: Carefully remove the bones.
It is good to serve with garlic and chili pepper.

jeju-gogi-guksu.desc: Jeju-style noodle soup served in a rich pork broth.
jeju-gogi-guksu.name: Jeju Pork Noodle Soup (Jeju Gogi-guksu)
steps: Soak pork in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood, then blanch it in boiling water for 5 minutes and wash it.
In a pot, combine 1.5 L of water, pork, 1/2 of green onion, ginger, and minced garlic, boil over medium-low heat for 50 minutes, take out the pork, and cut it into thin slices.
Season the broth with 1 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Place boiled thin wheat noodles in a bowl, top with pork and thinly sliced green onion, and pour the hot broth over them.
tips: Boil for a long time so the broth becomes milky and rich.
Serving with kimchi adds a refreshing taste.

jeju-gosari-yukgaejang.desc: A Jeju-style spicy soup thickened with buckwheat flour, made with boiled pork and fiddlehead ferns.
jeju-gosari-yukgaejang.name: Jeju Fiddlehead Fern Spicy Beef Soup (Jeju Gosari Yukgaejang)
steps: Boil the pork in 1.5L of boiling water for 40 minutes, take it out, shred it, and reserve the broth.
Cut the fiddlehead fern into 5cm pieces and cut the green onion into large chunks.
Add the fiddlehead fern, shredded pork, 1 tbsp of doenjang, minced garlic, and 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce to the broth and boil for 15 minutes.
Dissolve 3 tbsp of buckwheat flour in 4 tbsp of water, add it to the soup along with the green onion, and boil for 5 minutes.
tips: Buckwheat flour thickens the soup and adds a nutty flavor.
Soak the fiddlehead fern fully so it becomes tender.

jeju-haemul-ttukbaegi.desc: A refreshing seafood earthenware pot filled with abalone, shrimp, and manila clam.
jeju-haemul-ttukbaegi.name: Jeju-style Seafood Earthenware Pot (Jeju Haemul Ttukbaegi)
steps: Desalt the manila clam, wash the abalone with a brush, and slice thinly. Prepare the shrimp.
Pour water 600 ml into an earthenware pot, dissolve doenjang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes, and minced garlic, then bring to a boil.
Add manila clam, abalone, and tofu, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and green onion and boil for 3 more minutes.
tips: Add seafood in order so they do not overcook.
Adding kalguksu or ramen noodles is also good.

jeju-heukdwaeji-gui.desc: Thick black pork belly grilled with coarse salt.
jeju-heukdwaeji-gui.name: Jeju Black Pork Belly BBQ (Jeju Heukdwaeji-gui)
steps: Cut the pork thickly and sprinkle with 1 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Place on a heated pan or grill and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Check if it is cooked through to the center and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Wrap the pork with leaf lettuce, ssamjang, and minced garlic to eat.
tips: Since there is a lot of fat, wipe it off with a paper towel as you grill.
Dipping it in meljeot (anchovy sauce) is the Jeju style.

jeju-jeonbok-dolsotbap.desc: A nutty stone pot rice cooked with abalone viscera.
jeju-jeonbok-dolsotbap.name: Jeju Abalone Stone Pot Rice (Jeju Jeonbok Dolsotbap)
steps: Soak the uncooked rice for 30 minutes, wash the abalone with a brush to separate the flesh from the viscera, and slice the flesh thinly.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and stir-fry the abalone flesh and viscera over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add the uncooked rice and 290ml of water, bring to a boil over high heat, reduce to low heat for 15 minutes, turn off the heat, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Make a seasoned soy sauce with 2 tbsp of soy sauce, slice thinly green onion, and sesame seeds to serve on the side.
tips: Stir-frying the viscera together makes the rice nutty.
Pour water into the scorched rice at the bottom and drink it as sungnyung.

jeju-okdom-gui.desc: Red tilefish simply seasoned with salt and pan-fried until golden.
jeju-okdom-gui.name: Pan-fried Red Tilefish (Jeju Okdom-gui)
steps: Pat red tilefish dry with paper towels and make 2 score marks on it.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt over it and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Coat a pan with 2 tbsp of cooking oil and fry over medium heat starting skin-side down for 5 minutes.
Flip and fry for another 4 minutes until golden.
tips: If using semi-dried red tilefish, reduce the amount of salt.
Serve with seaweed soup to make it feel like a Jeju-style set meal.

jeju-okdom-miyeok-guk.desc: A refreshing Jeju-style seaweed soup simmered with red tilefish.
jeju-okdom-miyeok-guk.name: Jeju-style Red Tilefish Seaweed Soup (Jeju Okdom Miyeok-guk)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed for 10 minutes, rinse, cut into 5cm pieces, and cut the red tilefish into portions.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and sauté the dried seaweed over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add 800ml of water and the red tilefish, then boil for 15 minutes.
Season with minced garlic, 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, and 1/3 tsp of salt, then boil for 5 more minutes.
tips: Be careful when picking out fish bones while eating.
A clear broth is the Jeju style.

jeolla-galbitang.desc: Clear short rib soup boiled with glass noodles and Korean radish.
jeolla-galbitang.name: Jeolla-Style Short Rib Soup (Jeollado-sik Galbitang)
steps: Soak the beef in cold water for 1 hour to draw out the blood, blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes, and rinse.
Put the beef, 2L of water, and Korean radish in a pot, bring to a boil over high heat, and boil over medium-low heat for 60 minutes.
Take out and slice the Korean radish, and soak the glass noodles. Season the broth with minced garlic, 2 tbsp soup soy sauce, and 1 tsp salt.
Put the glass noodles and Korean radish back in, boil for 5 minutes, and top with green onion and black pepper.
tips: Blanching makes the broth much clearer.
Letting it cool and skimming off the oil makes it clean.

jeolla-jeon-mix.desc: Assorted ingredients coated in egg and pan-fried.
jeolla-jeon-mix.name: Jeolla-Style Assorted Jeon (Jeollado-sik Modum-jeon)
steps: Sprinkle 1/2 tsp salt over frozen pollack, shrimp, Korean zucchini, and tofu, let sit for 10 minutes, and wipe away the moisture.
Lightly coat each ingredient in flour.
Beat 3 egg to make the coating.
Drizzle cooking oil in a pan over medium-low heat and pan-fry each side for 2~3 minutes until golden.
tips: Wiping away the moisture helps the egg coating stick well.
Pan-frying slowly over low heat ensures the inside cooks through.

jeonbok-butter-gui.desc: Abalone pan-fried with butter and garlic.
jeonbok-butter-gui.name: Butter-Grilled Abalone (Jeonbok Butter Gui)
steps: Scrub the abalone with a brush, use a spoon to remove the flesh, and remove or reserve the viscera separately.
Make shallow, crisscross cuts on the flesh.
In a heated pan, add 1 tbsp butter and minced garlic, and cook the abalone over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side.
Season with 1/4 tsp salt and black pepper, and place back onto the shells.
tips: Cooking for too long makes it tough.
You can also stir-fry the viscera in butter to use as a sauce.

jeonbok-juk.desc: Savory porridge simmered with abalone and its viscera.
jeonbok-juk.name: Abalone Porridge (Jeonbok Juk)
steps: Wash the uncooked rice and soak for 30 minutes. Scrub the abalone with a brush, separate the flesh from the viscera, and slice the flesh thinly.
Drizzle 1 tbsp sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the abalone flesh and viscera over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Add the soaked uncooked rice, stir-fry for 1 minute, pour in 1 L water, and simmer over low heat for 25 minutes while stirring.
Season with 1 tsp soup soy sauce and 1/3 tsp salt.
tips: Stir-frying the viscera together gives the porridge a light green color and a savory flavor.
Stir frequently to prevent the bottom from burning.

jeonju-bibimbap.desc: Jeonju-style mixed rice topped with soybean sprout, various seasoned greens, beef, and an egg yolk.
jeonju-bibimbap.name: Jeonju Bibimbap
steps: Blanch soybean sprout and spinach, season with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and salt, and stir-fry carrot, fiddlehead fern, and bellflower root in 1 tbsp of cooking oil.
Marinate beef in 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of sugar, and 1 tbsp of sesame oil, then stir-fry in a pan for 3 minutes.
Separate the egg yolk or prepare a soft-fried egg.
Arrange cooked rice, greens, and beef around a bowl, top with egg, and 2 tbsp of gochujang, then mix well.
tips: Cooking the rice in beef broth is the Jeonju way.
Seasoning the greens separately keeps the flavor clean.

jeonju-kongnamul-gukbap.desc: Jeonju-style rice soup with cooked rice in a refreshing soybean sprout broth.
jeonju-kongnamul-gukbap.name: Jeonju Soybean Sprout Rice Soup (Jeonju Kongnamul Gukbap)
steps: Wash soybean sprout, drain, and slice thinly green onion.
Put 700 ml of water, soybean sprout, minced garlic, and shrimp in an earthenware pot, leave the lid open, and boil for 8 minutes.
Add cooked rice, 1/2 tsp of salt, and Korean red pepper flakes, then boil for 2 more minutes.
Crack in egg, cook until soft-boiled, and top with green onion.
tips: Boiling soybean sprout with the lid open prevents a grassy smell.
Adding squid on the side makes it even more refreshing.

jeonju-kongnamul-muchim.desc: Crunchy seasoned soybean sprouts tossed with Korean red pepper flakes and sesame oil.
jeonju-kongnamul-muchim.name: Jeonju-Style Seasoned Soybean Sprouts (Jeonju Kongnamul-muchim)
steps: Wash the soybean sprout, put them in a pot with 3 tbsp water, cover with a lid, and boil over high heat for 5 minutes.
Cook without opening the lid, then take them out, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Make the sauce by mixing Korean red pepper flakes, minced garlic, 1 tbsp soup soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and slice thinly green onion.
Toss the soybean sprout with the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Opening the lid while boiling will create a grassy smell.
Seasoning with soup soy sauce instead of salt gives it that Jeollado-style umami.

jeyuk-bowl.desc: A hearty one-bowl meal of fire-stir-fried spicy pork over rice.
jeyuk-bowl.name: Spicy Pork Rice Bowl (Jeyuk Deopbap)
steps: Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1/2 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, minced garlic 1/2 tbsp, sesame oil 1/2 tbsp, and black pepper to make the sauce, then coat the pork and marinate for 10 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips 0.5cm thick, and slice thinly the green onion.
Heat cooking oil 1/2 tbsp in a pan over high heat, stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes until the surface turns red.

Add the onion and stir-fry for 2~3 more minutes until the onion becomes translucent, then add the green onion and stir-fry for 30 seconds. If there is too much liquid, reduce it over high heat for 1 minute.
In a separate pan, fry the egg for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Place the pork and egg over cooked rice and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: The sauce burns easily, so lower the heat midway and stir frequently.
Serving with lettuce or perilla leaves helps cut through the richness.

jinju-bibimbap.desc: A Jinju-style bibimbap topped with seasoned and stir-fried beef instead of raw beef tartare.
jinju-bibimbap.name: Jinju Bibimbap
steps: Marinate beef in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, and 1 tbsp sesame oil, then stir-fry in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Blanch soybean sprout and spinach, toss with 1 tbsp sesame oil, cut carrot into thin strips, and stir-fry in cooking oil.
Fry egg into a soft-cooked sunny-side up.
Place cooked rice, vegetables, and beef in a bowl, top with egg and 2 tbsp gochujang, and mix well.
tips: Since the traditional Jinju style using raw beef requires fresh meat, this recipe safely uses stir-fried beef.
Squeeze the moisture firmly out of the blanched vegetables.

jinju-naengmyeon.desc: Jinju-style cold buckwheat noodles served in a rich beef broth and topped with savory meat pancakes.
jinju-naengmyeon.name: Jinju Naengmyeon
steps: Place 150g beef in 900ml water, boil for 30 minutes, remove the meat, let the broth cool, skim off the fat, and place in the freezer for 30 minutes. Slice the boiled beef thinly.
Season the broth with 2 tbsp soup soy sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp vinegar, and 1 tbsp sugar to make a deep brown broth.

Meat pancakes (Yukjeon): Slice the remaining 100g beef thinly, sprinkle with 1/4 tsp salt, coat in 2 tbsp flour and 1 beaten egg, pan-fry in 1 tbsp cooking oil over medium heat for 1 minute on each side, and cut into thin strips.
Boil naengmyeon noodles, rinse in cold water, squeeze out moisture, boil 1 egg and cut in half, and cut Korean radish and Korean pear into thin strips.
Place noodles in a bowl, top with meat pancakes, boiled beef, Korean radish, Korean pear, and boiled egg, pour cold broth over them, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Jinju naengmyeon is uniquely garnished with yukjeon (egg-battered pan-fried beef).
Although anchovy and seafood broth are used originally, you can easily make it with beef broth at home.

jjajang-bap.desc: A one-bowl meal with thick jajang sauce served over rice.
jjajang-bap.name: Jajang Bap
steps: Dice onion, potato, Korean zucchini, and pork into 1cm sizes. Dissolve 50 g of jajang powder in 100 ml of cold water.
Coat a pan with 1 tbsp of cooking oil, stir-fry pork for 3 minutes, then add onion and potato and stir-fry for 3 more minutes.
Add Korean zucchini and stir-fry for 1 minute, then pour 300 ml of water and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the dissolved jajang powder and 1/2 tbsp of sugar, stir, and simmer for 3 minutes to make it thick.
In another pan, fry egg with 1 tbsp of cooking oil.
Place the sauce and egg on top of cooked rice.
tips: Keep the broth less than when making jajangmyeon and simmer until thick.
Leftover sauce can be stored in the refrigerator for 3 days.

jjajang-ramyeon.desc: Simple jajang ramen made with jajang powder.
jjajang-ramyeon.name: Jajang Ramen
steps: Finely chop the onion and pork. Boil the ramen in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan and stir-fry the pork and onion for 2 minutes.
Add 150ml of water, 2 tbsp of jajang powder, and 1 tsp of sugar, and boil for 1 minute.
Add the ramen and toss for 1 minute.
tips: Dissolving the jajang powder in water beforehand prevents lumps from forming.
Serve topped with a fried egg.

jjajang-tteokbokki.desc: Children's tteokbokki made with jajang powder.
jjajang-tteokbokki.name: Jajang Tteokbokki
steps: Soak the rice cake in water to make it soft, and cut the fish cake and onion into bite-sized pieces.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 1 tbsp and stir-fry the onion for 1 minute.
Dissolve water 350ml, jajang powder 3 tbsp, and sugar 1 tsp, and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cake and fish cake, and simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes.
tips: Dissolve the jajang powder in water first so it doesn't clump.
Topping with cheese makes it even more savory.

jjajangmyeon.desc: Easy homemade jajangmyeon made with jajang powder.
jjajangmyeon.name: Jajangmyeon
steps: Dice onion, Korean zucchini, potato, and pork into 1.5cm sizes and cut cucumber into thin strips. Dissolve 50 g of jajang powder in 100 ml of cold water without lumps.
Coat a pan heated over medium heat with 2 tbsp of cooking oil and stir-fry pork for 3 minutes until cooked.
Add onion and potato and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add Korean zucchini and stir-fry for 1 more minute.
Pour 400 ml of water, and when it comes to a boil, cook over low heat for 8 minutes until potato is tender.
Add the dissolved jajang powder and 1/2 tbsp of sugar, stir, and boil for 3 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, boil thin wheat noodles in 2 L of boiling water for 6 minutes (3 minutes for thin wheat noodles) and rinse in cold water to drain, then place in a bowl and top with the sauce and cucumber.
tips: Adding the powder directly will cause lumps, so make sure to dissolve it in water first.
Adding a little bit of sugar brings out the unique sweetness and savory flavor of jajang.

jjamppong.desc: Spicy noodle soup made by stir-frying seafood and vegetables over high heat.
jjamppong.name: Spicy Seafood Noodle Soup (Jjamppong)
steps: Score the squid body and cut into bite-sized pieces; cut pork, cabbage, and onion into bite-sized pieces. Slice green onion diagonally.
Add 2 tbsp of cooking oil to a pot over high heat, stir-fry green onion, minced garlic, and pork for 2 minutes, then add 2 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add cabbage, onion, squid, and shrimp, stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1 tbsp of oyster sauce and stir-fry once more.
Pour in 700 ml of water and boil for 5 minutes.
Place pre-boiled knife-cut wheat noodles (boiled in boiling water for 3 minutes) in a bowl and pour the soup and toppings over them.
tips: Korean red pepper flakes must be stir-fried in oil to give the soup that smoky wok flavor.
Boil and rinse the noodles separately so the broth doesn't get cloudy.

jjamppong-bap.desc: A hearty one-bowl dish of rice in a spicy jjamppong broth.
jjamppong-bap.name: Spicy Seafood Rice Soup (Jjamppong-bap)
steps: Cut the squid, shrimp, pork, cabbage, and onion into bite-sized pieces, and slice the green onion thinly.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pot over high heat, stir-fry the green onion, minced garlic, and pork for 2 minutes, then add the Korean red pepper flakes and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add the cabbage, onion, squid, shrimp, and oyster sauce, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in 600 ml of water and boil for 5 minutes to develop the broth flavor.
Place the cooked rice in a bowl and pour the ingredients and broth over it.
tips: If the broth is slightly reduced, the rich flavor soaks well into the rice.
Add cheongyang pepper for an even sharper kick.

jjamppong-ramen.desc: A spicy jjamppong-style ramen stir-fried with vegetables and pork.
