jjamppong-ramen.name: Spicy Seafood-Style Ramen (Jjamppong Ramen)
steps: Cut the cabbage and onion into bite-sized pieces, slice thinly the green onion and Cheongyang chili, and cut the pork into 1 cm widths.
Coat a pot with 1 tsp of cooking oil and stir-fry minced garlic and green onion over medium heat for 30 seconds to release the aroma.
Add pork and stir-fry for 1 minute, then add 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes and 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Stir quickly so the Korean red pepper flakes do not burn.
Add 500 ml of water, cabbage, and onion. Once it starts boiling, add ramen and the soup base, and boil for 3 minutes.
Add Cheongyang chili and boil for 30 more seconds.
tips: Stir-frying Korean red pepper flakes in oil creates a smoky, wok-like broth.
Using only 2/3 of the soup base reduces the saltiness.

jjimdak.desc: Soy sauce-braised chicken with plenty of glass noodles and vegetables.
jjimdak.name: Braised Spicy Chicken (Jjimdak)
steps: Blanch the chicken in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain, and soak the glass noodles in cold water for 30 minutes. Cut the potato, carrot, and onion into large chunks.
In a pot, combine the chicken, soy sauce 5 tbsp, sugar 2 tbsp, minced garlic, and water 500 ml, and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add the potato, carrot, and onion, and braise for 15 minutes.
Add the soaked glass noodles and Cheongyang chili, simmer for 5 minutes, and turn off the heat once a little broth remains.
tips: Blanching the chicken helps remove gamey odors and excess fat.
Add the glass noodles at the end so they do not get mushy.

jjokpa-jeon.desc: A crispy pancake loaded with plenty of thin green onion.
jjokpa-jeon.name: Green Onion Pancake (Jjokpa-jeon)
steps: Trim the roots of thin green onion, wash, cut to fit the pan length, and drain.
Mix Korean pancake mix 1/2 cup, water 100 ml, and salt 1/4 tsp to make a thin batter.
Add cooking oil to a heated pan, line up thin green onion neatly, drizzle the batter thinly, and cook over medium heat for 3 min.
Pour beaten egg on top, flip, and cook for 3 min more until crispy.
tips: Make the batter thin enough to just hold thin green onion together for crispiness.
Mixing vinegar with soy sauce for dipping goes really well with it.

jjokpa-kimchi.desc: Thin green onion kimchi seasoned with fish sauce.
jjokpa-kimchi.name: Green Onion Kimchi (Jjokpa-kimchi)
steps: Trim the roots and withered leaves of thin green onion, wash, and drain completely.
Immerse thin green onion in fish sauce 3 tbsp for 30 min to marinate, and set the remaining fish sauce aside.
Mix the leftover fish sauce with Korean red pepper flakes 5 tbsp, minced garlic 1 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, and water 3 tbsp to make seasoning.
Coat thin green onion with the seasoning, sprinkle sesame seeds, tie them in bundles of 3~4, and pack into a container.
Leave at room temperature for a day, then store in the refrigerator.
tips: Make sure to dry thin green onion completely as moisture makes them get soggy easily.
It is best to eat them within a week.

jjolmyeon.desc: A popular snack-bar dish of chewy noodles tossed in a sweet and spicy sauce.
jjolmyeon.name: Chewy Wheat Noodles with Spicy Sauce (Jjolmyeon)
steps: Boil the egg in cold water for 10 minutes after it starts boiling, then cut it in half. Cut the cabbage and cucumber into thin strips.
Mix 2 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tbsp sesame oil to make the sauce.
Add the jjolmyeon noodles to 2 L of boiling water, boil for 3 minutes, rinse in cold water several times, and squeeze out the water firmly.
Place the jjolmyeon noodles and vegetables in a bowl, top with the sauce, toss well, and garnish with the egg.
tips: Rinse the jjolmyeon noodles vigorously in cold water so they stay chewy.
If it lacks sweetness, add 1/2 tbsp more sugar.

jjolmyeon-bokkeum.desc: Stir-fried soy sauce jjolmyeon tossed with vegetables over high heat.
jjolmyeon-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Jjolmyeon with Soy Sauce (Jjolmyeon-bokkeum)
steps: Boil the jjolmyeon noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Cut the cabbage, onion, and carrot into thin strips.
Heat a pan over high heat, drizzle in 1 tbsp cooking oil, and stir-fry the vegetables for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Add the jjolmyeon noodles, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 tbsp oyster sauce, stir-fry for 1 minute 30 seconds, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: If you boil the noodles for too long, they will break easily when stir-frying.
Top with a fried egg for a hearty meal.

jogi-gui.desc: Crispy pan-fried yellow croaker seasoned simply with salt.
jogi-gui.name: Pan-Fried Yellow Croaker (Jogi-gui)
steps: Scrape off the scales of the yellow croaker, remove the internal organs, wash thoroughly, and pat dry with a paper towel.
Make 2 cuts on it, sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of salt, and let sit for 10 minutes.
Coat a pan with 2 tbsp of cooking oil and fry one side over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Flip and fry for another 4 minutes until crispy.
tips: Reduce the salt if you are using gulbi (salted and dried yellow croaker).
For bori-gulbi (barley-fermented dried yellow croaker), you can also serve it alongside cold water and rice.

jumeokbap.desc: Bite-sized rice balls perfect for lunchboxes.
jumeokbap.name: Tuna Mayo Rice Balls (Tuna Mayo Jumeokbap)
steps: Drain the canned tuna through a sieve, then mix with 1 tbsp of mayonnaise and 1 tsp of soy sauce to make the filling.
Mix 1 tsp of sesame oil, sesame seeds, and 1/3 tsp of salt into the warm cooked rice, and divide into 8 portions.
Apply water or sesame oil to your hands, flatten a portion of the cooked rice, place 1 tsp (about 8g) of the tuna mixture in the center, wrap it up, and shape it into a round ball.
Finish by tearing or cutting the roasted seaweed into small pieces with scissors, or roll the rice balls in the roasted seaweed.
tips: If the cooked rice is too hot, let it cool slightly before shaping so it holds its form well.
Wrapping them in plastic wrap prevents them from sticking to your hands and is more hygienic.

jungguk-bibimmyeon.desc: A Chinese-style mixed noodle dish seasoned with soy sauce instead of peanut sauce.
jungguk-bibimmyeon.name: Chinese-style Spicy Cold Noodles (Jung-guk-sik Bibimmyeon)
steps: Boil the thin wheat noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Cut the cucumber into thin strips and coarsely chop the mixed nuts.
Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Toss the thin wheat noodles with the sauce and top with the cucumber, mixed nuts, and sesame seeds.
tips: Even without peanut butter, the mixed nuts make the sauce nutty and rich.
It tastes best when served cold.

junghwa-naengmyeon.desc: Summer noodles served in a sweet and sour soy sauce broth with peanut sauce.
junghwa-naengmyeon.name: Chinese-Style Cold Noodles (Junghwa Naengmyeon)
steps: Boil 300 ml of water with 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 3 tbsp of vinegar, and 2 tbsp of sugar, let it cool, and chill it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. Mix in 1 tbsp of sesame oil.
Make a thin egg garnish, slice it into thin strips, and slice the cucumber and ham into thin strips as well. Finely crush the mixed nuts.
Boil the thin wheat noodles in 2 L of boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse in cold water, and drain well.
Place the noodles in a bowl, top with the vegetables, egg garnish, and ham, and pour the cold broth over them. Serve with the mixed nuts and mustard on the side.
tips: Freezing the broth in an ice cube tray makes it even more refreshing.
Dissolving the mustard gives it an authentic Chinese restaurant flavor.

kale-apple-salad.desc: A salad pairing bitter kale with the sweetness of apple.
kale-apple-salad.name: Kale Apple Salad
steps: Remove thick stems from kale, tear leaves into bite-sized pieces, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Cut apple thinly with the skin on and chop mixed nuts coarsely.
Mix 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/4 tsp salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Toss kale in the dressing first, let sit for 2 minutes to soften, then top with apple and mixed nuts.
tips: Resting kale in the dressing for 2 minutes reduces its toughness.
If it tastes too bitter, add 1/2 tsp oligosaccharide syrup.

kale-banana-smoothie.desc: A 3-minute morning substitute smoothie using only a blender.
kale-banana-smoothie.name: Kale Banana Yogurt Smoothie
steps: Remove the stem of the kale and tear the leaves roughly. Peel the banana and cut it into 3 pieces.
Put 100 ml of milk, 100 g of yogurt, banana, and kale into the blender in order.
Blend smoothly for more than 30 seconds so no kale pieces are visible.
Pour into a cup and drink immediately.
tips: If you freeze and add the banana, it is cooler and thicker.
If it lacks sweetness, add 1 tsp of oligosaccharide.

karaage.desc: Japanese-style fried chicken marinated in garlic soy sauce.
karaage.name: Japanese Fried Chicken (Karaage)
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and marinate for 20 minutes in a mixture of 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of mirin, minced garlic, ginger, and black pepper.
Evenly coat the marinated chicken with 4 tbsp of starch.
Deep fry in oil at 170 degrees for 3 minutes, take them out, let them rest for 3 minutes, and fry again at 180 degrees for 1 minute to make them crispy.
Place on a paper towel to drain the oil.
tips: Frying twice makes the inside juicy and the outside crispy.
Serve with lemon or mayonnaise.

kare-rice.desc: Hearty homemade curry loaded with vegetables and meat.
kare-rice.name: Japanese Curry Rice (Kare Rice)
steps: Cut the potato, carrot, and onion into 2 cm cubes, and cut the pork into bite-sized pieces. Soak the potato in cold water for 5 minutes to remove excess starch.
In a pot, add 1 tbsp cooking oil and stir-fry the pork over medium heat for 2 minutes, then add the onion and stir-fry for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the carrot and potato, stir-fry for 1 minute, then pour in 500 ml of water. When it comes to a boil, skim off the foam and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat when a chopstick easily pierces the potato.
In a small bowl, dissolve 4 tbsp curry powder in 100 ml of warm broth first to eliminate lumps, then pour it into the pot.
Simmer over low heat, stirring for 5 minutes, until thickened, then sprinkle with black pepper and serve over cooked rice.
tips: Adding the powder directly will cause lumps. Dissolve it separately first.
The flavor deepens even more after sitting overnight.

katsudon.desc: A rice bowl topped with crispy pork cutlet simmered in a sweet sauce with eggs and onions.
katsudon.name: Pork Cutlet Rice Bowl (Katsudon)
steps: Pound the pork to 0.8 cm thickness, season with salt and black pepper, coat with flour, beaten egg wash, and breadcrumbs, fry in 170°C oil for 3 minutes on each side, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Boil 150 ml of water, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of mirin, and 1 tbsp of sugar in a pan, add the sliced onion, and cook for 4 minutes.
Place the sliced pork cutlet on top, pour in 2 beaten eggs around the edges.
Put a lid on, cook for 30 seconds, and turn off the heat while the eggs are still half-cooked.
Place the cooked rice in a bowl and top it with the cutlet mixture.
tips: The eggs are most delicious when slightly soft and runny.
You can also use store-bought frozen pork cutlets.

kids-banana-oat-muffin.desc: Muffins sweetened naturally with banana instead of sugar.
kids-banana-oat-muffin.name: Banana Oatmeal Muffins
steps: Mash the banana thoroughly and finely chop the mixed nuts.
Mix the banana, 60 g oatmeal, 1 egg, and 50 ml milk, and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Fill 4 muffin tin compartments 80% full and top with mixed nuts.
Bake at 180 degrees for 18 minutes, and take them out when a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
tips: Riper bananas are sweeter, so sugar isn't needed.
Leave out the mixed nuts if there is a nut allergy.

kids-banana-pancake.desc: Fluffy pancakes naturally sweetened with bananas instead of sugar.
kids-banana-pancake.name: Banana Pancakes
steps: Put the banana in a bowl and mash it finely with a fork.
Add 1 egg, 50 ml of milk, and 50 g of flour, and mix without lumps to make a batter.
Lightly coat a pan heated over low heat with cooking oil using a paper towel, drop the batter into 8 cm circles, and cook for 2 minutes 30 seconds.
When bubbles form on the surface, flip and cook for 2 more minutes until cooked through.
tips: If the heat is too high, only the outside will burn. Cook slowly over low heat.
It is even better served with fruit or yogurt.

kids-bread-egg-tart.desc: Bite-sized snacks made by baking sandwich bread and egg in a muffin tin.
kids-bread-egg-tart.name: Sandwich Bread Egg Tarts
steps: Trim the crusts off the sandwich bread, flatten it with a rolling pin, and press it into 3 compartments of a muffin tin.
Whisk together 2 egg, 50 ml milk, and 1 tsp sugar until smooth, then strain through a sieve.
Fill the sandwich bread cups 80% full with the egg mixture and top with finely torn cheese.
Bake in an oven or air fryer preheated to 180 degrees for 12 minutes.
tips: Fill them only 80% full so the egg mixture doesn't overflow.
They firm up as they cool, so they are best eaten warm.

kids-bread-pudding.desc: Soft pudding made with leftover sandwich bread.
kids-bread-pudding.name: Bread Pudding (Sikppang Pudding)
steps: Cut sandwich bread into 2 cm cubes and place them in a heat-resistant dish.
Mix egg 2, milk 250ml, and sugar 1tbsp well, then strain through a sieve.
Pour the egg mixture over sandwich bread and let soak for 10 minutes.
Bake in a 170-degree oven or air fryer for 20 minutes, poke with a chopstick, and take out if nothing sticks.
tips: The egg mixture must soak into sandwich bread thoroughly to be soft.
It is fine to reduce or omit sugar.

kids-cheese-egg-roll-bread.desc: A snack made by rolling cheese and egg in sandwich bread and toasting it.
kids-cheese-egg-roll-bread.name: Cheese Egg Toast Roll (Chijeu Gaeran Toseuteu Rol)
steps: Cut off the crusts of the sandwich bread and flatten it thinly with a rolling pin.
Beat 1 egg, cook it thinly in a pan over low heat, and cut it in half.
Place the cheese and the thin egg sheet on the sandwich bread and roll it up tightly.
Brush the pan with cooking oil, roll the bread around while toasting for 3 minutes until golden brown, and slice it into bite-sized pieces.
tips: Roll out the sandwich bread thinly so it rolls up well.
Place the seam side down when toasting so it doesn't unroll.

kids-cheese-riceball.desc: Bite-sized rice balls with cheese and roasted seaweed flakes.
kids-cheese-riceball.name: Cheese Rice Ball (Chijeu Jumeokbap)
steps: Cut roasted seaweed finely with scissors to make seaweed flakes and cut cheese into small pieces.
Mix cooked rice with sesame oil 1tsp and sesame seeds.
Scoop a spoonful of cooked rice, add a piece of cheese, and shape it into a 3 cm diameter ball.
Roll in the seaweed flakes and place on a plate.
tips: When cooked rice is hot, let the steam escape slightly before shaping.
Wrapping it in plastic wrap to shape prevents it from sticking to your hands.

kids-egg-bread-roll.desc: Bite-sized snacks made by rolling sandwich bread, coating it in egg, and pan-frying.
kids-egg-bread-roll.name: Egg Bread Rolls
steps: Cut off the crusts of the sandwich bread and flatten it thinly with a rolling pin. Place half a slice of cheese on top.
Roll up the sandwich bread tightly and place it seam-side down without using toothpicks.
Roll and coat the sandwich bread rolls in a mixture of 2 eggs and 2 tbsp of milk.
Cook in a pan heated over medium heat with cooking oil, rolling them around for 4 minutes until golden.
tips: Cutting off the crusts of the sandwich bread makes it easier to roll.
Cheese was used instead of jam to keep it from being too sweet.

kids-mild-tteokbokki.desc: Non-spicy tteokbokki made with soy sauce instead of red pepper powder.
kids-mild-tteokbokki.name: Mild Soy Sauce Tteokbokki (Sunhan Ganjang Tteokbokki)
steps: Soak rice cake in cold water for 10 minutes and cut fish cake into bite-sized pieces. Slice green onion diagonally.
Put water 250ml, soy sauce 2tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1tbsp, and sugar 1tsp in a pan and bring to a boil.
When it starts to boil, add rice cake and fish cake and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes.
When the sauce becomes reduced and thick, add green onion, drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle sesame seeds, then turn off the heat.
tips: Blanching fish cake in boiling water reduces oil and sodium.
If you want a spicy flavor, add red pepper powder only to the adults' plates instead of red pepper paste.

kids-mini-gimbap.desc: Small gimbap that is easy to eat in one bite.
kids-mini-gimbap.name: Mini Gimbap (Kkoma Gimbap)
steps: Mix cooked rice with sesame oil 1/2tbsp, salt 1/3tsp, and sesame seeds, then let it cool. Make thin egg crepes without salt and cut them into thin strips. Cut ham and carrot into thin strips and stir-fry them in a pan for 1 minute each.
Cut roasted seaweed in half, place it with the rough side facing up, and spread cooked rice thinly.
Place the filling ingredients in a line, roll them up tightly, and seal the end with water 1tsp.
Brush the outside with remaining sesame oil, slice into 1.5 cm thickness, and place on a plate.
tips: Slice the filling ingredients very thinly to suit a child's mouth.
You can also add pickled radish or imitation crab meat if you have them.

kids-oat-cookie.desc: A light and simple cookie made without butter or sugar.
kids-oat-cookie.name: Oatmeal Cookie
steps: Mash the banana finely and crush the mixed nuts very finely.
Mix the mashed banana, oatmeal 60g, egg 1 piece, and mixed nuts, then let it sit for 5 minutes.
Scoop out 12 portions of the dough with a spoon onto parchment paper, flattening them to a 4 cm diameter.
Bake in an air fryer preheated to 170°C for 12 minutes and let cool.
tips: Leave out the mixed nuts if there is a nut allergy.
The sweetness varies depending on how ripe the banana is.

kids-potato-croquette.desc: Crispy potato croquettes made with less oil.
kids-potato-croquette.name: Air Fryer Potato Croquette
steps: Peel the potato and either boil it or microwave it for 7 minutes, mash it finely while it's hot, and mix in salt 1/4 tsp.
Mix finely chopped cheese into the mashed potato and shape them into bite-sized oval patties.
Coat them in flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in that order, and spray cooking oil evenly.
Cook in a 190°C air fryer for 8 minutes, flip them, and cook for 5 more minutes.
tips: Potatoes don't hold together well once they cool down. Mash them while hot.
Serve ketchup on the side.

kids-quesadilla.desc: A kid-friendly snack made by folding a flour tortilla in half and toasting it.
kids-quesadilla.name: Cheese Ham Quesadilla
steps: Tear and lay cheese 1.5 slices on one half of the flour tortilla, then top with ham and corn.
Fold the remaining half to form a half-moon shape.
Grease a pan over medium-low heat with cooking oil and place the half-moon flour tortilla on it, cooking for 1 minute and 30 seconds on each side.
Once the cheese melts, take it out, cut it into 4 pieces, and let it cool.
tips: If you put too much filling inside, it will burst.
You must cook it over low heat so the cheese melts all the way through.

kids-sausage-veg-skewer.name: Sausage and Vegetable Skewers
steps: Cut the sausage into thirds and cut the bell pepper and onion into 2cm pieces.
Alternately thread the sausage, bell pepper, and onion onto the skewer and trim off the sharp ends.
Grease a pan with 1 tsp cooking oil and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes while rolling them around.
Brush with 2 tbsp ketchup and cook for 1 more minute.
tips: Trim the skewer ends to be rounded so children don't get hurt.
Blanching the sausage reduces the sodium.

kids-sweetpotato-cheese-ball.desc: A sweet potato snack with gooey cheese inside.
kids-sweetpotato-cheese-ball.name: Sweet Potato Cheese Balls
steps: Peel the sweet potato, boil it or microwave it for 6 minutes to cook, and mash it finely while hot.
Mix 1 tbsp of starch and 1 tbsp of milk into the mashed sweet potato to make a dough.
Cut the cheese into small pieces, pinch off portions of the dough into 4 cm balls, flatten them, add the cheese, and shape them into rounds.
Cook in a pan heated over medium-low heat with cooking oil, rolling them around for 5 minutes until golden.
tips: Wrap the dough securely so the cheese doesn't burst out.
The cheese firms up when cold, so it's best to eat them while warm.

kids-sweetpotato-stick.desc: Crispy sweet potato sticks baked without sugar.
kids-sweetpotato-stick.name: Air Fryer Sweet Potato Sticks
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 1cm thick sticks.
In a bowl, mix the sweet potato, 1 tsp cooking oil, and a pinch of salt.
Place them in the air fryer basket without overlapping.
Bake at 180 degrees for 10 minutes, flip, and bake for 5 more minutes.
tips: Cut them to an even thickness so they cook uniformly.
Serve with yogurt instead of ketchup.

kids-tofu-nugget.desc: Crispy nuggets made with tofu instead of chicken.
kids-tofu-nugget.name: Tofu Nugget
steps: Squeeze the water completely out of the tofu, mash it, and mix it with 1/2 egg, 2 tbsp starch, and 1/4 tsp salt to make a dough.
Shape the dough into bite-sized flat pieces.
Dip them into the beaten remaining 1/2 egg and coat them with breadcrumbs.
Drizzle cooking oil over them and bake in an air fryer at 190 degrees for 8 minutes, then flip and bake for 4 minutes more.
tips: You must squeeze out the water from the tofu thoroughly so the shape holds.
You can pan-fry them instead of using an air fryer.

kids-tteok-skewer.desc: Crispy on the outside, chewy rice cake skewers with a sweet and savory soy sauce glaze.
kids-tteok-skewer.name: Soy Sauce Rice Cake Skewers (Ganjang Tteok-kkochi)
steps: Blanch the rice cake in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain in a sieve, and thread 3 to 4 pieces onto each skewer.
Mix soy sauce 1 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, and ketchup 1 tbsp to make the sauce.
Heat a pan over medium heat with cooking oil 1 tbsp and pan-fry the skewers for 4 minutes, turning them until golden brown.
Brush the sauce on both sides and cook for 1 more minute over low heat.
tips: Cut off the sharp ends of the skewers so your child won't get hurt.
Keep the heat low after brushing the sauce, as it burns easily.

kids-yogurt-fruit-cup.desc: A visually delightful snack layered in a cup.
kids-yogurt-fruit-cup.name: Fruit Yogurt Cup
steps: Cut the apple and banana into bite-sized 0.7 cm pieces.
Put the mixed nuts in a plastic bag and crush them very finely with a rolling pin.
Fill the cup with yogurt 1/2, then layer the fruit and the remaining yogurt in that order.
Top with the crushed mixed nuts.
tips: Be sure to crush the mixed nuts finely. Serving them whole can cause choking.
Use unsweetened plain yogurt.

kimbap.desc: Classic kimbap rolled with egg, ham, carrot, and cucumber.
kimbap.name: Kimbap
steps: Mix 1/2 tsp of salt, 1 tbsp of sesame oil, and 1 tbsp of sesame seeds into the warm cooked rice using a spatula in a slicing motion, then let it cool slightly.

Beat 3 egg(s), add a pinch of salt, pour 1 tsp of cooking oil in a pan, cook into a thick layer over low heat, and cut into 1cm widths. Cut the carrot into thin strips and stir-fry in 1 tsp of cooking oil for 1 minute, cut the cucumber lengthwise into 4 pieces and remove the seeds, and cut the ham lengthwise and fry in a pan for 1 minute.
Place the roasted seaweed on a bamboo rolling mat with the rough side facing up, and spread the cooked rice thinly while leaving 2cm at the bottom edge of the roasted seaweed.
Neatly arrange the egg, ham, carrot, and cucumber in the center of the cooked rice.
Roll tightly with the bamboo rolling mat to shape it, and seal the edge with 1 tsp of water.
Apply 1 tbsp of sesame oil to the outside, coat the knife with sesame oil, and slice into 1.5cm thickness.
tips: If you put in too many fillings, it will burst. 4 to 5 types are just right.
Wiping the knife with sesame oil or water helps cut clean cross-sections.

kimchi-bibim-guksu.desc: Sweet, sour, and spicy mixed noodles made with well-fermented kimchi.
kimchi-bibim-guksu.name: Spicy Mixed Kimchi Noodles (Kimchi Bibim Guksu)
steps: Boil water 2L in a large pot. Place the egg in cold water, boil for 10 minutes after it starts boiling, cool in cold water, and cut in half.
Finely chop the kimchi into 1 cm pieces and cut the cucumber into thin strips. Leave only 2 tbsp (30 ml) of kimchi juice.
In a bowl, mix gochujang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1/2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and the kimchi juice to make the sauce.
Add thin wheat noodles to the boiling water and boil for 4 minutes. When bubbles rise, pour in cold water 1 cup (200 ml).
Rinse the thin wheat noodles 3 to 4 times while rubbing in cold water, then drain thoroughly in a colander.
Place the thin wheat noodles, kimchi, and sauce in a bowl, mix well, and top with cucumber, egg, and sesame seeds.
tips: Drain the noodles thoroughly so the sauce doesn't become watery.
If you like it spicy, increase the Korean red pepper flakes to 1 tbsp (about 6g) instead of gochujang.

kimchi-fried-rice.desc: A college-dorm and solo-living staple that only needs well-fermented kimchi and cooked rice.
kimchi-fried-rice.name: Kimchi Fried Rice (Kimchi Bokkeumbap)
steps: Squeeze the liquid thoroughly out of the kimchi and cut it into 1 cm pieces using kitchen shears, then slice the green onion thinly into 0.5 cm rounds. Microwave the cooked rice for 1 minute to warm it up, and break up any clumps in advance.

Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan (about 24 cm in diameter) over medium heat, add the green onion, and stir-fry for 1 minute to infuse the oil. It is ready when the edges of the green onion turn lightly golden.

Add the kimchi and stir-fry over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes. Move to the next step once the edges of the kimchi turn translucent and the sour aroma cooks off. If the kimchi is overly sour, add 1/3 tsp of sugar.

Add the cooked rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes, pressing and cutting through the grains with a spatula to separate them. Drizzle 1/2 tbsp of soy sauce around the rim of the pan to create a smoky charred aroma, then stir-fry for 30 seconds more.
Reduce the heat to low, add 1 tsp of sesame oil and sesame seeds, toss lightly, and turn off the heat.
In another pan, drizzle a tiny bit of cooking oil and fry the egg over medium-low heat for 2 minutes, then place it on top of the cooked rice. Break the yolk and mix it all together to eat.
tips: The more aged and sour the kimchi, the deeper the flavor. Adding 1 tbsp (15 ml) of kimchi juice at the very end yields an even richer taste.
Using cold cooked rice makes it stir-fry with a fluffier, firmer texture. Freshly cooked rice gets mushy, so let the steam dissipate and cool it down before using.

kimchi-jeon.desc: A crispy kimchi pancake that comes to mind on rainy days.
kimchi-jeon.name: Crispy Kimchi Pancake (Kimchi-jeon)
steps: Cut the kimchi into 1cm pieces and cut the onion into thin strips.

In a bowl, combine 100g Korean pancake mix, 150ml water, 3 tbsp (45ml) kimchi juice, and 1/2 tsp sugar, then mix well with a whisk or chopsticks to remove any lumps. The consistency should be thin enough to flow slowly off a spoon.
Add the kimchi and the onion, and mix gently.
Heat 3 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, ladle the batter in, and spread it thin to 12cm in diameter.
Pan-fry for 3 minutes on the front and 3 minutes on the back until golden, then turn the heat up to medium-high for the last 30 seconds to make it extra crispy.
tips: Using cold water in the batter makes it crispier.
Adding 50g of squid or pork makes for a hearty kimchi pancake.

kimchi-jjigae.desc: Traditional kimchi stew simmered with pork and aged kimchi.
kimchi-jjigae.name: Kimchi Stew (Kimchi Jjigae)
steps: Cut the kimchi into 5cm lengths, the pork into bite-sized pieces, the tofu to a thickness of 2cm, cut the onion into thin strips, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Heat cooking oil 1 tsp in a pot over medium heat, stir-fry the pork for 2 minutes until the surface turns white.
Add the kimchi and stir-fry for 5 minutes. Once the kimchi softens and red oil comes to the surface, pour in water 500ml.
When it comes to a boil over high heat, reduce to medium-low heat and simmer for 15 minutes while skimming off any foam.
Add the Korean red pepper flakes, minced garlic, and onion, simmer for 3 more minutes, taste, and if it's too bland, substitute salted fermented shrimp with a pinch of salt (about 1g).
Add the tofu and green onion, simmer for 5 more minutes, and finish.
tips: Stir-frying the kimchi thoroughly brings out its deep flavor.
If the kimchi is too sour, balance the acidity with sugar 1/2 tsp (about 2g).

kimchi-jjim.desc: A deeply braised dish made with aged kimchi and pork.
kimchi-jjim.name: Braised Kimchi and Pork (Kimchi Jjim)
steps: Without shaking off the filling, cut the whole kimchi into 4 to 5 cm lengths starting from the stem part, and cut the pork into 5 cm pieces. Cut the onion into thick strips.
Place the onion on the bottom of the pot, then layer half of the kimchi, the pork, and the remaining kimchi on top in that order.
Sprinkle 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1/2 tbsp sugar, and black pepper on top, and pour 300 ml water around the edges.
When it comes to a boil over high heat, reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid, and braise thoroughly for 30 to 35 minutes. It is done when the pork easily falls apart with chopsticks.
Top with the green onion and simmer for 5 more minutes.
tips: If you are not using aged kimchi, add 1/2 tbsp more sugar to balance the sourness.
It tastes great served on top of rice without needing any other side dishes.

kimchi-kongnamul-guk.desc: A refreshing and spicy hangover soup.
kimchi-kongnamul-guk.name: Kimchi and Soybean Sprout Soup (Kimchi-kongnamul-guk)
steps: Wash the soybean sprout and drain in a colander, cut the kimchi into 2cm pieces, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Put 700ml of water and kimchi in a pot and boil. When it comes to a boil, simmer over medium heat for 5 min to draw out the kimchi flavor.
Add the soybean sprout, cover with a lid, and boil for 7 min. Opening the lid while boiling will cause a grassy smell.
Add minced garlic and Korean red pepper flakes, season with 1/2 tsp of salt, then add the green onion and boil for 1 more min.
tips: Seasoning with 1 tsp (about 6g) of salted fermented shrimp adds extra freshness.
It is great as a hangover soup with rice rolled into it.

kimchi-mandu-jeongol.desc: A spicy hot pot filled with dumplings and vegetables.
kimchi-mandu-jeongol.name: Dumpling Hot Pot (Mandu Jeongol)
steps: Cut the napa cabbage and onion into bite-sized pieces, slice the green onion diagonally, and slice the tofu thickly.
Arrange the napa cabbage, onion, mushroom, and tofu around a pot and place the dumpling in the center.
Mix soup soy sauce 2 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, and minced garlic into water 800 ml, and pour it in.
Cover with a lid, cook over medium heat for 12 minutes, and then top with the green onion.
tips: You can add frozen dumpling straight in without thawing.
Adding noodle noodles at the end makes it a complete meal.

kimchi-mari-bap.desc: North Korean-style cold rice soup immersed in chilled kimchi broth.
kimchi-mari-bap.name: Hwanghae Style Cold Kimchi Rice Soup (Kimchi Mari Bap)
steps: Chop kimchi finely, cut cucumber into thin strips, and boil egg and cut it in half.
Mix 250 ml of cold water with 3 tbsp of kimchi juice, 1/2 tbsp of vinegar, and 1 tsp of sugar to chill.
Put cooked rice in a bowl and top with kimchi, cucumber, and egg.
Pour kimchi juice over it and garnish with sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Add ice cubes for an even more refreshing taste.
Using aged sour kimchi deepens the flavor.

kimchi-mari-guksu.desc: Refreshing noodles served in a tangy kimchi broth.
kimchi-mari-guksu.name: Cold Kimchi Noodle Soup (Kimchi-mari-guksu)
steps: Boil the thin wheat noodles, rinse thoroughly in cold water, and drain. Boil the egg, cut in half, and cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Finely chop the kimchi and mix with 3 tbsp kimchi juice, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, and 500 ml cold water to chill.
Place the thin wheat noodles in a bowl and pour the kimchi broth over it.
Top with the cucumber, egg, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
tips: Adding ice cubes makes it much more refreshing.
Adjust the sugar depending on how sour the kimchi is.

kimchi-ramen.desc: Ramen with a deep broth made by stir-frying kimchi.
kimchi-ramen.name: Kimchi Ramen
steps: Cut the kimchi into 2cm pieces and slice thinly the green onion.
Coat a pot with 1 tsp of cooking oil and stir-fry the kimchi over medium heat for 1 minute to bring out the aroma.
Pour 550ml of water, bring it to a boil, then add the ramen and soup packet and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the egg and green onion, and cook for 1 minute more.
tips: Stir-frying kimchi softens the sourness and makes the broth refreshing.
Even if you use only half the soup packet, the kimchi will add plenty of flavor.

kiwi-yogurt-cup.desc: A layered cup filled with kiwi and yogurt.
kiwi-yogurt-cup.name: Kiwi Yogurt Cup
steps: Peel the kiwi and cut it into cubes.
Layer oatmeal at the bottom of a cup and fill it halfway with yogurt.
Top with the kiwi, cover with the remaining yogurt, and add the kiwi one more time.
Drizzle 1 tsp of honey over it and serve.
tips: Kiwi helps digestion, but some people may be allergic to it.
If it's not sweet enough, increase the amount of honey.

kkaennip-jeon.desc: Pan-fried perilla leaves stuffed with meat filling.
kkaennip-jeon.name: Stuffed Perilla Leaves
steps: Squeeze the moisture out of the tofu, mash it, add the pork, 1/3 tsp of salt, and black pepper, and knead until sticky.
Wash the perilla leaf, pat dry, trim the stems, spread a thin layer of filling on the inside, and fold in half.
Coat the folded perilla leaf lightly in flour and dip in beaten egg.
Heat a pan over medium heat, add 2 tbsp of cooking oil, and pan-fry until golden brown for 3 minutes on each side until cooked through.
tips: Spread the filling thinly so the inside cooks thoroughly.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of vinegar.

kkaennip-yangnyeom.desc: A salty perilla leaf side dish to enjoy on top of rice.
kkaennip-yangnyeom.name: Seasoned Perilla Leaves (Yangnyeom Kkaennip)
steps: Wash perilla leaf one by one, shake off the water, and cut the stems. Mince the green onion finely.

In a bowl, mix soy sauce 3tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1tbsp, minced garlic 1tbsp, green onion, sesame oil 1tbsp, sesame seeds, and water 3tbsp (45ml) to make the seasoning sauce.
Layer 2~3 perilla leaf in a bowl, spread 1tsp of seasoning sauce on each layer, and stack them up.
Age them in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before eating.
tips: Spread the seasoning thinly on each layer so it is not too salty.
You can store them in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

kkakdugi.name: Diced Radish Kimchi (Kkakdugi)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into 2 cm cubes, sprinkle with 2 tbsp salt, pickle for 30 minutes, and drain off the liquid.
Blend onion and ginger until smooth, then mix with 4 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp minced garlic, and 1 tbsp sugar to make the seasoning.
Add the seasoning to the Korean radish, mix thoroughly, then add green onion and mix.
Place in a container, leave at room temperature for a day, and then store in the refrigerator.
tips: The pickled liquid must be discarded so the diced radish kimchi does not get mushy.
It starts to ripen after 3 days.

kkanpunggi.desc: Crispy Chinese-style fried chicken tossed in a sweet and spicy sauce.
kkanpunggi.name: Spicy Garlic Fried Chicken (Kkanpunggi)
steps: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces, season with 1/3 tsp of salt and black pepper, and toss with 1 egg and 5 tbsp of starch.
Fry chicken in 170°C cooking oil for 4 minutes, remove, and fry again at 180°C for 1 more minute to make it crispy. Slice Cheongyang chili and green onion finely.
Sauté minced garlic, green onion, and Cheongyang chili in a pan over low heat for 1 minute to release the aroma.
Add 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of sugar, 2 tbsp of vinegar, and 3 tbsp of water, and boil for 1 minute.
Add the fried chicken, toss quickly over high heat for 30 seconds, and turn off the heat.
tips: Stir-frying too long in the sauce will make it soggy. Finish within 30 seconds.
Making it with chicken breast makes it even leaner.

kkanso-saeu.desc: Crispy fried shrimp coated in a sweet and sour sauce.
kkanso-saeu.name: Sweet and Sour Shrimp (Kkanpoong Saeu)
steps: Prep the shrimp, wipe away moisture, and toss in egg and 3 tbsp of starch to coat.
Deep-fry in 170°C cooking oil for 2 minutes, take them out, and fry for 30 seconds more to make them crispy.
Put 3 tbsp of ketchup, 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of vinegar, and minced garlic in a pan and boil for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and toss quickly.
tips: Frying twice keeps them crispy for a long time.
Eat them right away as they get soggy if left in the sauce too long.

kkomak-bibimbap.desc: Bibimbap mixed with cockle meat, vegetables, and gochujang.
kkomak-bibimbap.name: Cockle Bibimbap (Kkomak Bibimbap)
steps: Desalt the cockles, boil them in boiling water, remove them when they open, and take out only the meat.
Toss the cockle meat with 1 tbsp soy sauce.
Cut the leaf lettuce and cucumber into thin strips.
Place cooked rice, vegetables, and cockles in a bowl, add 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp sesame oil, and sesame seeds, and mix well.
tips: Let the water used to boil cockles settle and use only the clear liquid for soup dishes.
Topping with a fried egg also goes well.

kkomak-muchim.desc: Boiled cockles topped with seasoned soy sauce.
kkomak-muchim.name: Seasoned Cockles (Kkomak Muchim)
steps: Desalt the cockles in salt water and scrub the shells clean.
Put the cockles in boiling water, stir in one direction, and remove them as soon as they open (about 3 minutes).

Mince the green onion and Cheongyang chili, and mix with 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp sesame oil, minced garlic, 1 tsp sugar, and sesame seeds to make the seasoned soy sauce.
Remove one shell from each cockle and place a spoonful of the seasoned soy sauce on top.
tips: Stirring in one direction keeps the meat attached to the shell.
Boiling them for too long makes them tough.

kkongchi-kimchi-jjim.desc: Easy braised dish made with canned saury and aged kimchi.
kkongchi-kimchi-jjim.name: Braised Saury and Kimchi (Kkongchi Kimchi-jjim)
steps: Cut the kimchi into large pieces, cut the onion into thin strips, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Layer the kimchi and onion in a pot, then place the canned saury and its liquid on top.
Add 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, minced garlic, 1 tsp of sugar, and 200 ml of water.
Simmer over medium heat, and once it starts boiling, reduce the heat to low, simmer for 15 minutes, and top with green onion.
tips: Adding the liquid from the canned saury enhances the savory flavor.
If the kimchi is too sour, add a little more sugar.

kkongchi-mu-jorim.desc: Flavorful braised saury with radish that absorbs all the savory seasoning.
kkongchi-mu-jorim.name: Braised Saury with Radish (Kkongchi Mu-jorim)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into thick square chunks and cut the onion into thin strips.
Put the Korean radish, onion, and 300 ml of water in a pot and boil for 8 minutes.
Mix in 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tsp of sugar, and minced garlic, then place the canned saury on top.
Simmer over medium heat for 12 minutes and top with green onion.
tips: Cook the Korean radish first so the seasoning absorbs well.
Since it's canned fish it has little fishiness, but adding a little ginger is also nice.

kkotge-tang.desc: A spicy and refreshing blue crab soup made with Korean radish.
kkotge-tang.name: Spicy Blue Crab Soup (Chungnam Kkotge-tang)
steps: Scrub the blue crab clean with a brush, remove the top shell, and cut it into 4 pieces. Cut the Korean radish into thin rectangular slices.
In a pot, add water 900 ml, Korean radish, Korean red pepper flakes 2 tbsp, gochujang 1 tbsp, and minced garlic, and boil for 10 minutes.
Add the blue crab and boil for 10 minutes. Skim off any foam.
Add the Korean zucchini, onion, green onion, and soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, and boil for 5 more minutes.
tips: Use live blue crabs that you clean yourself, or use thawed frozen ones.
Topping with crown daisy adds a nice aroma.

kodari-jorim.desc: Semi-dried pollack braised with Korean radish.
kodari-jorim.name: Braised Semi-dried Pollack (Kodari-jorim)
steps: Cut the semi-dried pollack into pieces and wash them, cut Korean radish into thick pieces, cut onion into thin strips, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Mix 2 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Place Korean radish and onion at the bottom of a pot, top with the semi-dried pollack, and pour the sauce and 300 ml of water over it.
Simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes while spooning the broth over the fish, then top with green onion.
tips: Cooking the Korean radish first helps the flavors absorb well.
Semi-dried pollack is dried, so it has a chewy texture.

kongnamul-bap.desc: Rice cooked with soybean sprouts on top, served with a seasoned soy sauce.
kongnamul-bap.name: Soybean Sprout Rice (Kongnamul Bap)
steps: Wash uncooked rice and soak for 30 minutes, wash soybean sprout and drain the water.
In a pot, add the soaked uncooked rice and water 300ml, place soybean sprout on top, and bring to a boil over high heat.
When it starts to boil, reduce to low heat for 12 minutes, turn off the heat, and let steam for 5 minutes.
Make a seasoned soy sauce with soy sauce 3 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes, sesame oil 1 tbsp, slice thinly green onion, and sesame seeds to mix and eat with.
tips: Do not open the lid so the soybean sprout does not get tough.
The amount of water was set a little less than usual since water comes out from soybean sprout.

kongtteuchigi-guksu.desc: Jeongseon-style hot noodle soup with thick buckwheat noodles you slurp right up.
kongtteuchigi-guksu.name: Chewy Buckwheat Noodle Soup (Jeongseon Kotteongchigi Guksu)
steps: Boil anchovy in 1 L water for 10 minutes, remove them, and cut potato and Korean zucchini into thin strips.
Add potato, minced garlic, and 2 tbsp soup soy sauce to the broth and boil for 5 minutes.
Boil soba noodle separately, rinse in cold water, and place in a bowl.
Boil Korean zucchini in the broth for 1 minute, pour over the noodles, and top with Korean red pepper flakes.
tips: Boil the noodles separately so the broth doesn't get cloudy.
Dissolving some doenjang (fermented soybean paste) makes it even more savory.

konjac-bibim-noodle.desc: Tangy mixed noodles made with konjac noodles instead of carbs.
konjac-bibim-noodle.name: Konjac Bibim Noodles (Konjac-Bibim-Guksu)
steps: Put konjac in a strainer, rinse twice in cold water to remove the unique smell, and squeeze out the water firmly.
Cut cucumber and cabbage into thin strips. Boil egg for 10 minutes and cut in half.
Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1/2 tsp, and sesame oil 1 tsp to make the sauce.
Add the sauce to konjac and vegetables, mix well, and top with egg and sesame seeds.
tips: The smell comes out better if konjac is blanched in boiling water for 1 minute.
Since konjac noodles have a lot of water, you must squeeze them tightly so the sauce does not get watery.

konjac-bokkeum.desc: A sweet and savory side dish of chewy konjac.
konjac-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Soy Sauce Konjac (Konjac-Jang-Bokkeum)
steps: Cut konjac into bite-sized pieces, blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, and drain in a strainer. Cut onion and carrot into thin strips, and slice thinly green onion.
Pour cooking oil 1 tsp into a pan heated over medium heat and stir-fry minced garlic and green onion for 30 seconds.
Add konjac, onion, and carrot, and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes to evaporate the moisture.
Add soy sauce 1 tbsp and oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp, reduce for 1 minute, and sprinkle with sesame seeds when glossy.
tips: You must stir-fry konjac while evaporating the moisture so the seasoning absorbs well.
The seasoning absorbs better if you make diagonal cuts before slicing.

konjac-bokkeumbap.desc: A low-calorie fried rice using konjac instead of rice.
konjac-bokkeumbap.name: Konjac Fried Rice
steps: Blanch the konjac in boiling water for 2 minutes, strain in a colander, and drain thoroughly. Mince finely the carrot and onion.
Heat 1 tsp cooking oil in a pan and stir-fry the carrot and onion for 2 minutes.
Add the konjac and cooked brown rice, and stir-fry for 3 minutes to evaporate the moisture.
Drizzle 1 tbsp soy sauce along the edge of the pan, stir-fry, then scramble the egg and mix it in.
tips: Evaporate as much moisture from the konjac as possible so the dish won't turn out mushy.
If you don't have cooked brown rice, regular cooked rice works fine.

lemon-ade.desc: A refreshing ade made with lemon and sugar.
lemon-ade.name: Homemade Lemonade (Suje Lemonade)
steps: Rub and wash the lemon with salt, then slice 1 lemon and squeeze the juice from 1 lemon.
Put the lemon slice, 3 tbsp sugar, and 1 tbsp honey in a cup, and press with a spoon to extract the juice.
Add the lemon juice, pour 400 ml of cold water and ice.
Stir and drink immediately.
tips: Change it to sparkling water and it becomes a real ade.
Reduce the sugar if you are worried about sugar intake.

lemon-butter-salmon.desc: Salmon steak finished with butter and lemon.
lemon-butter-salmon.name: Lemon Butter Salmon Steak
steps: Pat the salmon dry with a paper towel and sprinkle with 1/3 tsp salt and black pepper.
Coat the pan with 1 tbsp olive oil and cook the salmon starting skin-side down over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Flip, add 1 tbsp butter, and cook for 3 more minutes while spooning the melted butter over it.
Place on a plate and squeeze lemon juice over it.
tips: Do not touch it at first and sear one side thoroughly so the skin becomes crispy.
It is okay if the inside remains pink.

lettuce-chicken-ssam.desc: A low-calorie meal wrapped with just a thin layer of ssamjang.
lettuce-chicken-ssam.name: Lettuce Chicken Ssam
steps: Boil 500 ml of water and 1/3 tsp of salt in a pot, add the chicken breast, cook on high for 2 minutes, turn off the heat, cover with a lid, and let it sit for 12 minutes. After cooling, shred it thinly.
Wash the iceberg lettuce leaf by leaf, shake off the water, and cut the bell pepper and cucumber into thin strips.
Mix 1 tbsp of doenjang, 1 tsp of gochujang, 1/2 tsp of oligosaccharide syrup, and 1/2 tsp of sesame oil to make the ssamjang.
Place the chicken breast, vegetables, and a little ssamjang on the iceberg lettuce and wrap it up.
tips: Use only 1/2 tsp (about 3g) of ssamjang per wrap to reduce sodium.
Serving with mustard sauce will liven up your appetite.

lowsalt-beef-mu-guk.desc: A low-sodium beef and radish soup flavored with the natural sweetness drawn from Korean radish.
lowsalt-beef-mu-guk.name: Low-Sodium Beef and Radish Soup (Sogogi Mu-guk)
steps: Pat the beef dry with paper towels, cut the Korean radish into bite-sized thin pieces, and slice thinly the green onion.
Heat 1 tbsp of sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the beef and Korean radish over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour 800ml of water, skim off the foam as it comes to a boil, and simmer over medium-low heat for 25 minutes.
Season with minced garlic, 1 tsp of soup soy sauce, and black pepper, then add the green onion and simmer for 3 minutes more.
tips: Simmering the Korean radish thoroughly draws out its sweetness, making it delicious even with reduced soy sauce.
Do not drink all the broth; focus on eating the solid ingredients.

lowsalt-bibim-guksu.desc: Noodles mixed with Korean red pepper flakes and vinegar instead of gochujang and soy sauce.
lowsalt-bibim-guksu.name: Low-Sodium Vinegar Mixed Noodles (Bibim-guksu)
steps: Boil thin wheat noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse vigorously in cold water, and drain.
Cut the cucumber and onion into thin strips.
Mix Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of sesame oil, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Toss the noodles and vegetables with the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Rinsing thin wheat noodles in cold water several times reduces sodium.
The more vegetables you add, the less sauce you need.

lowsalt-broccoli-tofu-bokkeum.desc: A clean-tasting broccoli and tofu stir-fry flavored with garlic and black pepper.
lowsalt-broccoli-tofu-bokkeum.name: Low-Sodium Broccoli and Tofu Stir-Fry (Jeoyeom Broccoli Tofu Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces, blanch in boiling water for 1 min 30 sec, cut the tofu into cubes, and dab dry.
Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan and sear the tofu over medium heat for 3 min until golden.
Add the minced garlic and broccoli, and stir-fry for 2 min.
Drizzle in 1 tsp of soy sauce and black pepper, and stir-fry for 1 more min.
tips: Drizzling soy sauce along the edge of the pan maximizes flavor with a small amount.
Sprinkling sesame seeds on top adds a nutty flavor.

lowsalt-brown-rice-bokkeumbap.desc: Brown rice fried rice with soy sauce reduced to less than a tablespoon.
lowsalt-brown-rice-bokkeumbap.name: Low-Sodium Brown Rice Vegetable Fried Rice (Jeonyeom Hyeonmi Yachae Bokkeumbap)
steps: Mince carrot, onion, and Korean zucchini finely.
Add 1 tsp of cooking oil to a pan and stir-fry the vegetables over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Push them to one side, beat the egg, and scramble it.
Add cooked brown rice, 1 tsp of soy sauce, and black pepper, stir-fry for 3 minutes, and finish by drizzling with sesame oil.
tips: Adding plenty of vegetables makes it delicious even with little soy sauce.
Drizzle the soy sauce along the edge of the pan to infuse a smoky flavor.

lowsalt-chicken-juk.desc: A comforting porridge cooked with savory sesame oil with almost no seasoning.
lowsalt-chicken-juk.name: Low-Sodium Chicken and Vegetable Porridge (Dak-juk)
steps: Boil the chicken breast in boiling water for 12 minutes, shred finely, and mince finely the carrot and Korean zucchini.
Heat 1 tbsp of sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the carrot, Korean zucchini, and cooked rice over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Pour 700ml of water and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes while stirring.
Add the chicken breast and 1/2 tsp of soup soy sauce and simmer for 3 minutes more.
tips: The savory flavor of sesame oil takes the place of salt.
Porridge gets thicker as it cools, so add water to adjust the consistency.

lowsalt-chicken-mushroom-bokkeum.desc: Chicken breast and mushroom stir-fry with reduced sodium enhanced by the aroma of perilla oil.
lowsalt-chicken-mushroom-bokkeum.name: Low-Sodium Chicken Breast and Mushroom Perilla Oil Stir-Fry (Jeonyeom Dakgaseumsal Beoseot Deul-gireum-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces, tear the mushroom, and cut the onion into thin strips.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of perilla oil in a pan and stir-fry the chicken breast over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add the mushroom, onion, and minced garlic, and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Season with 1/4 tsp of salt and black pepper.
tips: The umami flavor released from the mushroom substitutes for salt.
Perilla oil is sensitive to heat, so stir-fry over medium heat.

lowsalt-danhobak-yogurt-salad.desc: A salad enjoyed with the natural sweetness of kabocha squash without salt.
lowsalt-danhobak-yogurt-salad.name: Kabocha Squash Yogurt Salad (Danhobak Yogurt Salad)
steps: Peel the kabocha squash, cut it into bite-sized pieces, steam it in a steamer for 12 minutes, and let it cool.
Chop the mixed nuts coarsely.
Mix 100g of yogurt, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, and black pepper to make the sauce.
Pour the sauce over the kabocha squash and sprinkle the mixed nuts.
tips: It is fine to eat the kabocha squash with the skin on.
Reduce the amount of oligosaccharide syrup if you are worried about sugar.

lowsalt-deulkkae-tofu-jorim.desc: Braised tofu with reduced sodium enhanced by the nutty flavor of perilla seeds.
lowsalt-deulkkae-tofu-jorim.name: Low-Sodium Braised Tofu with Perilla Seeds (Deulkkae Tofu-jorim)
steps: Cut the tofu into thick slices, pat dry, and cut the onion into thin strips.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan and pan-fry the tofu on both sides for 3 minutes each until golden brown.
Add 150ml of water, 1 tsp of soy sauce, minced garlic, and onion, and braise over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add perilla seed powder and sesame oil and braise for 2 minutes more.
tips: Pan-frying the tofu first prevents it from breaking apart and adds a nutty flavor.
Perilla seeds contain almost no sodium, making them great for reducing salt.

lowsalt-gaji-deulgireum.desc: Eggplant stir-fried with less than a spoonful of soy sauce.
lowsalt-gaji-deulgireum.name: Low-Sodium Eggplant Stir-Fried in Perilla Oil (Gaji-deulgireum-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the eggplant into bite-sized pieces, soak them in water for 5 minutes, and squeeze out the water.
Coat a pan with 1 tbsp of perilla oil and stir-fry the eggplant over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and 1 tsp of soy sauce, and stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Squeezing out the water helps it absorb less oil.
Cover with a lid and cook over low heat to make it tender.

lowsalt-kongnamul-muchim.desc: Soybean sprouts tossed with vinegar and sesame oil instead of salt.
lowsalt-kongnamul-muchim.name: Low-Sodium Seasoned Soybean Sprouts (Jeoyeom Kongnamul Muchim)
steps: Wash the soybean sprout, place in a pot with 3 tbsp of water, cover, and steam over high heat for 5 min.
Drain, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out excess water firmly.
Mix 1 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of sesame oil, minced garlic, and 1/4 tsp of salt.
Toss the soybean sprout with the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Opening the lid while boiling will cause a grassy smell.
The tartness of the vinegar replaces the salty flavor.

lowsalt-lemon-chicken.desc: Chicken breast seasoned with lemon and garlic instead of salt.
lowsalt-lemon-chicken.name: Low-Sodium Lemon Chicken Breast
steps: Slice the thick part of chicken breast horizontally to make the thickness even and squeeze juice from lemon.
Coat chicken breast with lemon 1 tbsp, minced garlic, black pepper, and salt 1/4 tsp, then marinate for 15 min.
Heat olive oil 1 tbsp in a pan and cook over medium heat for 5 min on each side until cooked through.
Let rest for 5 min, slice into bite-sized pieces, and serve with remaining lemon on the side.
tips: The sourness of lemon replaces the salty taste, so it's delicious even with reduced salt.
Brushing with olive oil while marinating makes it more moist.

lowsalt-lemon-garlic-shrimp.desc: Shrimp stir-fried with lemon and garlic without salt.
lowsalt-lemon-garlic-shrimp.name: Low-Sodium Lemon Garlic Stir-Fried Shrimp (Jeonyeom Lemon Maneul Saewu-bokkeum)
steps: Clean the shrimp and pat them dry.
Stir-fry 1 tbsp of olive oil and minced garlic in a pan over low heat for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry over medium heat for 2 minutes 30 seconds.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle with lemon juice and black pepper, and mix.
tips: Shrimp has natural salinity so salt is not needed.
Add the lemon juice after turning off the heat to preserve the aroma.

lowsalt-mackerel-gui.desc: Mackerel baked with lemon and black pepper instead of salt.
lowsalt-mackerel-gui.name: Low-Sodium Lemon Mackerel (Mackerel Gui)
steps: Cut the mackerel in half, wipe off the moisture, and make slashes on it.
Apply lemon juice, minced garlic, and black pepper, then marinate for 15 minutes.
Pour 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan and cook skin-side down over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Flip and cook for 4 more minutes, then serve with lemon.
tips: Use fresh mackerel and avoid salted mackerel.
Lemon takes away the fishy smell.

lowsalt-miyeok-guk.desc: A seaweed soup seasoned with fragrant sesame oil instead of heavy soup soy sauce.
lowsalt-miyeok-guk.name: Low-Sodium Beef Seaweed Soup (Jeoyeom Sogogi Miyeok-guk)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 10 min, rinse, cut into 5cm pieces, and dab the beef to remove blood.
Heat 1 tbsp of sesame oil in a pot and stir-fry the beef and dried seaweed over medium heat for 3 min.
Pour in 800 ml of water, and once it comes to a boil, simmer over medium-low heat for 20 min.
Season with minced garlic and 1 tsp of soup soy sauce, then simmer for 5 more min.
tips: Boiling it long enough brings out the natural sweetness from the dried seaweed.
You can cut sodium even further by drinking only half the broth.

lowsalt-oi-sikcho-salad.desc: A refreshing cucumber salad tossed in vinegar without salting them first.
lowsalt-oi-sikcho-salad.name: Low-Sodium Cucumber Vinegar Salad (Jeoyeom Oi Sikcho Salad)
steps: Slice the cucumber thinly on the diagonal and cut the onion into thin strips.
Mix 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, 1/4 tsp of salt, and sesame oil to make the dressing.
Add the dressing to the cucumber and onion, and toss gently.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately.
tips: Skipping the salting process significantly reduces sodium.
Toss right before eating to keep it crunchy.

lowsalt-onion-pickle.desc: Sweet and sour onion pickles made with vinegar and oligosaccharide syrup without salt.
lowsalt-onion-pickle.name: Low-Sodium Onion Pickles (Jeonyeom Yangpa Pickle)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips and place it in a jar.
Put 100ml of vinegar, 100ml of water, 3 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, and black pepper in a pot and bring to a boil.
Pour the boiling pickling liquid over the onion.
After letting it cool, leave it in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before eating.
tips: Pairing it with meat and fish dishes keeps things refreshing even with less salt seasoning.
Keep it refrigerated and eat within a week.

lowsalt-potato-soup.desc: A smooth soup made with potato and milk without salt.
lowsalt-potato-soup.name: Low-Sodium Potato Milk Soup
steps: Peel and slice the potato thinly, and cut the onion into thin strips.
Melt butter in a pot and stir-fry the onion over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the potato and 200 ml of water, and boil for 12 minutes until tenderly cooked.
Add 300 ml of milk, blend smoothly with a blender, heat it up, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: Stir-frying the onion thoroughly brings out sweetness, eliminating the need for salt.
Boiling over high heat will cause the milk to separate, so heat it over low heat.

lowsalt-potato-yogurt-salad.desc: Potato salad tossed with yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
lowsalt-potato-yogurt-salad.name: Low-Sodium Potato Yogurt Salad
steps: Peel and boil the potato, mash it, and finely chop the cucumber and carrot.
Marinate the cucumber in 1/4 tsp of salt for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the moisture.
Mix 100g of yogurt, 1 tsp of vinegar, and black pepper to make the sauce.
Toss the potato, cucumber, and carrot with the sauce.
tips: Using yogurt instead of mayonnaise cuts down both calories and sodium.
It tastes even better when chilled in the refrigerator.

lowsalt-salmon-lemon.desc: Salmon pan-seared with lemon and black pepper without salt.
lowsalt-salmon-lemon.name: Low-Sodium Lemon Grilled Salmon
steps: Pat the salmon dry with paper towels, rub with lemon juice, minced garlic, and black pepper, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan and cook over medium heat, starting skin-side down, for 4 minutes.
Flip and cook for 3 minutes more.
Transfer to a plate and serve with lemon wedges.
tips: Salmon naturally has a rich umami flavor, so it tastes delicious without added sodium.
Serve with grilled vegetables to make it a complete meal.

lowsalt-shabu.desc: Low-sodium shabu-shabu blanched in broth and dipped in vinegar sauce.
lowsalt-shabu.name: Low-Sodium Beef and Vegetable Shabu-Shabu
steps: Add kombu to 1 L of water, boil for 5 minutes, and remove it.
Cut napa cabbage, mushroom, and mung bean sprout into bite-sized pieces and arrange them.
Mix 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, minced garlic, and 1 tbsp of water to make the sauce.
Add vegetables to the broth, and when it boils, briefly blanch the beef and dip it into the sauce.
tips: Do not season the broth; let the sauce provide all the flavor.
If you avoid drinking the soup, your sodium intake drops significantly.

lowsalt-sigeumchi-namul.desc: Spinach seasoned with a pinch of salt.
lowsalt-sigeumchi-namul.name: Low-Sodium Spinach Seasoned with Sesame Oil (Sigeumchi Namul)
steps: Trim the roots of spinach, blanch in boiling water for 40 seconds, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out the moisture firmly.
Cut into 5cm pieces and loosen them up.
Add 1 tbsp of sesame oil, minced garlic, and 1/4 tsp of salt, then toss gently.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Rinse in cold water after blanching to keep the color vibrant and crisp.
If the sesame oil aroma is strong, you can reduce the salt even more.

lowsalt-tofu-lemon-salad.desc: Tofu salad tossed with lemon and olive oil without salt.
lowsalt-tofu-lemon-salad.name: Low-Sodium Tofu Lemon Salad
steps: Blanch tofu in boiling water for 3 min, drain, and dice into bite-sized pieces.
Dice tomato and cucumber, finely mince onion, soak in cold water for 5 min, and drain.
Mix olive oil 1 tbsp, lemon, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Put all ingredients in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing, and toss.
tips: Soaking onion in cold water removes the sharp pungency and makes it mild.
Adding nuts on top adds a nutty crunch.

lowsalt-tofu-steak.desc: Tofu steak pan-fried with black pepper and onion without salt.
lowsalt-tofu-steak.name: Low-Sodium Tofu Steak
steps: Wrap the tofu in a cotton cloth, squeeze out the water firmly to mash it, and mince the onion finely.
Mix the tofu, onion, egg, and black pepper, and shape them into thick patties.
Coat a pan with 1 tbsp of olive oil and pan-fry them golden brown over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side.
Drizzle with lemon juice to serve.
tips: You must squeeze out the water firmly so they hold their shape.
Serving with grilled vegetables is great.

lowsalt-tomato-egg.desc: An egg stir-fry with reduced sodium achieved through the umami of tomatoes.
lowsalt-tomato-egg.name: Low-Sodium Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
steps: Cut the tomato into bite-sized pieces and slice thinly the green onion. Beat the egg with 1/4 tsp of salt and set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan, cook the egg until 70% done, and remove from the pan.
In the same pan, add the green onion and tomato, stir-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes, and add 1 tsp of sugar.
Return the egg to the pan and toss together for 1 minute more to finish.
tips: Stir-frying the tomato thoroughly brings out its umami flavor.
Removing the egg temporarily keeps it tender.

lowsalt-veggie-omelet.desc: An omelet flavored with vegetables and black pepper instead of salt.
lowsalt-veggie-omelet.name: Low-Sodium Vegetable Omelet (Jeoyeom Chaeso Omelet)
steps: Finely mince the onion, bell pepper, and mushroom, stir-fry in 1/2 tbsp of olive oil over medium heat for 3 min, and set aside.
Beat the egg and mix in the black pepper.
Pour the remaining olive oil into the pan, add the egg mixture, and cook over low heat until half set.
Top with the cooked vegetables, fold in half, and cook for 1 more min.
tips: Cook slowly over low heat so the outside doesn't tear.
Serve with tomatoes for a fresh touch.

lowsalt-veggie-scramble.desc: Scrambled eggs flavored with black pepper and vegetables instead of salt.
lowsalt-veggie-scramble.name: Low-Sodium Vegetable Egg Scramble
steps: Finely chop onion, bell pepper, and mushroom.
Heat olive oil 1 tbsp in a pan and sauté vegetable over medium heat for 3 min.
Beat egg 3 times, mix with black pepper, and pour into the pan.
Cook over low heat for 1 min 30 sec while stirring with a spatula until soft and curdled.
tips: The natural saltiness of egg is enough. Great for breakfast.
Cooking slowly over low heat makes it tender.

makguksu.desc: Gangwon-style buckwheat noodles tossed in a sweet and sour sauce.
makguksu.name: Buckwheat Noodles (Makguksu)
steps: Boil the soba noodle, rinse in cold water, and drain. Boil the egg for 10 min and cut it in half.
Cut into thin strips the cucumber and chop the kimchi finely.
Mix gochujang 2 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, and sesame oil 1 tbsp to make the sauce.
Toss the soba noodle with the sauce, kimchi, and cucumber, then top with the egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Serve with broth on the side to make it cold noodle soup style.
Adding blended Asian pear will make it sweet.

mapa-dubu.name: Mapo Tofu (Mapa Dubu)
steps: Dice tofu into 2cm sizes, blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, and drain in a sieve. Slice largely green onion and Cheongyang chili thinly.
Coat a pan heated over medium heat with 1 tbsp of cooking oil, and stir-fry minced garlic and 2/3 of green onion for 30 seconds to release the aroma.
Add ground pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes until cooked, then add 1 tbsp of gochujang and 1/2 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add 200 ml of water, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce, and 1/2 tsp of sugar, and when it comes to a boil, add tofu and boil for 3 minutes.
Dissolve 1 tbsp of flour in 3 tbsp (45 ml) of water, add it little by little, and boil for 1 minute until it becomes thick.
Add the remaining green onion, Cheongyang chili, and 1 tsp of sesame oil, mix well, and finish.
tips: Blanching tofu makes it firm so it won't break apart.
Serving it over rice makes Mapo Tofu Rice Bowl.

mapa-gaji-deopbap.desc: Rice bowl topped with eggplant and meat braised in a spicy sauce.
mapa-gaji-deopbap.name: Eggplant Mapo Tofu Rice Bowl (Mapa Gaji Deopbap)
steps: Dice eggplant and slice green onion thinly.
Add 2 tbsp of cooking oil to a pan and stir-fry minced garlic, green onion, and pork over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add 1 tbsp of gochujang and 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, stir-fry for 30 seconds, then add eggplant and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in 200 ml of water, cover with a lid, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in a mixture of 1 tsp of starch dissolved in 1 tbsp of water, and once thickened, pour over cooked rice.
tips: Eggplant absorbs water, so measure the water precisely.
Add Cheongyang chili for an even spicier kick.

mapo-dwaeji-galbi.desc: Mapo-style pork ribs in a sweet soy sauce marinade.
mapo-dwaeji-galbi.name: Mapo-Style Pork Ribs (Mapo Dwaeji Galbi)
steps: Soak pork in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood and make score cuts.
Blend onion and mix with 4 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of sugar, minced garlic, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, black pepper, and sesame oil.
Toss pork in the marinade and let it marinate for at least 2 hours.
Cook in a pan over medium heat for 7 minutes on each side until cooked through to the center.
tips: Brushing oligosaccharide syrup on at the end adds a nice gloss.
Enjoy wrapped in lettuce or alongside seasoned green onion salad.

masan-agujjim.desc: Spicy braised monkfish loaded with soybean sprout and water dropwort.
masan-agujjim.name: Masan Agujjim
steps: Cut the monkfish into pieces, blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes, and take it out. Wash the soybean sprout and cut the water dropwort to 5cm.
Make the sauce by mixing 4 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of minced garlic, and 1 tbsp of sugar.
Put soybean sprout and monkfish in a pot, add the sauce and 300 ml of water, and boil over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Top with water dropwort, pour in 1 tbsp of starch dissolved in 2 tbsp of water, and boil for 2 more minutes.
tips: Soybean sprout releases water, so start with only a little water.
Stir-frying rice in the leftover sauce is a treat.

meat-sauce-spaghetti.desc: A hearty pasta made with ground beef meat sauce.
meat-sauce-spaghetti.name: Meat Sauce Spaghetti
steps: Mince onion and carrot finely. Boil water 1L, add salt 2 tsp, cook spaghetti for 6~7 minutes, and drain while reserving pasta water 100ml.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 1 tbsp, and sauté minced garlic, onion, and carrot over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add beef, and sauté for 3 minutes until fully cooked.
Add pasta sauce 250g and pasta water, and simmer over low heat for 8 minutes.
Add spaghetti, toss for 1 minute, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: You must stir-fry the beef thoroughly so there is no gamey smell.
Blending fresh tomatoes into it makes it even fresher.

memil-chongtteok.desc: Gangwon-do style buckwheat wraps stuffed with napa cabbage and kimchi filling.
memil-chongtteok.name: Buckwheat Chongtteok (Memil Chongtteok)
steps: Blanch napa cabbage in boiling water, squeeze out the liquid, chop it finely, and mix with chopped kimchi and 1 tbsp sesame oil to make the filling.
Make a thin batter using 1 cup buckwheat flour, 1/3 tsp salt, and 200 ml water.
Grease a pan with cooking oil, cook the batter thinly, and place the filling on top.
Roll it up tightly, roll back and forth to brown evenly on both sides, and slice into bite-sized pieces.
tips: Squeeze the moisture completely out of the filling so it doesn't get soggy.
Slice into bite-sized pieces and plate them.

memil-jeonbyeong.desc: Buckwheat crepes rolled with a savory kimchi and pork filling.
memil-jeonbyeong.name: Buckwheat Crepe Roll (Memil Jeonbyeong)
steps: Finely chop kimchi, squeeze out excess liquid, mince pork, stir-fry in a pan for 3 minutes, let cool, and mix with 1 tsp sesame oil to make the filling.
Mix 1 cup buckwheat flour, 1/3 tsp salt, and 200 ml water to make a thin batter.
Lightly grease a pan with cooking oil, spread the batter thinly into a round shape, and place the filling on one side.
Roll it up tightly, place the seam side down, and cook while rolling until golden brown.
tips: Spread the batter thinly so the filling doesn't show through and it remains chewy.
Serve with a side of soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

minari-muchim.desc: A sweet, spicy, and fragrant seasoned water dropwort dish.
minari-muchim.name: Seasoned Water Dropwort (Minari Muchim)
steps: Trim the roots and withered leaves of the water dropwort and cut them into 5cm lengths.
Blanch the water dropwort in 1L of boiling water for only 20 seconds, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out the excess moisture firmly.
Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, minced garlic, and sesame oil in a bowl to make the seasoning.
Add the water dropwort, toss lightly, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching for too long will cause the fragrance to fade. 20 seconds is just right.
Adjust the tartness with the amount of vinegar.

mini-burger.desc: Bite-sized hamburgers made with dinner rolls.
mini-burger.name: Mini Burger
steps: Mince the onion finely, mix with the pork, breadcrumbs 2 tbsp, salt 1/3 tsp, and black pepper, knead well, divide into 6 portions, and shape into flat patties.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, and cook the patties completely for 4 minutes on each side.
Cut the dinner roll in half and toast in a dry pan.
Top the bread with iceberg lettuce, the patty, cheese, tomato, and ketchup, then cover.
tips: Cook them all the way through to the center.
Mixing in some beef adds great flavor.

misoshiru.desc: A Japanese soybean paste soup boiled with doenjang, tofu, and dried seaweed.
misoshiru.name: Miso Soup (Misoshiru)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 5 minutes and squeeze out the water. Cut the tofu into 1.5cm cubes, and slice thinly the green onion.
Put water 600ml, anchovy 10g, and kombu in a pot and bring to a boil; just before it boils, remove the kombu, boil for 5 minutes, and remove the anchovy.
Add tofu and dried seaweed and boil for 2 minutes.
Lower the heat, dissolve doenjang through a strainer into the soup, add green onion just before it boils, and turn off the heat.
tips: Boiling doenjang for too long makes its aroma fade. Dissolve it at the very end.
Boiling kombu to make the broth deepens the umami flavor.

mixed-fruit-yogurt-salad.desc: A salad tossed with assorted fruits and yogurt.
mixed-fruit-yogurt-salad.name: Fruit Yogurt Salad
steps: Cut the strawberry, kiwi, and banana into bite-sized pieces.
Mix 150 g of yogurt and 1 tbsp of honey to make the dressing.
Place the fruits and blueberry in a large bowl.
Add the dressing and toss lightly to serve.
tips: Add the banana at the very end to minimize browning.
Topping it with mixed nuts adds a nutty flavor.

miyeok-naengguk.desc: Tangy and refreshing cold soup made with rehydrated dried seaweed.
miyeok-naengguk.name: Cold Seaweed Soup (Miyeok Naengguk)
steps: Soak dried seaweed in cold water for 10 minutes, rinse, and cut to bite-sized pieces.
Cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Dissolve 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, 2 tbsp of vinegar, and 1 tbsp of sugar in 400 ml of water to make the broth.
Add the dried seaweed and cucumber, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanch the dried seaweed in boiling water for 10 seconds to reduce the fishy taste.
Serve immediately with ice cubes so it stays cold.

morning-bread-egg-sandwich.desc: Dinner rolls stuffed with boiled egg salad.
morning-bread-egg-sandwich.name: Dinner Roll Egg Sandwich
steps: Boil the egg for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel, and mash.
Mix mayonnaise 3 tbsp, salt 1/4 tsp, and black pepper into the mashed egg.
Make a slit in the center of the dinner roll and fill with the egg salad.
Place on a plate and serve immediately.
tips: If the filling is too wet, the bread will get soggy, so reduce the mayonnaise.
Adding finely chopped cucumber pickle gives a tangy flavor.

mukeunji-godeungeo-jorim.desc: Jeolla-style braised dish made with aged kimchi and mackerel.
mukeunji-godeungeo-jorim.name: Braised Mackerel with Aged Kimchi (Mukeunji Godeungeo-jorim)
steps: Cut the mackerel into segments and wash them, and tear the kimchi into large pieces. Cut the Korean radish into thick pieces and cut the onion into thin strips.
Place the Korean radish, onion, and kimchi at the bottom of a pot, then put the mackerel on top.
Mix Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, minced garlic, sugar 1 tsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, and water 300 ml, then pour it over.
Simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes, spooning the broth over the ingredients.
tips: If the kimchi is too sour, rinse it once in water.
The kimchi takes away the fishy smell of the mackerel.

mukssabal.desc: Cold acorn jelly soup mixed with kimchi and cucumber in a chilled broth.
mukssabal.name: Cold Acorn Jelly Soup (Mukssabal)
steps: Cut acorn jelly into thin strips, finely chop kimchi, and cut cucumber into thin strips.
Mix 400 ml water with 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 tbsp soup soy sauce to make the broth and chill it.
Place acorn jelly, kimchi, and cucumber in a bowl.
Pour in the broth and top with crushed roasted seaweed, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
tips: Drain the acorn jelly on a strainer beforehand so the broth doesn't get watery.
Add ice cubes to make it extra refreshing.

mul-naengmyeon.desc: Homestyle cold naengmyeon served in a sweet and tangy broth.
mul-naengmyeon.name: Cold Buckwheat Noodle Soup (Mul-naengmyeon)
steps: Mix water 700 ml, beef bouillon powder 1 tsp, soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, sugar 2 tbsp, and salt 1/2 tsp, then chill in the freezer for 40 minutes.
Boil naengmyeon noodles in boiling water for 1 minute 30 seconds, rinse vigorously in cold water, and squeeze out all the water.
Boil the egg, cut it in half, and cut the cucumber and Korean pear into thin strips.
Place naengmyeon noodles in a bowl, top with the garnishes, and pour the cold broth over.
tips: Rinsing by rubbing in cold water makes them chewy.
Using store-bought naengmyeon broth makes it even easier.

muneo-sukhoe.desc: Tender boiled octopus served with chogochujang (spicy vinegar sauce).
muneo-sukhoe.name: Boiled Octopus (Muneo Sukhoe)
steps: Pat the octopus dry with paper towels and slice thinly on an angle.
Mix gochujang 2 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and sesame oil to make the chojang.
Place the octopus on a plate and serve with the chojang on the side.
It is also great wrapped in lettuce or perilla leaf.
tips: Slice the octopus thinly by laying the knife flat so it stays tender.
It is also delicious dipped in sesame oil and salt.

munguh-gambas.desc: Octopus and garlic simmered in olive oil.
munguh-gambas.name: Octopus Gambas
steps: Cut the octopus into bite-sized pieces and dice the tomato.
In a small pan, simmer olive oil 1/2 cup and minced garlic over low heat for 3 minutes to release the aroma.
Add the tomato and octopus, simmer for 3 minutes, and season with salt 1/2 tsp and black pepper.
Toast the baguette and serve on the side.
tips: Heat slowly over low heat so the garlic does not burn.
It is also great to toss pasta into the leftover oil.

musaengchae-namul.desc: A light and clean side dish of sautéed julienned radish.
musaengchae-namul.name: Sautéed Radish (Musaengchae Namul)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into thin 5cm-long strips and slice the green onion thinly.
Coat a pan with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and sauté the Korean radish over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add 100ml of water, minced garlic, and 1/2 tsp of salt, cover with a lid, and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the green onion and sesame seeds, and stir-fry for 1 minute.
tips: Covering with a lid after adding water makes the Korean radish translucent.
Adding perilla seed powder makes it nutty and savory.

mushroom-bokkeum.desc: Chewy stir-fried mushrooms quickly cooked over high heat.
mushroom-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Mushrooms (Mushroom-bokkeum)
steps: Do not wash the mushroom in water; instead, wipe it with a damp paper towel and tear it into bite-sized pieces or cut it to 0.5cm thickness. Cut the onion into thin strips.
In a pan heated over high heat, add cooking oil 1tbsp, minced garlic, and onion, and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

Do not add the mushroom all at once; add it in two or three batches and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes so the pan does not cool down. If liquid comes out, stir-fry a little longer until the moisture evaporates.
Season with salt 1/3tsp, oyster sauce, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 30 seconds more.
Finish by adding the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Washing the mushroom will release water and make it soggy.
Adding 5g of butter at the end gives it a nutty flavor.

mushroom-cream-risotto.desc: An easy mushroom cream risotto made with cooked rice.
mushroom-cream-risotto.name: Mushroom Cream Risotto
steps: Slice thinly mushroom and mince finely onion.
Melt butter 1 tbsp in a pan, and sauté onion for 1 minute and mushroom for 3 minutes.
Pour in milk 300ml and water 100ml, and when it comes to a boil, add cooked rice and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes while stirring.
Tear and add cheese to melt, and season with salt 1/3 tsp and black pepper.
tips: As cooked rice absorbs the milk, it becomes thick. Stir frequently.
Adding bacon or shrimp is also delicious.

mushroom-cream-soup.desc: A smooth cream soup made by blending mushrooms.
mushroom-cream-soup.name: Mushroom Cream Soup
steps: Mince the mushroom and onion.
Melt 1 tbsp of butter in a pot, sauté the mushroom and onion over medium heat for 6 minutes, then add 1 tbsp of flour and sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in 500 ml of milk a little at a time while stirring, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smoothly with a hand blender or mixer, and season with 1/2 tsp of salt and black pepper.
tips: Sautéing the flour eliminates the raw flour taste.
Serve with croutons or bread on the side.

mushroom-egg-scramble.desc: A protein scramble made with mushroom and egg.
mushroom-egg-scramble.name: Mushroom Egg Scramble
