steps: Slice the mushroom thinly, and beat egg 3 with milk 2 tbsp and salt 1/4 tsp.
Coat a pan with olive oil and sauté the mushroom over medium heat for 3 minutes to evaporate moisture.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook over low heat for 1 minute and 30 seconds while stirring with a spatula until softly set.
Sprinkle black pepper and serve.
tips: Stirring slowly over low heat makes it tender.
Adding salt later to the mushroom prevents too much water from coming out.

mushroom-tofu-tang.desc: A clear and light broth infused with mushroom aroma.
mushroom-tofu-tang.name: Mushroom Tofu Soup (Beoseot Dubu Tang)
steps: Tear or slice mushroom into bite-sized pieces and cut tofu into 1.5cm thickness. Slice green onion thinly at an angle.
Pour water 500ml into a pot, and when it comes to a boil, add mushroom and minced garlic and boil for 3 minutes.
Season with soy sauce 1 tbsp and salt 1/4 tsp, add tofu, and boil for 3 more minutes.
Add green onion and black pepper, boil for 1 minute, and turn off the heat.
tips: Mixing different types of mushrooms deepens the flavor.
You can also drop a few drops of sesame oil at the end.

muu-saengchae.desc: Crispy and refreshing sweet-and-sour radish salad.
muu-saengchae.name: Spicy Radish Salad (Muu-saengchae)
steps: Peel the Korean radish and cut into fine strips 0.3cm thick. Using a mandoline makes it easy.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt over the Korean radish, pickle for 5 minutes, and then firmly squeeze out and discard the released water.
First toss the Korean radish with 2 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes to tint it red.
Add 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of vinegar, minced garlic, and green onion, and toss gently. If the flavor is lacking, add a pinch of salt (about 1g).
Add sesame oil and sesame seeds and mix.
tips: Coating with Korean red pepper flakes first yields a pretty color and prevents excess liquid.
It is the crunchiest when eaten right after making.

myeolchi-bokkeum.desc: A crispy, sweet, and savory staple side dish.
myeolchi-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Anchovies (Myeolchi-bokkeum)
steps: Dry-roast the anchovy in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 2 minutes to get rid of the fishy smell. Sift through a strainer to shake off crumbs.
In the same pan, drizzle 1 tbsp of cooking oil and stir-fry minced garlic and Cheongyang chili for 30 seconds to release the aroma.
Add 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, and 2 tbsp of water, and simmer over low heat. When the sauce bubbles, add the anchovy and stir-fry quickly for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, add the remaining 1/2 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup and sesame seeds, and mix. Letting it cool for a moment makes it crispy.
tips: Anchovies are naturally salty, so we used very little soy sauce (watch out for sodium).
Stir-frying 30g of nuts together makes it a nutritious side dish.

myeolchi-guksu.desc: Banquet noodles with a refreshing anchovy broth.
myeolchi-guksu.name: Anchovy Noodle Soup (Myeolchi-guksu)
steps: Remove the entrails from the anchovy, stir-fry in a dry pan for 1 minute, boil with 1.2 L water and kombu, take out the kombu after 10 minutes, boil for 5 minutes more, and take out the anchovy.
Season the broth with 2 tbsp soup soy sauce.
Cut the Korean zucchini into thin strips and stir-fry in cooking oil, make egg garnish and cut into thin strips, and boil the thin wheat noodles and rinse in cold water.
Place the thin wheat noodles in a bowl, pour hot broth over it, and top with toppings and sesame seeds.
tips: Stir-frying the anchovy removes the fishy smell.
Take out the kombu early since boiling it too long makes it slimy.

myeongran-butter-rice.desc: A bowl of warm cooked rice mixed with pollock roe and butter.
myeongran-butter-rice.name: Pollock Roe Butter Rice (Myeongran Butter-bap)
steps: Peel the pollock roe to extract only the eggs.
Place 1 tsp of butter on warm cooked rice to melt it.
Add pollock roe and 1/2 tsp of sesame oil.
Sprinkle with roasted seaweed and sesame seeds and mix well.
tips: The cooked rice must be hot for the butter to melt well.
If you are worried about raw pollock roe, stir-fry it in a pan for 1 minute before using.

myeongran-egg-roll.desc: A fancy rolled omelet filled with salty pollock roe.
myeongran-egg-roll.name: Pollock Roe Rolled Omelet (Myeongran Gyeran-mari)
steps: Peel the pollock roe to extract only the eggs, and slice thinly the green onion.
Beat 3 egg, and mix with the green onion and half of the pollock roe. Since the pollock roe is salty, do not add salt.
Lightly coat a pan heated over low heat with cooking oil, pour half of the egg mixture, and when the edges are cooked, place the remaining pollock roe in the center and roll it up tightly.
Roll it one more time with the remaining egg mixture, let it cool slightly, and slice it.
tips: Since the pollock roe is salty, do not add salt.
Roll it slowly over low heat so the pollock roe doesn't burst.

myeongran-pasta.desc: A savory Japanese-style pasta made with butter and pollock roe.
myeongran-pasta.name: Pollock Roe Pasta
steps: Boil 500ml of water, add 1 tsp of salt, cook the spaghetti for 7 minutes, and drain in a colander. Reserve 3 tbsp (45ml) of pasta water.
Peel the pollock roe to extract only the eggs and place them in a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp of butter, 3 tbsp of milk, and half of the pollock roe into a pan, and stir to dissolve over low heat for 1 minute.
Add the spaghetti and pasta water, toss for 1 minute, place on a plate, and top with the remaining pollock roe, roasted seaweed, and black pepper.
tips: Since the pollock roe is salty, only season the boiling water with salt.
Stir-frying over high heat for too long makes the pollock roe dry.

naeng-somyeon.desc: Thin wheat noodles served with a chilled soy sauce broth for dipping.
naeng-somyeon.name: Cold Thin Wheat Noodles (Naeng Somyeon)
steps: Put 300 ml of water and 10 g of anchovy in a pot, boil for 5 minutes, and take out anchovy.
Add 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of mirin, and 1 tsp of sugar to the broth, boil for 2 more minutes, and cool it by placing it in the freezer for 15 minutes or by adding ice to make it cold.
Cut cucumber into thin strips and cut roasted seaweed thinly with scissors. Boil egg for 10 minutes and cut in half.
Put thin wheat noodles into 2 L of boiling water and boil for 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Rub and rinse thin wheat noodles in cold water 3 to 4 times to remove the starchiness, then drain through a sieve.
Place thin wheat noodles neatly in a bowl and top with cucumber, roasted seaweed, and egg. Eat by dipping into the cold broth.
tips: You must wash off the noodle starch to make them chewy.
You need to boil and cool the broth once to make it clean and free from fishy smell.

naengi-doenjang-guk.desc: A comforting soybean paste soup filled with the aroma of spring shepherd's purse.
naengi-doenjang-guk.name: Shepherd's Purse Soybean Paste Soup (Naengi Doenjang-guk)
steps: Scrape the dirt off the roots of the shepherd's purse with a knife, wash multiple times, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Pour water 600 ml into a pot, dissolve doenjang 2 tbsp, and bring to a boil.
When it boils, add the minced garlic and the root side of the shepherd's purse first, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu, the remaining shepherd's purse, and green onion, and boil for 3 more minutes.
tips: Shepherd's purse has a lot of dirt, so wash it while changing the water several times.
Using rice-rinsing water makes the soup even more savory.

naengi-muchim.desc: Shepherd's purse greens seasoned tangy and spicy with gochujang.
naengi-muchim.name: Seasoned Shepherd's Purse (Naengi-muchim)
steps: Trim and wash the shepherd's purse, blanch in boiling water without salt for 30 seconds, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out the water firmly.
Cut into bite-sized pieces.
Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, vinegar 1/2 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Toss the shepherd's purse in the sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching for too long will cause the aroma to fade.
Seasoning it with doenjang gives it a savory flavor.

naengso-ba.desc: Buckwheat noodles dipped in cold tsuyu.
naengso-ba.name: Cold Soba (Naengsoba)
steps: Boil soba noodle in boiling water according to the package time, rinse thoroughly in cold water, and drain.
Mix water 150ml and tsuyu 3tbsp and chill.
Grate Korean radish and squeeze out the moisture, and slice thinly green onion.
Place soba noodle on a plate, top with crushed roasted seaweed, and serve with the sauce, Korean radish, green onion, and wasabi.
tips: Rigorously rinsing in cold water to wash off the starch makes them chewy.
Floating ice cubes makes it even colder and more refreshing.

naju-gomtang.desc: Clear and clean Naju-style beef bone soup.
naju-gomtang.name: Clear Beef Soup (Naju-gomtang)
steps: Soak the beef in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood.
Put water 2 L, beef, Korean radish, and 1/2 of the green onion in a pot and bring to a boil over high heat, skim off the foam, and simmer over medium-low heat for 80 minutes.
Take out the beef and Korean radish, cut them into bite-sized pieces, and season the broth with soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and salt 1 tsp.
Put cooked rice, beef, and Korean radish in a bowl, pour the hot broth over, and top with green onion and black pepper.
tips: Cool the broth and skim off the fat to make it clear.
It pairs wonderfully with kkakdugi.

nakji-bokkeum.name: Stir-fried Small Octopus (Nakji Bokkeum)
steps: Rub and wash the small octopus with flour or salt, then cut into 5cm pieces. Cut the onion and cabbage into thin strips, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Mix 1 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over high heat, and stir-fry the onion and cabbage for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Add the small octopus and sauce, stir-fry quickly for only 1 minute 30 seconds, and add the green onion.
tips: Cooking the small octopus for too long makes it tough, so stir-fry it briefly over high heat.
It is also good to boil thin noodles and toss them in.

nakji-yeonpo-tang.desc: Refreshing clear soup boiled with Korean radish and small octopus.
nakji-yeonpo-tang.name: Clear Octopus Soup (Nakji Yeonpo-tang)
steps: Wash small octopus by rubbing with flour or salt, and cut Korean radish and Korean zucchini into flat square pieces.
Put water 800ml, kombu, and Korean radish in a pot, boil for 10 minutes, and remove the kombu.
Add Korean zucchini, minced garlic, and soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, and boil for 3 minutes.
Add small octopus, cook briefly for 1 minute and 30 seconds, season with salt 1/3 tsp, and top with green onion.
tips: Small octopus gets tough if cooked too long, so add it at the end.
If there is ink, clean it carefully so it does not burst.

natto-egg-rice.desc: Japanese-style natto egg rice that you mix well.
natto-egg-rice.name: Natto Egg Rice (Natto Gyeran-bap)
steps: Open 1 pack of natto, add the sauce, and stir 20 times with chopsticks until it becomes sticky.
Put cooked rice in a bowl and top with an egg yolk or 1 beaten egg.
Add natto and drizzle with 1 tsp of soy sauce.
Crush roasted seaweed on top and mix well to eat.
tips: The more you stir natto, the more savory flavor comes out.
If you are worried about raw eggs, replace it with a half-cooked fried egg.

natto-kimchi-rice.desc: A hearty rice bowl topped with two fermented foods.
natto-kimchi-rice.name: Natto Kimchi Rice Bowl
steps: Slice thinly kimchi and squeeze out the moisture lightly. Add the sauce to natto and stir 20 times.
Put cooked rice in a bowl and top with kimchi and natto.
Drizzle with 1/2 tsp of sesame oil and crush roasted seaweed on top.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and mix to eat.
tips: If there is a lot of kimchi juice, the cooked rice gets mushy, so squeeze it before topping.
Adding an egg yolk makes it creamier.

nikujaga.desc: Japanese-style braised beef and potatoes with a sweet and savory sauce.
nikujaga.name: Nikujaga
steps: Cut potato and carrot into bite-sized pieces and soak potato in cold water for 5 minutes to remove the starch. Cut onion into 1cm widths, and cut beef into bite-sized pieces.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of cooking oil and stir-fry beef over medium heat for 2 minutes until it changes color, then add onion and stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Add potato and carrot and stir-fry for 1 minute, then pour in 400 ml of water and bring to a boil. Skim off any rising foam.
Add 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of mirin, and 1 tbsp of sugar, cover the lid at an angle, and braise over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat when potato is easily pierced with a chopstick and about 1/3 of the broth remains. Let it sit for 10 minutes so the flavors absorb.
tips: Stirring while braising will break potato. Shake the pot instead.
Serve over rice to make a rice bowl dish.

nokdu-jijim.desc: A thick, Pyeongan-style mung bean pancake loaded with fiddlehead fern and pork.
nokdu-jijim.name: Thick Mung Bean Pancake (Nokdu Jijim)
steps: Soak mung bean for 4 hours, remove the skins, and grind coarsely with 200 ml of water.
Chop pork and fiddlehead fern finely, and slice thinly mung bean sprout and green onion.
Mix the ingredients and 1/2 tsp of salt into the batter.
Pour a generous amount of cooking oil into a pan, spoon the batter thickly, and pan-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side.
tips: The fat from the pork makes it extra savory.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

nongma-guksu.desc: Hamgyeong-do style noodles served with chewy starch noodles in a refreshing broth.
nongma-guksu.name: Hamgyeong-do Nongmaguksu
steps: Boil the beef in 700 ml water for 25 minutes, take it out, shred it, and let the broth cool to season with 1 tbsp soup soy sauce, 1 tbsp vinegar, and sugar.
Boil the glass noodles in boiling water for 7 minutes, rinse in cold water, and drain.
Boil the egg, cut in half, and cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Place glass noodles and toppings in a bowl and pour cold broth.
tips: Rinse the glass noodles by rubbing in cold water for a chewy texture.
Hamgyeong-do locals use noodles made with potato starch.

oatmeal-egg-porridge.desc: A savory oatmeal porridge made without rice.
oatmeal-egg-porridge.name: Oatmeal Egg Porridge (Oatmeal-Gyeran-Juk)
steps: Mince carrot finely and slice thinly green onion.
Put water 250ml, oatmeal 40g, and carrot in a pot and boil over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Beat egg, pour it around, leave it for 30 seconds without stirring, and then stir once.
Season with salt 1/4 tsp and top with green onion and sesame oil 1/2 tsp.
tips: Oatmeal becomes thick like paste if boiled for too long. Adjust to 3~5 minutes to your taste.
It also goes well with shiitake mushrooms or spinach.

oatmeal-milk-bowl.desc: A light breakfast ready in 3 minutes using the microwave.
oatmeal-milk-bowl.name: Oatmeal Milk Bowl (Oatmeal-Uyu-Juk)
steps: Put oatmeal 40g and milk 200ml into a heat-resistant bowl and mix.
Microwave for 2 minutes, take it out, stir once, and microwave for 1 minute more.
Let it sit as is for 1 minute to become thick.
Crush mixed nuts 1 tbsp finely, put them on top, and sprinkle with oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp.
tips: Use a large bowl because it may overflow.
Calories drop further if you use soy milk instead of milk.

oi-bokkeum.name: Stir-fried Cucumbers (Oi-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the cucumber into thick half-moons, marinate in salt 1/2 tsp for 5 minutes, and squeeze out the moisture tightly.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over high heat and stir-fry minced garlic for 10 seconds.
Add the cucumber and quickly stir-fry for only 1 minute 30 seconds.
Add sesame oil and sesame seeds, mix, and take off the heat right away.
tips: Stir-fry quickly over high heat to keep it crunchy.
Squeeze out the moisture thoroughly after marinating so it doesn't get watery.

oi-maesil-muchim.desc: A tangy cucumber salad with the subtle sweetness of green plum syrup.
oi-maesil-muchim.name: Plum Syrup Cucumber Salad (Oi Maesil Muchim)
steps: Rub cucumber with salt, rinse, and cut into 0.5 cm thick diagonal slices.
Sprinkle 1/3 tsp salt, marinate for 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture firmly.
Toss cucumber in a seasoning mixture of 1 tbsp green plum syrup, 1 tbsp vinegar, and 1/2 tsp Korean red pepper flakes.
Sprinkle sesame seeds and chill in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
tips: Green plum syrup varies by brand, so start with 1/2 tbsp and taste.
It is crunchiest when eaten immediately after mixing.

oi-naengguk.desc: A refreshing, tangy chilled cucumber soup for hot days.
oi-naengguk.name: Chilled Cucumber Soup (Oi Naengguk)
steps: Cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Mix soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, and salt 1/2 tsp into cold water 400 ml and dissolve.
Add the cucumber cut into thin strips and float ice cubes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.
tips: Chilling the water beforehand makes it even more refreshing.
Adding soaked dried seaweed makes it chilled seaweed and cucumber soup.

oi-sobagi.desc: Crunchy stuffed cucumber kimchi filled with garlic chives.
oi-sobagi.name: Stuffed Cucumber Kimchi (Oi Sobagi)
steps: Rub and wash cucumber with salt, cut into 5cm lengths, and make deep cross slits in the center.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp of salt, marinate for 30 minutes, and drain the moisture.
Cut garlic chive into 1cm pieces, mince onion, and mix with 3 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of fish sauce, minced garlic, and sugar to make the filling.
Stuff the filling into the cucumber slits, place in a container, leave at room temperature for half a day, and then refrigerate.
tips: Do not pickle the cucumber for more than 30 minutes or it will become mushy.
Eating it right away tastes like fresh geotjeori and has a crunchy texture.

ojingeo-bokkeum.desc: Squid stir-fried over high heat in a sweet and spicy sauce.
ojingeo-bokkeum.name: Stir-fried Squid (Ojingeo-bokkeum)
steps: Split the body of the squid, peel off the inner skin, score it diagonally at 1.5 cm intervals, and cut it into bite-sized pieces. Cut the tentacles into 5 cm lengths.
Cut the onion and cabbage into bite-sized pieces, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Mix 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp minced garlic, and 3 tbsp (45 ml) water to make the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over high heat, stir-fry the onion and cabbage for 1 minute, then add the squid and sauce and stir-fry quickly for 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Add the green onion and 1 tsp sesame oil, mix for 30 seconds, and turn off the heat.
tips: Cooking squid too long makes it tough and releases water. Finish within 3 minutes over high heat.
Scoring helps the sauce absorb well and makes the pieces curl up nicely.

ojingeo-deopbap.desc: A rice bowl topped with spicy stir-fried squid.
ojingeo-deopbap.name: Spicy Squid Rice Bowl (Ojingeo Deopbap)
steps: Score the squid body with a knife and cut into bite-sized pieces, then cut the onion and cabbage into thin strips.
Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, and sugar 1 tsp to make the sauce.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over high heat, sauté the onion and cabbage for 1 minute, then add the squid and sauce and stir-fry for 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Add the green onion and serve over cooked rice.
tips: Stir-fry the squid quickly over high heat to keep it tender and chewy.
If too much liquid forms, turn up the heat to evaporate it.

ojingeo-muguk.desc: A clear soup brewed with refreshing Korean radish and squid.
ojingeo-muguk.name: Squid and Radish Soup (Ojingeo-muguk)
steps: Cut the Korean radish into thin 2 cm rectangular slices, and split the body of the squid to cut it into 1 cm width. Slice the green onion diagonally.
Drizzle 1 tsp sesame oil in a pot, stir-fry the Korean radish over medium heat for 2 minutes, and pour in 700 ml water.
When it comes to a boil, cook over medium heat for 10 minutes to soften the Korean radish.
Add the squid, minced garlic, 1 tbsp soup soy sauce, and 1/3 tsp salt, boil for 3 minutes, add the green onion, and turn off the heat.
tips: Add the squid at the end so it stays tender.
Skim off any foam if the broth looks cloudy.

ojingeo-pajeon.desc: Chewy green onion pancake packed with plenty of squid.
ojingeo-pajeon.name: Squid and Green Onion Pancake (Ojingeo-pajeon)
steps: Cut the green onion into 15cm lengths and chop the squid finely.
Mix 100g of Korean pancake mix and 170ml of water to make a batter, then mix in the squid.
Heat 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, lay down the green onion, and pour the batter over it.
Crack and spread 1 egg on top and cook for 4 minutes. Flip, pour the remaining oil around the edges, and cook for another 4 minutes until crispy.
tips: The batter should be thin so the pancake is thin and crispy.
It pairs well with makgeolli.

ojingeo-sundae.desc: Squid tubes stuffed with a mixture of tofu and vegetables, then steamed.
ojingeo-sundae.name: Stuffed Squid (Ojingeo-sundae)
steps: Clean the squid body and mince the legs. Boil the glass noodles and cut them short.
Mix mashed tofu, glass noodles, minced carrot, onion, and garlic chive, squid legs, egg, 1/2 tsp of salt, sesame oil, and black pepper to make the filling.
Fill the squid body only 70% with the filling and secure the opening with a toothpick.
Steam in a steamer with rising steam for 20 minutes, let it cool, and slice thickly.
tips: Fill it only 70% because packing it tightly will cause it to burst while cooking.
Slice it after cooling so the cross-section looks neat.

ojingeo-twigim.name: Crispy Fried Squid (Ojingeo-twigim)
steps: Cut the squid into 1 cm ring shapes and pat dry with a paper towel.
Mix 5 tbsp Korean pancake mix, 3 tbsp starch, 1/4 tsp salt, and 6 tbsp cold water to make the batter.
Coat the squid in the batter and fry in 170 degree cooking oil for 2 minutes 30 seconds.
Take them out, drain the oil, and serve immediately.
tips: Use cold water to make it extra crispy.
Pat the squid dry so the oil doesn't splatter.

okonomiyaki.desc: A Japanese-style pancake generously packed with cabbage.
okonomiyaki.name: Japanese Savory Pancake (Okonomiyaki)
steps: Cut the cabbage into thin strips and cut the bacon into bite-sized pieces.
In a bowl, mix flour 100g, water 100ml, and 2 egg to make a batter, then stir in the cabbage.
Heat 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, spread the thick batter, top with bacon, cook for 4 minutes, flip, and cook for 4 more minutes.
Mix 2 tbsp of ketchup, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, and 1 tsp of sugar, spread it on top, and drizzle with mayonnaise.
tips: Cook it thick and cover with a lid so the inside cooks through.
Topping with bonito flakes makes it even more authentic.

oksusu-sujebi.desc: Gangwon-style sujebi made with corn and potato.
oksusu-sujebi.name: Corn Hand-pulled Dough Soup (Oksusu Sujebi)
steps: Add 4 tbsp (60ml) of water to 1 cup of flour to make a firm dough, and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Boil anchovy in 1 L of water for 8 minutes, remove them, add potato, and boil for 5 minutes.
Tear the dough thinly into the pot and boil for 6 minutes along with corn and Korean zucchini.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce and 1/3 tsp of salt.
tips: The sweetness of the corn seeps into the broth, making it pleasantly sweet.
Tear the dough thinly so it becomes chewy.

olgaengi-guk.desc: A savory, comforting soup made with marsh snails and garlic chives in a doenjang broth.
olgaengi-guk.name: Marsh Snail Soup (Olgaengi-guk)
steps: Soak and wash the marsh snail in salted water, slice the garlic chive into 3cm pieces, and slice the green onion thinly.
In a pot, dissolve water 800 ml, doenjang 2 tbsp, and gochujang 1/2 tbsp, then bring to a boil.
When it starts to boil, add the marsh snail and minced garlic, and boil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic chive, green onion, and perilla seed powder, and boil for 2 more minutes.
tips: Soak the marsh snail thoroughly so no grit is felt when chewing.
Adding mallow leaves makes it even more savory.

olgaengi-muchim.desc: Marsh snails tossed in a sweet and sour chogochujang dressing.
olgaengi-muchim.name: Marsh Snail Salad (Olgaengi-muchim)
steps: Soak and boil the marsh snail to remove the meat, cut the onion and cucumber into thin strips, and cut the water dropwort into 4cm pieces.
Mix gochujang 2 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, and sugar 1 tbsp to make the seasoning sauce.
Toss the marsh snail and vegetables in the seasoning sauce.
Sprinkle sesame seeds on top and serve.
tips: Tossing right before eating prevents excess water from forming.
It is also great mixed with noodles.

olgaengi-sujebi.desc: Hand-pulled dough soup simmered in a rich marsh snail broth.
olgaengi-sujebi.name: Marsh Snail Hand-Pulled Dough Soup (Olgaengi Sujebi)
steps: Combine flour 1 cup with water 4 tbsp (60 ml) to make a firm dough, and let it rest for 30 minutes.
In a pot, dissolve water 800 ml and doenjang 1 tbsp, then add the potato, marsh snail, and minced garlic, and boil for 10 minutes.
Tear the dough thinly into the pot and boil with the Korean zucchini for 6 minutes.
Season with soup soy sauce 1 tbsp and top with the garlic chive.
tips: Tear the dough thinly so it is chewy.
The longer the resting time, the more elastic the dough becomes.

olive-tomato-pasta.name: Olive Tomato Pasta
steps: Boil spaghetti in 1.5L of boiling water with 1 tsp salt for 8 minutes and reserve 1/2 cup (100 ml) of water.
Slice black olive thinly and dice tomato.
Stir-fry 2 tbsp olive oil and minced garlic in a pan over low heat for 1 minute, then add tomato and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add pasta sauce, 3 tbsp water, spaghetti, and black olive, and toss for 2 minutes.
tips: Since black olive is salty, adjust the salt at the end.
Adding bacon also goes well with it.

omegi-tteok.desc: Chewy Jeju omegi rice cakes coated in red bean paste.
omegi-tteok.name: Jeju Omegi Rice Cake (Omegi-tteok)
steps: Soak the glutinous rice for 3 hours, blend it finely in a blender with 150ml of water, and mix in 1/3 tsp of salt.
Place the dough in a heat-resistant container, microwave for 3 minutes, mix, and microwave for another 2 minutes to cook through.
Mash the red bean and mix it with 2 tbsp of sugar to make red bean paste.
Divide the cooked dough into bite-sized pieces and coat them with red bean paste.
tips: Shape the dough while it is hot so it stretches well.
Applying cooking oil to your hands prevents sticking.

omelet.desc: An omelet filled with cheese and ham inside moist eggs.
omelet.name: Cheese Omelet
steps: Finely mince onion and ham into 0.5 cm pieces.
In a bowl, add 3 egg, 2 tbsp milk, 1/4 tsp salt, and black pepper, and beat until no whites are visible.
Melt 1/2 tbsp butter in a pan heated over medium heat, stir-fry onion and ham for 1 minute, and remove.
Lower the heat to low and pour the egg mixture into the pan. When the edges are set, stir the center 2-3 times with chopsticks.
When the surface is half cooked, place cheese and the stir-fried ingredients on one side and fold in half. Cook for 30 seconds more and place on a plate.
tips: If the heat is too high, only the outside cooks. Cook slowly over low heat.
Adding milk makes it even softer.

omurice.desc: Ketchup fried rice wrapped in a fluffy, soft egg omelet.
omurice.name: Omurice
steps: Finely mince the onion, carrot, and ham into 5mm pieces. Crack 3 eggs, add milk 2 tbsp and a pinch of salt, whisk well, and strain through a sieve once.

Heat cooking oil 1/2 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, and stir-fry the onion, carrot, and ham for 2 minutes. Add cooked rice and ketchup 1 tbsp, stir-fry for 2 more minutes, transfer to a plate, and shape into a rugby ball.
Wipe the pan clean, add cooking oil 1 tbsp, and lower the heat to low. Pour in the egg mixture, and once the edges begin to set, vigorously stir the center with chopsticks to make it soft-boiled.
When the surface is half-cooked and still moist, turn off the heat and drape the egg over the fried rice.
Drizzle the remaining ketchup 1 tbsp in a zigzag pattern to finish.
tips: Remove the egg from the heat before it fully sets to keep it tender.
You don't need to add salt to the rice as the seasoning from the ketchup and ham is plenty.

onepan-beef-curry.desc: Beef curry stirred and simmered in a single pan.
onepan-beef-curry.name: One-Pan Beef Curry
steps: Cut the onion, potato, and carrot into 2cm pieces. Dissolve the curry powder in 100ml of water.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a deep pan, and sauté the beef and onion over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot, sauté for 1 minute, pour in 400ml of water, bring to a boil, and simmer over low heat for 12 minutes.
Add the dissolved curry and simmer for 5 minutes while stirring.
Place the cooked rice in a bowl and top with the curry.
tips: Add the curry at the end so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Blending and adding an apple gives it a sweet flavor.

onepan-bulgogi-japchae.desc: Glass noodles cooked directly in broth with bulgogi without soaking beforehand.
onepan-bulgogi-japchae.name: One-Pan Bulgogi Glass Noodles (One-Pan Bulgogi Japchae)
steps: Mix beef with soy sauce 1 tbsp, sugar 1/2 tbsp, minced garlic, and black pepper, then marinate for 10 minutes. Cut onion and carrot into thin strips, and slice green onion diagonally.
Coat a wide pan with sesame oil 1 tbsp and stir-fry beef over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add water 400 ml, the remaining soy sauce 2 tbsp, and sugar 1/2 tbsp, and when it comes to a boil, add onion, carrot, and glass noodles.
Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes while stirring until glass noodles look translucent and the broth is almost reduced.
Add green onion, mix for 1 minute, and turn off the heat.
tips: Glass noodles tend to stick to the bottom, so stir frequently for the first 3 minutes.
Dry glass noodles will cook while absorbing the broth even without soaking.

onepan-chicken-cream-risotto.desc: Cream risotto made entirely in one pan.
onepan-chicken-cream-risotto.name: One-Pan Chicken Breast Cream Risotto
steps: Cut the chicken breast into 1.5cm pieces, season with 1/3 tsp of salt and black pepper, and mince the onion.
Melt 1 tbsp of butter in a pan, sauté the chicken breast for 3 minutes, add the onion, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add 350ml of milk and cooked rice, and simmer over low heat for 8 minutes while stirring.
Add the cheese to melt and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: Milk can curdle over high heat, so be sure to keep it on low heat.
Adding mushrooms enhances the flavor.

onepan-chicken-rice.desc: Soy sauce rice cooked together with chicken breast from uncooked rice in a single pan.
onepan-chicken-rice.name: One-Pan Chicken Soy Sauce Rice
steps: Wash the uncooked rice, soak for 20 minutes, and drain in a colander. Cut the chicken breast into 1.5cm pieces, and cut the carrot and onion into small pieces.
In a thick-bottomed pan with a lid, combine the uncooked rice, chicken breast, carrot, onion, 2tbsp soy sauce, and 230ml water, and mix.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low heat, cover with a lid, and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat, let steam for 10 minutes, then add 1tsp sesame oil and mix.
tips: You must soak the uncooked rice so the water amount is correct.
Cook without opening the lid so the rice does not turn out undercooked.

onepan-cream-pasta.desc: One-pan cream pasta made with milk instead of heavy cream.
onepan-cream-pasta.name: One-Pan Milk Cream Pasta (On-paen Uyu Keurim Pasta)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips, bacon into 1cm width, and break the spaghetti in half.
Stir-fry bacon in a dry pan on medium heat for 2 minutes to render fat, then add onion and minced garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour 400 ml of milk, 200 ml of water, and 1/3 tsp of salt, and add spaghetti just before it comes to a boil.
Boil on low heat, stirring frequently, for 12 minutes. Milk overflows on high heat, so reduce the heat.
Tear and add cheese to melt, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: Stir frequently as the spaghetti cooks while absorbing the milk.
If the consistency is too thick, add 50 ml of milk or water.

onepan-curry-udon.desc: A simple one-bowl dish where udon noodles are boiled directly in curry broth.
onepan-curry-udon.name: One-Pan Curry Udon
steps: Cut onion into thin strips, slice green onion diagonally, and cut pork into bite-sized pieces. Dissolve curry powder in water 100 ml without any lumps.
Coat a pot with cooking oil 1 tsp and stir-fry pork and onion over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour water 600 ml, bring to a boil, add the dissolved curry, and boil for 3 minutes.
Add udon noodle and boil for 3 minutes, then top with green onion and turn off the heat.
tips: Adding curry all at once can cause lumps, so dissolve it in advance.
Adding 1 egg and mixing it in makes it creamy.

onepan-egg-cheese-sandwich.desc: A breakfast where egg and bread are toasted together in a single frying pan.
onepan-egg-cheese-sandwich.name: One-Pan Egg Cheese Sandwich
steps: Grease the pan with 1tsp cooking oil and preheat over low heat.
Place two slices of sandwich bread side by side, toast for 1 minute, and crack 2 eggs on one side to make fried eggs.
Place cheese, ham, and egg on one slice of sandwich bread, sprinkle with black pepper, and cover with the other slice of sandwich bread.
Press down while toasting for 1 minute on each side, then cut in half.
tips: Keep the heat low so the egg yolks do not burst.
You can also add tomatoes or lettuce.

onepan-egg-tomato-stew.desc: A brunch dish made by poaching eggs in tomato sauce.
onepan-egg-tomato-stew.name: One-Pan Egg and Tomato Stew (One-Pan Egg Tomato Stew)
steps: Dice the tomato and mince the onion.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan, stir-fry the onion for 1 minute and the tomato for 3 minutes, then add the pasta sauce and 1/4 tsp of salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Make 3 wells with a spoon and crack the eggs into them one by one.
Cover with a lid, cook over low heat for 5 minutes, and top with cheese and black pepper.
tips: Cook for only 4 minutes if you want runny yolks.
It is delicious to dip bread into it.

onepan-eomuk-udon-bokkeum.desc: Soy sauce stir-fried udon noodles with fish cake and cabbage.
onepan-eomuk-udon-bokkeum.name: One-Pan Stir-Fried Udon with Fish Cake (One-pan Eomuk Udon Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the fish cake into bite-sized pieces, and cut the cabbage and onion into thin strips. Blanch the udon noodle in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over high heat, and stir-fry the cabbage, onion, and fish cake for 2 minutes.
Add the udon noodle, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce, and 2 tbsp of water, then stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: If the noodles stick together, add 1 tbsp of water at a time.
Topping it with a fried egg makes it filling.

onepan-haemul-bokkeumbap.desc: One-pan seafood fried rice loaded with shrimp and squid.
onepan-haemul-bokkeumbap.name: One-Pan Seafood Fried Rice (One-Pan Haemul Bokkeumbap)
steps: Cut the shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces and slice the green onion thinly.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over high heat and stir-fry the green onion, shrimp, and squid for 2 minutes.
Push them to one side, beat the egg, and make scrambled eggs.
Add the cooked rice, 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
tips: Seafood must be stir-fried quickly over high heat so it doesn't get tough.
If moisture forms, evaporate it over high heat.

onepan-ham-potato-bokkeum.desc: A kid-friendly side dish made by stir-frying ham and potatoes with ketchup.
onepan-ham-potato-bokkeum.name: One-Pan Ham and Potato Stir-Fry (One-Pan Ham Potato Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the potato into 1 cm thick sticks, cut the onion into thin strips, and cut the ham into bite-sized pieces.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat and stir-fry the potato for 5 minutes.
Add 3 tbsp of water, cover with a lid, and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the ham, onion, and 1/4 tsp of salt, stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add 2 tbsp of ketchup and toss for 1 minute.
tips: You must add water and cover with a lid so the potato cooks through to the center.
Children love it when cheese is added on top.

onepan-kimchi-pork-rice.desc: A one-pan rice dish where kimchi and pork are stir-fried, then rice is mixed right in.
onepan-kimchi-pork-rice.name: One-Pan Kimchi Pork Fried Rice
steps: Cut the kimchi into small pieces, cut the pork into bite-sized pieces, and slice thinly the green onion.
In a pan heated over high heat, drizzle 1tbsp cooking oil and stir-fry the green onion and pork for 3 minutes.
Add the kimchi and Korean red pepper flakes and stir-fry for 3 minutes to cook off the sourness.
Add the cooked rice, press down while stir-frying for 3 minutes, then drizzle with sesame oil and sesame seeds to finish.
tips: Stir-frying the kimchi thoroughly brings out the umami flavor.
Top with a fried egg to reduce the spiciness.

onepan-sausage-potato.desc: A great drinking snack with potatoes and sausages pan-fried until golden in a single pan.
onepan-sausage-potato.name: One-Pan Sausage and Potato Stir-Fry
steps: Cut potato into bite-sized pieces and microwave for 3 minutes to cook them halfway. Make diagonal cuts on sausage. Cut onion into thick pieces.
Heat a pan over medium heat, coat with cooking oil 1 tbsp, add potato, and pan-fry for 5 minutes until golden.
Add sausage and onion, cook for 4 more minutes, and sprinkle with salt 1/4 tsp and black pepper.
Transfer to a plate and serve with ketchup 2 tbsp on the side.
tips: Pre-cooking potatoes prevents only the outsides from burning.
Adding cheese and covering with a lid makes it cheesy sausage and potato.

onepan-sausage-veg-rice.desc: Fried rice finished in just 5 minutes with a single pan.
onepan-sausage-veg-rice.name: One-Pan Sausage and Vegetable Fried Rice (On-paen Sosiji Yachae Bokkeumbap)
steps: Finely dice sausage, onion, and carrot into 0.7cm sizes.
In a pan heated over high heat, coat with 1 tbsp of cooking oil and stir-fry carrot, onion, and sausage for 2 minutes.
Push to one side, crack egg, and make scrambled eggs.
Add cooked rice, 2 tbsp of ketchup, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 3 minutes while pressing so the rice grains separate.
tips: Strying the ketchup at the edge first removes the sour taste and makes it delicious.
Children love it when cheese is added and melted on top.

onepan-shrimp-garlic-pasta.desc: A one-pan oil pasta packed with the aroma of shrimp and garlic.
onepan-shrimp-garlic-pasta.name: One-Pan Shrimp Garlic Pasta
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and season with 1/4tsp salt and black pepper. Slice thinly the Cheongyang chili.
In a 28cm pan, add 2tbsp olive oil and minced garlic, and stir-fry over low heat for 2 minutes to release the aroma.
Pour in 450ml water and the remaining 1/4tsp salt. Once boiling, add the spaghetti broken in half, and boil for 8 minutes while stirring frequently.
When the liquid is almost reduced, place the shrimp and Cheongyang chili on top, cover with a lid, and cook for 3 minutes.
Mix well and transfer to a plate.
tips: If the liquid reduces and the spaghetti sticks to the pan, add 50ml more water.
Add the shrimp at the end so they do not become tough.

onepan-soy-chicken-potato.desc: A side dish made by simmering chicken and potato in one pan.
onepan-soy-chicken-potato.name: One-Pan Soy Sauce Chicken and Potato Stew (On-paen Ganjang Dak Gamjajorim)
steps: Cut the potato into large pieces, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, drain, and cut the onion into large pieces. Blanch chicken in boiling water for 2 minutes and wash.
In a wide pan, place chicken, potato, and onion, and pour 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of oligosaccharide syrup, minced garlic, black pepper, and 250 ml of water.
When it boils on high heat, reduce to medium-low heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Open the lid, baste with the broth, and simmer for another 10 minutes until glossy, then turn off the heat.
tips: Removing the chicken skin reduces fat.
Adding 1 Cheongyang pepper makes it spicy.

onepan-spam-kimchi-bap.desc: A hearty rice bowl topped with Spam and kimchi stir-fried in a single pan.
onepan-spam-kimchi-bap.name: One-Pan Spam Kimchi Rice Bowl (One-Pan Spam Kimchi Bap)
steps: Cut Spam into 1 cm cubes, chop kimchi finely, and slice green onion thinly.
Heat a pan over medium heat, coat with cooking oil 1 tsp, and sear Spam for 2 minutes until the outer surfaces are golden brown.
Add kimchi and green onion, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Crack egg on one side to make a fried egg after 1 minute and 30 seconds, put cooked rice in a bowl, top with everything, and drizzle with sesame oil.
tips: If kimchi is sour, add sugar 1/2 tsp to balance the flavor.
Since Spam is salty, do not add kimchi juice.

onepan-tofu-kimchi-jorim.desc: A spicy and savory braised dish of tofu and kimchi cooked together in one pan.
onepan-tofu-kimchi-jorim.name: One-Pan Tofu and Kimchi Stew (One-Pan Tofu Kimchi Jorim)
steps: Cut the tofu into 1.5 cm thick slices and cut the kimchi into bite-sized pieces. Cut the pork into bite-sized pieces, and slice the green onion thinly at an angle.
Put the pork, kimchi, Korean red pepper flakes, and 1 tsp of sugar into a pan and stir-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour 150 ml of water, place the tofu on top, cover with a lid, and braise for 10 minutes.
Put the green onion on top, drizzle 1 tsp of sesame oil, and braise for 2 more minutes.
tips: Do not stir as the tofu will break; instead, spoon the broth over it.
If the kimchi is too sour, add a little more sugar.

onepan-tomato-egg-rice.desc: A soft risotto made by simmering tomatoes, cooked rice, and eggs.
onepan-tomato-egg-rice.name: One-Pan Tomato Egg Risotto
steps: Cut tomato into dice and mince onion finely.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 1 tsp, stir-fry onion for 1 minute and tomato for 3 minutes, then mash them.
Add water 300 ml, cooked rice, and salt 1/3 tsp, and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes while stirring.
Beat egg and pour it around the edge, and after 1 minute tear cheese and place it on top.
Once cheese melts, sprinkle black pepper to finish.
tips: You must stir-fry tomatoes thoroughly to reduce the sour taste.
Adding egg at the end and keeping it soft-boiled makes it tender.

onepan-tomato-pasta.desc: Pasta boiled together with sauce in one pan without boiling noodles separately.
onepan-tomato-pasta.name: One-Pan Tomato Pasta (On-paen Tomato Pasta)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips and bacon into 1cm width. Break the spaghetti in half.
In a 28cm wide deep pan, coat with 1 tsp of cooking oil and stir-fry minced garlic, onion, and bacon on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add 500 ml of water, 200 g of pasta sauce, and 1/4 tsp of salt. When it boils, add spaghetti.
Boil on medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently with tongs so the spaghetti absorbs the sauce. If water is short, add 50 ml more.
When the broth reduces slightly and spaghetti is cooked properly, sprinkle with black pepper and turn off the heat.
tips: Stir continuously for the first 2 minutes so the spaghetti does not stick to the bottom of the pan.
Boiling time for the spaghetti may take 1~2 minutes longer than indicated on the package.

onigiri-tuna-mayo.desc: Japanese-style rice balls shaped into triangles.
onigiri-tuna-mayo.name: Tuna Mayo Onigiri
steps: Drain the oil from canned tuna and mix with 1 tbsp of mayonnaise.
Mix 1/4 tsp of salt into cooked rice and divide in half.
Wet your hands with water, make a hollow in the center of cooked rice, add canned tuna, and shape into a triangle.
Wrap with roasted seaweed.
tips: Wetting your hands with saltwater prevents cooked rice from sticking and seasons it.
Don't squeeze too hard or it will become firm.

oori-baeksuk.desc: Nourishing duck soup slowly boiled with glutinous rice and potatoes.
oori-baeksuk.name: Duck Baeksuk (Oori Baeksuk)
steps: Blanch the duck pieces in boiling water for 3 minutes and wash away the foam and fat. Wash the glutinous rice and soak it for 30 minutes.

In a large pot, add the duck, water 2L, half a green onion, and ginger, and boil over high heat. When it comes to a boil, reduce to medium heat and simmer for 30 minutes while skimming off foam and fat.

Cut the potato into large chunks and add it along with minced garlic and the soaked glutinous rice, simmering over low heat for 25 more minutes. Stir occasionally so the glutinous rice does not stick to the bottom.
Check that the meat easily falls off the bone and is cooked longer than chicken, then top with sliced green onion and black pepper.
Serve with salt 1 tsp on the side for dipping.
tips: The more you skim off the duck fat, the cleaner the broth tastes.
You can also add rice or kalguksu noodles into the leftover broth to eat.

oori-bokkeumtang.desc: A spicy braised duck stew simmered with potato.
oori-bokkeumtang.name: Spicy Braised Duck Stew (Oori Bokkeumtang)
steps: Blanch the duck pieces in boiling water for 3 minutes to wash away fat and foam. Cut the potato and onion into bite-sized chunks.
Place the duck, water 600ml, potato, and onion in a pot and bring to a boil.

Dissolve Korean red pepper flakes 3 tbsp, gochujang 1 tbsp, soy sauce 3 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and ginger into the pot, and simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes. Skim off any rising fat.
Add the green onion and simmer for 5 more minutes until the sauce is reduced and thick.
tips: Blanching helps reduce the gamey flavor of the duck.
Adding sujebi dough or perilla leaf goes very well with it.

oori-bulgogi.desc: Duck marinated in a sweet and spicy sauce and stir-fried over high heat.
oori-bulgogi.name: Duck Bulgogi (Oori Bulgogi)
steps: Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, soy sauce 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic 1 tbsp, mirin 1 tbsp, and black pepper to make a sauce.

Wipe the blood off the duck with a paper towel, mix it with the sauce, and marinate for 20 minutes. Cut the onion into thin strips, cut the green onion diagonally, and cut the garlic chive into 5 cm lengths.
Heat a pan without oil over high heat, spread out the duck, and stir-fry for 3 minutes. Since oil comes out from the duck, no separate oil is needed.
Add the onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then wipe away the released oil with a paper towel.
Add the garlic chive, green onion, and sesame oil 1 tsp, stir-fry for 30 more seconds, and turn off the heat. Check that the inside of the duck is cooked through without any pink color.
tips: Duck renders a lot of fat from its skin. Wiping it off halfway through makes it less greasy.
It is even better wrapped in leaf lettuce or perilla leaf.

oori-deulkkae-tang.desc: A rich soup where the nutty flavor of perilla seed powder masks any gamey duck smell.
oori-deulkkae-tang.name: Duck Perilla Soup (Oori Deulkkae Tang)
steps: Blanch the duck in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse. Cut the Korean radish into bite-sized flat pieces and slice thinly the green onion.
Add 1 tbsp of perilla oil to a pot, sauté the Korean radish over medium heat for 3 minutes, then pour in the duck and 1.2 L of water.
When it comes to a boil, cook over medium-low heat for 35 minutes while skimming off foam and oil.
Add 3 tbsp of perilla seed powder, minced garlic, 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, and 1/2 tsp of salt, then simmer for 10 more minutes.
Add the green onion and black pepper, cook for 2 minutes, and turn off the heat.
tips: Add the perilla seed powder at the end to prevent it from tasting bitter.
If there is too much duck oil, let it cool and skim off the solidified fat.

oori-rosugui.desc: A grilled dish that highlights the natural flavor of duck seasoned only with salt and black pepper.
oori-rosugui.name: Pan-Seared Duck (Oori Rosugui)
steps: Pat the duck dry with a paper towel and season with salt 1/2 tsp and black pepper. Cut the onion into thin strips.
Heat a pan without oil over medium heat, place the duck skin-side down, and cook for 4 minutes.
Flip the duck and cook for 3 more minutes while wiping away the rendered fat with a paper towel.
Add the onion to grill alongside and wrap the meat in a perilla leaf with ssamjang.
tips: Duck produces a lot of fat, so wipe it away midway.
Make sure it is cooked through to the center.

oyakodon.desc: Japanese-style rice bowl topped with tender chicken and soft-scrambled egg.
oyakodon.name: Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl (Oyakodon)
steps: Cut the chicken into 2 cm pieces and cut the onion into 0.5 cm thick strips. Lightly beat 3 egg just until the whites are loosened.
In a small pan, combine 150 ml of water, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, and 1 tbsp sugar and bring to a boil.
When the broth boils, add the onion and chicken and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Pour in 2/3 of the beaten egg, cover with a lid, and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the remaining egg, turn off the heat, cover, and let steam for 20 seconds. A soft-set state is the most delicious.
Serve over cooked rice and top with green onion.
tips: Adding the egg in two stages creates both set layers and soft, fluffy layers.
Chicken thigh is more tender than chicken breast.

parae-jeon.desc: Crispy green laver pancake with a gorgeous green color.
parae-jeon.name: Green Laver Pancake (Parae Jeon)
steps: Wash the green laver in cold water, squeeze out the water, and chop finely with scissors.
In a bowl, mix the green laver, 3 tbsp of Korean pancake mix, 1 egg, 1/4 tsp of salt, and 4 tbsp (60ml) of water to make a batter.
Drizzle 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan heated over medium heat, and spread the batter thinly with a spoon.
Pan-fry until crispy for 2 minutes and 30 seconds on each side.
tips: If there is too much water in the batter, it will be soggy. Measure carefully.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce made of 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of vinegar.

parae-muchim.desc: Sweet and sour seasoned green laver with a fragrant ocean scent.
parae-muchim.name: Seasoned Green Laver (Parae Muchim)
steps: Rinse the green laver in cold water by shaking it several times to remove impurities, drain in a colander, and squeeze out the water.
Cut it with scissors into bite-sized pieces.
Add the green laver to the sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of vinegar, 1/2 tbsp of sugar, 1 tsp of soy sauce, and minced garlic, and toss well.
Finish by adding 1 tsp of sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Soaking the green laver in water for too long will make it lose its aroma.
Cut radish into thin strips and toss them together for a crunchy texture.

patjuk.desc: Winter solstice red bean porridge with glutinous rice rice balls.
patjuk.name: Red Bean Porridge (Patjuk)
steps: Wash the red bean, boil in water 1 L, discard the first water, pour water 1.5 L again, and boil thoroughly for 50 minutes.
Mash the boiled red bean, strain through a sieve, and discard the skins.
Knead glutinous rice 3/4 cup with water 4 tbsp to shape rice balls, and put the remaining glutinous rice into the red bean water to boil.
Add the rice balls, boil for 5 more minutes until they float, and season with salt 1 tsp and sugar.
tips: Discarding the first red bean water removes the bitter taste.
People can add sugar individually to taste.

pickle-tuna-salad.desc: Refreshing tuna salad made with pickled cucumber.
pickle-tuna-salad.name: Pickle Tuna Salad
steps: Drain the oil from canned tuna. Finely mince pickled cucumber and tear iceberg lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Mix canned tuna with pickled cucumber, 1 tbsp mayonnaise, and black pepper.
Place iceberg lettuce on a plate and top with tuna salad.
Eat immediately or serve with bread.
tips: Adding a spoonful of pickled cucumber juice makes it refreshing.
It is also great as an open-faced sandwich on bread.

pohang-gwamegi.desc: Semi-dried saury wrapped in roasted seaweed and water dropwort.
pohang-gwamegi.name: Pohang Gwamegi Wrap
steps: Peel the skin of the semi-dried saury and cut it into bite-sized pieces. Wash the water dropwort and cut it to 5cm.
Cut the Cheongyang chili diagonally.
Mix minced garlic with 3 tbsp of ssamjang.
Place water dropwort, semi-dried saury, ssamjang, and chili on top of roasted seaweed and wrap to eat.
tips: If you are worried about the fishy taste, wrap it together with kimchi.
It is also good to dip in red chili paste with vinegar.

pohang-mori-guksu.desc: Spicy and hearty Pohang-style noodle soup with seafood and knife-cut noodles.
pohang-mori-guksu.name: Pohang Mori Guksu
steps: Cut potato into half-moons and slice squid and shrimp into bite-sized pieces.
In a pot, put 900 ml of water, potato, 2 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, and 1 tbsp of minced garlic, and boil for 10 minutes.
Shake off excess flour from knife-cut wheat noodles and cook for 5 minutes, then add seafood and soybean sprout and cook for 4 more minutes.
Season with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce and top with green onion.
tips: The potato breaks down, making the broth thick and rich.
Boiling and rinsing the noodles once beforehand makes the broth clean.

pohang-ojingeo-mulhoe.desc: Refreshing and sweet-sour cold soup with blanched squid.
pohang-ojingeo-mulhoe.name: Pohang-style Cold Raw Squid Soup (Pohang Ojingeo Mulhoe)
steps: Blanch squid, cut into bite-sized pieces, and cut cucumber, onion, and Korean pear into thin strips.
Mix 3 tbsp of gochujang, 3 tbsp of vinegar, 2 tbsp of sugar, and minced garlic to make the sauce.
Place vegetables and squid in a bowl and put the sauce on top.
Right before eating, pour 300 ml of ice water and sprinkle sesame seeds.
tips: Using blanched squid instead of raw fish lets you enjoy it safely.
Mixing in noodles or cooked rice makes it a complete meal.

pork-doenjang-gui.desc: Pork marinated in doenjang and grilled.
pork-doenjang-gui.name: Grilled Pork with Doenjang (Doenjang-gui)
steps: Mix doenjang 1 tbsp, mirin 1 tbsp, minced garlic, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, and sesame oil 1 tsp to make the marinade.
Coat the pork with the marinade and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a heated pan and cook completely over medium heat for 6 minutes on each side.
Cut into bite-sized pieces.
tips: The doenjang marinade burns easily, so grill slowly over medium-low heat.
It is great wrapped in lettuce wraps.

pork-gochujang-jjigae.desc: A savory gochujang stew loaded with potato and pork.
pork-gochujang-jjigae.name: Spicy Pork Gochujang Stew (Pork Gochujang Jjigae)
steps: Cut potato, onion, Korean zucchini, and tofu into bite-sized pieces. Cut pork into bite-sized pieces.
Place pork, potato, and 600 ml of water in a pot and boil.
Dissolve 2 tbsp of gochujang, Korean red pepper flakes, and minced garlic, then boil for 10 minutes.
Add onion, Korean zucchini, and tofu, boil for 7 minutes, and top with green onion.
tips: Stir-frying the meat first deepens the flavor.
The key is letting the potato break down to make the broth thick.

pork-jangjorim.name: Soy-Braised Pork (Pork Jangjorim)
steps: Cut the pork into large chunks and boil it in boiling water with the green onion for 20 minutes. Boil the egg for 10 minutes and peel the shell.
Put 400ml of the boiling water, 4 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, and 2 tbsp of mirin into a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the meat and egg, and simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes.
Take out the meat, tear it along the grain, and submerge it back into the broth.
tips: Making slashes on the egg helps the seasoning absorb well.
Let it cool and store it together with the broth.

pork-kimchi-stir-fry.desc: The sweet and salty combination of kimchi and pork.
pork-kimchi-stir-fry.name: Pork and Kimchi Stir-Fry (Dwaeji-gimchi-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the kimchi into 4cm lengths, cut the onion into thin strips, and slice thinly the green onion.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan heated over high heat, and stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes to sear the outside.
Add the kimchi, onion, and 1/2 tbsp of sugar, and stir-fry over medium heat for 7~8 minutes until the kimchi wilts and looks glossy.
Add the green onion and stir-fry for 1 minute, then finish with sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Adjust the amount of sugar in 1 tsp (4g) increments depending on how sour your kimchi is.
Pan-fry some tofu and serve it on the side to make tofu kimchi.

pork-saenggang-gui.desc: A sweet and savory Japanese-style pork stir-fry with a rich ginger aroma.
pork-saenggang-gui.name: Pork and Ginger Stir-Fry (Pork Saenggang-gui)
steps: Finely grate or mince the ginger. Cut the onion into thin strips 1 cm wide.
Mix soy sauce 2 tbsp, mirin 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tsp, and ginger to make the sauce.
Cut the pork into bite-sized pieces, sprinkle with black pepper, and marinate in half of the sauce for 10 minutes.
Heat a pan over high heat, add cooking oil 1 tbsp, stir-fry the onion for 1 minute, add the pork to stir-fry for 2 minutes, and pour in the remaining sauce to reduce for 1 minute.
tips: Marinating the meat for too long can make it tough. 10 minutes is enough.
Serving it with sliced cabbage makes it a complete meal.

pork-sangchu-ssam.desc: A table spread of grilled pork belly served with ssamjang, perilla leaf, and leaf lettuce.
pork-sangchu-ssam.name: Grilled Pork Belly Lettuce Wraps (Samgyeopsal Sangchu Ssam)
steps: Wash leaf lettuce and perilla leaf, drain them in a strainer, and remove the water. Cut pork into 1cm thick slices and sprinkle with salt 1/2tsp and black pepper.
In a pan heated over medium heat, coat with cooking oil 1tsp, place pork, and grill for 4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Wipe away the rendered fat with a paper towel while grilling to make it crispy.
Mix minced garlic into ssamjang 2tbsp, and wrap leaf lettuce with perilla leaf, pork, and ssamjang.
tips: On high heat, only the outside burns. Grill slowly over medium heat.
Check that the cooked inside meat has no pink color left.

potato-cheese-bake.desc: A dish made by topping microwave-cooked potatoes with cheese and baking them.
potato-cheese-bake.name: Baked Cheesy Potatoes (Potato Cheese Bake)
steps: Peel the potato, cut it into 1 cm thick rounds, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, and pat dry.
Spread the potato on a plate, cover with plastic wrap, and microwave at 700W for 4 minutes to cook through. It's done when a chopstick goes through easily.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, pan-fry the potato for 2 minutes on each side until golden, and sprinkle with salt 1/3 tsp and black pepper.
Top the potato with cheese, cover the pan with a lid, and melt over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve with ketchup.
tips: Cooking in the microwave beforehand helps it brown quickly in the pan.
Adding bacon bits makes it more hearty.

potato-cheese-ball.desc: Crispy on the outside with gooey cheese on the inside potato balls.
potato-cheese-ball.name: Cheese Potato Balls (Cheese Gamja Ball)
steps: Boil the potato, peel the skin, mash while hot, and mix with salt 1/2 tsp.
Cut the cheese into small pieces, wrap it with the mashed potato, and shape into balls.
Coat them in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs in that order.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 3 tbsp and fry over medium heat for 5 minutes, rolling them until golden brown.
tips: Wrap them tightly without gaps so the cheese doesn't leak out.
An air fryer at 180°C for 10 minutes works too.

potato-cream-soup.desc: A smooth cream soup made by blending potatoes.
potato-cream-soup.name: Potato Cream Soup (Gamja Cream Soup)
steps: Slice thinly potato and onion, and stir-fry them in 1 tbsp of butter over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour 300 ml of water, and when it starts to boil, simmer thoroughly over low heat for 15 minutes.
Blend smoothly with a mixer or hand blender, and pour it back into the pot.
Add 300 ml of milk, boil over low heat for 5 minutes, and season with 1/2 tsp of salt and black pepper.
tips: Keep the heat low after adding milk so it doesn't boil over.
It tastes great with toasted breadcrumbs sprinkled on top.

potato-gochujang-jjigae.desc: A spicy gochujang stew with tender, mealy potatoes.
potato-gochujang-jjigae.name: Potato Gochujang Stew (Potato Gochujang Jjigae)
steps: Cut the potato into thick half-moon shapes, and cut the Korean zucchini, onion, and tofu into bite-sized pieces.
Pour water 500 ml into a pot, dissolve gochujang 2 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes, and minced garlic, and bring to a boil.
Add the potato and onion and boil for 10 minutes.
Add the Korean zucchini and tofu, boil for another 7 minutes, and then top with the green onion.
tips: Cook the potato until a chopstick goes through smoothly.
Using anchovy broth makes it much richer.

potato-gratin.desc: A gratin baked in the oven with potatoes, milk, and cheese.
potato-gratin.name: Potato Cheese Gratin (Gamja Cheese Gratin)
steps: Slice potato thinly to 0.3 cm thickness, cut onion into thin strips, and cut bacon into bite-sized pieces.
Grease a heat-resistant dish with butter, and layer potato, onion, and bacon in it.
Mix 1/3 tsp of salt and black pepper into 200 ml of milk, pour it over, and tear 2 slices of cheese to place on top.
Bake in an oven or air fryer at 180 degrees covered with foil for 20 minutes, then remove the foil, add cheese, and bake for 10 more minutes until golden.
tips: Slice potato thinly so the inside cooks through.
It is done when a chopstick goes all the way through easily.

potato-korokke.name: Potato Korokke
steps: Boil potato, peel, mash, and mince onion.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan, sauté pork and onion for 4 minutes, season with 1/2 tsp of salt and black pepper, and mix with potato.
Shape into bite-sized ovals and coat in the order of flour, egg, and breadcrumbs.
Fry in 170-degree cooking oil for 3 minutes on each side until golden and drain.
tips: Let the filling cool before shaping so it holds its form.
Air frying at 180 degrees for 12 minutes is also possible.

potato-omelet-spanish.desc: A thick omelet made with potato and onion.
potato-omelet-spanish.name: Spanish Potato Omelet (Tortilla de Patatas)
steps: Cut the potato into 3mm thin slices and cut the onion into thin strips.
Coat a pan with 3 tbsp of olive oil and sauté the potato and onion over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until softened.
Beat 4 eggs with 1/2 tsp of salt and black pepper, and mix them with the sautéed potato.
Pour back into the pan, cook over low heat for 5 minutes, flip and cook for 3 more minutes, then cut and serve.
tips: Slice the potato thinly so it cooks through to the center.
It is easy to flip by covering the pan with a plate and inverting it.

potato-pancake.desc: A chewy pancake made with just potatoes and salt.
potato-pancake.name: Chewy Potato Pancake (Gamja-jeon)
steps: Peel the potatoes and grate them using a grater or blend them in a blender without adding water.
Place the grated potato in a colander set over a bowl to catch the water, and let it sit undisturbed for 5 minutes. White starch will settle at the bottom.
Carefully pour off and discard only the upper liquid, mix the settled starch back into the potato pulp, and add 1/3 tsp of salt.
Heat a pan over medium heat with 3 tbsp of cooking oil, ladle the batter into the pan, and spread it thinly to 10cm in diameter.
Pan-fry the front side for 3 minutes until the edges are golden, then flip and pan-fry for 3 more minutes. Press down on the pancake over low heat for 1 minute at the end.
tips: Using plenty of oil ensures the exterior is crispy.
Mix 1 tbsp (15ml) of soy sauce with 1 tsp (5ml) of vinegar to use as a dipping sauce.

potato-salad.desc: A smooth salad of boiled potatoes tossed in mayonnaise.
potato-salad.name: Potato Salad
steps: Peel potato, cut into 3cm pieces, put egg together in a pot, and pour cold water. When it starts boiling, boil over medium heat for 12 minutes, take out the egg to cool, and check if a chopstick goes smoothly into the potato.
Drain the water from the boiled potato, put the pot back on low heat for 1 minute to evaporate the moisture, and mash coarsely with a fork.
Slice cucumber thinly, pickle in a pinch of salt for 5 minutes, squeeze out the water, and mince carrot finely. Peel the shell of the egg and mash it.
When the mashed potato cools, add cucumber, carrot, egg, mayonnaise 3 tbsp, salt 1/3 tsp, sugar 1/2 tsp, vinegar, and black pepper, and mix.
tips: If you mix mayonnaise while the potato is hot, the oil will separate, so let it cool down before tossing.
It is also good to stuff it between sandwich bread to eat as a sandwich.

pyeongan-dubu-jeongol.desc: A mild hot pot simmered with tofu, beef, and mushrooms.
pyeongan-dubu-jeongol.name: Pyeongan-do style Tofu Hot Pot (Pyeongan-do Dubu Jeongol)
steps: Slice the tofu thickly, cut the napa cabbage and mushroom into bite-sized pieces, and slice the green onion diagonally.
Add kombu to 800 ml water, boil for 5 minutes, take it out, and season with 2 tbsp soup soy sauce and minced garlic.
Arrange the tofu, beef, napa cabbage, and mushroom in a pot and pour the broth.
Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes and top with green onion.
tips: As it features a clean and mild flavor, keep the seasoning light.
It is also great to add knife-cut noodles (kalguksu) to eat.

pyeongan-gyeoja-chae.desc: Chilled cold salad of shredded chicken breast and vegetables tossed in a tangy mustard sauce.
pyeongan-gyeoja-chae.name: Gyeojachae
steps: Boil the chicken breast in boiling water for 12 minutes, let it cool, and tear it along the grain.
Cut the cucumber, cabbage, carrot, and Korean pear into thin strips.
Mix 1 tbsp mustard, 2 tbsp vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, and 1/3 tsp salt to make a mustard sauce.
Place the ingredients on a plate and pour the sauce to toss right before eating.
tips: Toss right before eating to keep it crunchy.
Adjust the spiciness by the amount of mustard.

pyeongan-kimchi-mandu.desc: Pyeongan-style dumplings packed generously with kimchi and tofu.
pyeongan-kimchi-mandu.name: Pyeongan Style Kimchi Dumplings (Pyeongan Kimchi Mandu)
steps: Mix 2 cups of flour, 1/4 tsp of salt, and 100 ml of water to make dough, then let it rest for 30 minutes.

Chop kimchi finely and squeeze out the moisture, mash tofu and squeeze out the moisture, mince pork, mung bean sprout, and green onion, and mix them with 1 tbsp of sesame oil and 1/4 tsp of salt to make the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly, cut it into circles, place the filling in the center, fold in half, and press the edges to seal.
Drop them into boiling water and boil for 3 more minutes after they float to the top.
tips: Squeeze out the moisture from the filling so the dumplings do not burst.
Add them to soup to make dumpling soup.

pyeongan-mandu-guk.desc: A clear dumpling soup made with large dumplings.
pyeongan-mandu-guk.name: Pyeongan-style Dumpling Soup (Pyeongan Mandu-guk)
steps: Boil beef in water 900 ml for 25 min, take it out, shred it, and keep the broth.
Season the broth with soup soy sauce 2 tbsp, minced garlic, and salt 1/3 tsp, then bring to a boil.
Add dumpling and cook for 3 min more after they float to the top.
Pour beaten egg over the top and garnish with green onion and beef.
tips: You can add frozen dumpling straight from the freezer without thawing.
Adding shredded seaweed makes it even more nutty and savory.

pyeongyang-naengmyeon.desc: Light and subtle Pyongyang-style cold noodles served in beef broth.
pyeongyang-naengmyeon.name: Pyongyang Cold Buckwheat Noodles (Pyeongyang Naengmyeon)
steps: Boil beef in 1 l water for 40 minutes, remove and slice thinly, then let the broth cool, skim off the fat, and place in the freezer for 40 minutes.
Season the broth with 1 tbsp soup soy sauce and 1 tsp salt.
Boil naengmyeon noodles, rinse vigorously in cold water, and squeeze out the excess water. Boil egg and cut Korean pear and cucumber into thin strips.
Place the garnishes on top of naengmyeon noodles, pour the broth over, and serve with 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, and mustard.
tips: Keeping the broth light and mild is the hallmark of Pyeongyang naengmyeon.
It is traditional to eat the noodles without cutting them with scissors.

pyeongyang-onban.desc: Onban features cooked rice in chicken broth topped with mung bean pancake and garnishes.
pyeongyang-onban.name: Pyongyang Style Rice Soup with Chicken (Pyeongyang Onban)
steps: Boil chicken breast in 900 ml of water for 15 minutes, take it out, shred it along the grain, and keep the broth.
Make thin egg garnish from egg, cut it into thin strips, and slice thinly green onion.
Season the broth with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce, 1/2 tsp of salt, and black pepper, then bring it to a boil.
Put cooked rice, chicken breast, and egg in a bowl, pour hot broth over them, and top with green onion.
tips: The rice must be steaming hot for it to feel like authentic onban.
Serving it alongside mung bean pancakes makes it true Pyongyang style.

quail-egg-jangjorim.desc: Sweet and salty bite-sized braised quail eggs that absorb flavors wonderfully.
quail-egg-jangjorim.name: Braised Quail Eggs (Quail Egg Jangjorim)
steps: Boil quail egg in cold water for 3 minutes after it starts boiling, cool in cold water, and peel the shells. Cut green onion into large pieces, and slice thinly Cheongyang chili.
In a pot, combine water 300 ml, soy sauce 4 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, mirin 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and green onion, and bring to a boil.
When it boils, add quail egg and Cheongyang chili, and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
When the broth reduces to 1/3, turn off the heat and let it cool so the flavors soak in.
tips: Leaving it overnight allows the flavors to absorb much better.
It is also delicious to mix the remaining broth into rice.

rabokki.desc: A Korean street food classic combining tteokbokki with ramen noodles.
rabokki.name: Spicy Rice Cakes with Ramen (Rabokki)
steps: Soak the rice cake in cold water for 10 minutes, cut the fish cake into bite-sized pieces, and slice diagonally the green onion. Boil the egg for 10 minutes and peel it.
In a pot, combine water 500ml, gochujang 2 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, and soy sauce 1 tbsp, mix well, and bring to a boil.
When it starts boiling, add the rice cake and fish cake, and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Add the ramen noodles and cook for 3 minutes until the noodles loosen. Do not add the ramen seasoning packet.
Add the green onion and boiled egg, cook for 1 more minute, and turn off the heat once the sauce reduces to a thick consistency.
tips: If you boil the ramen noodles too long, the soup becomes thick and the noodles get mushy.
Placing 1 slice of cheese on top tones down the spicy flavor.

rice-paper-mandu.desc: Crispy pan-fried dumplings wrapped in rice paper.
rice-paper-mandu.name: Rice Paper Dumplings (Rice Paper Mandu)
steps: Take out only the filling from the dumpling and mash it (discard the dumpling wrapper or use it separately).
Wet the rice paper in water for 5 sec, lay it flat, place the filling on top, and fold it.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 2 tbsp and pan-fry over medium heat for 3 min on each side until crispy.
Transfer to a plate and serve with soy sauce for dipping.
tips: Soak only slightly because soaking too much will tear it.
Mix vinegar into soy sauce for dipping.

rolled-omelet.desc: A classic side dish that is great for lunchboxes and drinks alike.
rolled-omelet.name: Rolled Omelet (Gyeran Mari)
steps: Finely mince the green onion and carrot into tiny grains the size of rice. Crack 3 egg into a bowl, whisk well, and mix in 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water, 1 pinch of salt, and the green onion and carrot. Adding water makes the texture softer.
Heat a pan over medium-low heat and wipe a thin film of cooking oil across the surface with a paper towel. Lower the heat down close to low.
Pour in 1/3 of the egg mixture, and when the edges set, poke any large air bubbles with chopsticks to pop them, then roll it up gently from the end and slide it to one side of the pan.
Wipe a little more cooking oil onto the empty space and pour in half of the remaining egg mixture. Lift the rolled egg slightly so the liquid egg flows underneath, then roll it up again.
Repeat once more with the rest of the egg mixture to build a thick roll, gently roll and shape it in the pan, let it rest for 1 minute, and transfer to a cutting board.
Let it cool down slightly (2 minutes) and slice into 2 cm thick pieces. It will fall apart if sliced while piping hot, so be sure to let it cool before cutting.
tips: Starting over high heat will scorch the outside. Keep the heat on low from start to finish.
Fold 1 slice of cheese in half, place it inside, and roll it up to make a cheese rolled omelet.

rose-pasta.desc: A creamy rosé pasta made by adding milk to tomato sauce.
rose-pasta.name: Rosé Pasta
steps: Boil water 1L, add salt 2 tsp, cook spaghetti for 6 minutes, drain while reserving pasta water 50ml.
Sauté bacon in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, then add onion and minced garlic and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add pasta sauce 200g and boil for 1 minute, then slowly pour in milk 150ml and simmer over low heat for 3 minutes. High heat will cause it to separate, so be sure to keep it on low heat.
Add spaghetti, pasta water, and cheese, toss for 1 minute, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: You must pour in milk slowly after the sauce comes to a boil so it doesn't separate.
Using heavy cream will make it richer.

rose-tteokbokki.desc: Rosé tteokbokki combining cream and gochujang.
rose-tteokbokki.name: Rosé Tteokbokki
steps: Soak the rice cake in water to make it soft, and cut the fish cake into bite-sized pieces.
Put water 100ml, milk 200ml, gochujang 1 tbsp, pasta sauce 3 tbsp, and sugar 1 tsp in a pan and boil.
Add the rice cake and fish cake, and simmer over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Top with the cheese and melt it.
tips: Milk will separate if boiled over high heat, so keep it on low heat.
Adding a little red pepper powder makes it spicy.

saeu-chili.desc: Crispy shrimp coated in a sweet and sour chili sauce.
saeu-chili.name: Chili Shrimp (Saeu Chili)
steps: Pat the shrimp dry, season with 1/4 tsp of salt and black pepper, and toss with 1 egg and 4 tbsp of starch.
Fry the shrimp in 170°C oil for 2 minutes and remove them.
Stir-fry the minced garlic in a pan over low heat for 30 seconds, then add 3 tbsp of ketchup, 1 tsp of gochujang, 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of vinegar, and 3 tbsp of water, and boil for 1 minute.
Add the fried shrimp and toss over high heat for 30 seconds before transferring to a plate.
tips: Overfrying makes the shrimp tough. Do not exceed 2 minutes.
Adjust the spiciness with the amount of gochujang.

saeu-gyeran-jjim.desc: Fluffy steamed eggs topped with shrimp.
saeu-gyeran-jjim.name: Shrimp Steamed Egg (Saeu Gyeran-jjim)
steps: Beat egg 4, mix with water 200 ml and salt 1/2 tsp, and strain through a sieve.
Minced shrimp finely and slice thinly green onion.
Put the egg mixture in an earthenware pot and top with shrimp.
Cook while stirring over low heat, and when it becomes clumpy, cover with a lid and cook for 5 more minutes, then top with green onion.
tips: You must cook slowly over low heat for it to be tender.
Straining through a sieve makes it smooth.

saeu-jeon.desc: Plump shrimp coated in egg and pan-fried.
saeu-jeon.name: Pan-Fried Shrimp (Saeu Jeon)
steps: Pat the shrimp dry, make small cuts on them, and season with 1/4 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Lightly coat with flour and dip into beaten egg (2 eggs).
Heat a pan over medium heat, add cooking oil, and pan-fry for 2 minutes on each side.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of vinegar.
tips: Shrimp gets tough if cooked too long. Cook for under 2 minutes.
Making cuts on the shrimp prevents them from curling up.

saeu-maneul-bokkeum.name: Garlic Shrimp Stir-fry (Saeu-maneul-bokkeum)
steps: Prep the shrimp, pat dry, and slice thinly the Cheongyang chili.
In a pan, stir-fry 2 tbsp olive oil and minced garlic over low heat for 1 minute to release the aroma.
Turn up the heat to medium, add the shrimp, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the Cheongyang chili, 1/3 tsp salt, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 30 seconds more.
tips: Sauté the garlic over low heat so it doesn't burn.
Serve with bread for a complete meal.

saeu-twigim.name: Deep-Fried Shrimp (Saeu Twigim)
steps: Peel shrimp while leaving the tails on, make a slit along the back to straighten them, and season with 1/4 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Coat in flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in that order.
Deep-fry in 170°C oil for 2 minutes and 30 seconds until golden brown, then drain excess oil.
Place on a plate and serve with sauce on the side.
tips: Squeeze out any water at the tip of the tail so the oil doesn't splatter.
Enjoy dipped in tartar sauce or soy sauce.

salmon-avocado-bowl.desc: A poke-style rice bowl topped with salmon and avocado.
salmon-avocado-bowl.name: Salmon Avocado Rice Bowl (Yeoneo Avocado Deopbap)
steps: Dice the salmon and avocado into bite-sized pieces.
Mix soy sauce 1 tbsp and sesame oil 1 tsp, then toss the salmon and avocado in it.
Place cooked brown rice in a bowl and top with the salmon and avocado.
Crush and top with roasted seaweed, then sprinkle sesame seeds.
tips: Make sure to use fresh raw salmon on the day of purchase.
If the seasoning tastes too salty, mixing it well with the rice will balance it out.

salmon-chobap.name: Salmon Sushi (Salmon Chobap)
steps: Mix vinegar 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, and salt 1/2 tsp into cooked rice, then let it cool.
Fillet the salmon to a thickness of 0.7cm.
Wet your hands, shape the cooked rice into bite-sized pieces, apply a small amount of wasabi, and top with salmon.
Dip in soy sauce to eat.
tips: Wetting your hands with vinegar water prevents the rice from sticking.
Only use fresh raw salmon.

salmon-don.desc: A rice bowl topped with fresh salmon tossed in soy sauce.
salmon-don.name: Salmon Rice Bowl (Salmon Don)
steps: Slice the salmon into 1cm thickness, and cut the cucumber into thin half-moons. Cut the roasted seaweed into thin strips using scissors.
Mix soy sauce 1 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1/2 tsp, and sesame oil 1 tsp to make the sauce.
Put the cooked rice in a bowl and top with the cucumber and salmon.
Drizzle the sauce over, top with the roasted seaweed and sesame seeds, and mix to eat.
tips: Freshness is key for raw salmon. Make sure to use one labeled for sashimi.
Using smoked salmon makes it safe and easy.

salmon-ochazuke.desc: Chazuke made by pouring warm broth over salmon and rice.
salmon-ochazuke.name: Salmon Ochazuke
steps: Pan-fry salmon without salt for 3 minutes on each side and flake coarsely.
Mix 1 tbsp of tsuyu into 200ml of water and bring to a boil.
Place cooked rice in a bowl and top with salmon.
Pour hot water, crush and add roasted seaweed on top, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Pour the broth boiling hot so the salmon stays warm.
Using kelp-infused water gives it a deep flavor.

salmon-salad.desc: A salad topped with fresh salmon and vegetables.
salmon-salad.name: Salmon Salad
steps: Tear the iceberg lettuce and leaf lettuce, soak them in cold water for 5 minutes, and drain. Cut the tomato into bite-sized pieces.
Slice the salmon thin.
Mix 1 tbsp of olive oil, 1 tbsp of vinegar, 1/4 tsp of salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Place the vegetables and salmon on a plate and drizzle with the dressing.
tips: Use fresh raw salmon and consume it the same day.
It is also delicious using grilled salmon.

salmon-steak.desc: Pan-seared salmon drizzled with a garlic and soy sauce glaze.
salmon-steak.name: Pan-Seared Salmon Steak (Salmon Steak)
steps: Pat the salmon dry with a paper towel, sprinkle with salt 1/4 tsp and black pepper, and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, place the salmon skin-side down, and cook for 3 minutes.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes and 30 seconds more, then reduce the heat to low, add minced garlic, soy sauce 1 tsp, and mirin 1 tbsp, and glaze by spooning the sauce over for 1 minute.
Transfer to a plate and pour the pan sauce over the top.
tips: Do not fiddle with the salmon while cooking; flipping it only once helps keep its shape intact.
