It is most delicious when the inside is still pink and moist.

samchi-gui.desc: Mild Spanish mackerel seasoned with salt and pan-seared until golden.
samchi-gui.name: Pan-Seared Spanish Mackerel (Samchi-gui)
steps: Wipe the moisture off the Spanish mackerel with a paper towel, sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt and black pepper on both sides, and let sit for 10 minutes.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan heated over medium heat, place the Spanish mackerel on it, and cook for 4 minutes.
Flip and cook for 4 more minutes until cooked through to the center.
Place on a plate and serve with lemon juice or soy sauce.
tips: Spanish mackerel is tender, so it will break if you flip it often. Flip it only once.
Air frying at 180°C for 10 minutes is also good.

samchi-mu-jorim.desc: Spicy Spanish mackerel braised with flavor-infused Korean radish.
samchi-mu-jorim.name: Braised Spanish Mackerel and Radish (Samchi-mu-jorim)
steps: Cut Korean radish into 1.5 cm thickness, cut onion into thin strips, and cut green onion diagonally. Wipe the moisture off the Spanish mackerel.
Put Korean radish and 350 ml of water in a pot, bring to a boil over high heat, and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Pour in the sauce mixed with 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of minced garlic, and 1 tbsp of mirin, then top with Spanish mackerel and onion.
Simmer for 12 minutes while spooning the broth over it, then add green onion and boil for 2 more minutes.
tips: Spanish mackerel will break, so do not stir it around; just spoon the broth over it.
Adding 1 pepper makes it spicy.

samgyeop-kimchi-gui.desc: A great drinking snack of pork belly and kimchi grilled in a single pan.
samgyeop-kimchi-gui.name: Pan-Fried Pork Belly and Kimchi (Samgyeop Kimchi Gui)
steps: Cut the kimchi into bite-sized pieces and cut the onion into thin strips.
Place the pork in a heated pan and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side until golden brown, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
In the pan with the pork fat, add the kimchi, onion, and sugar 1 tsp, and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Serve alongside the grilled pork and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: Stir-frying the kimchi in the pork fat deepens the flavor.
Wrapping it in lettuce is a great way to eat it.

sanchae-bibimbap.desc: Mountain herb bibimbap topped with gondre, chwinamul, and fiddlehead ferns.
sanchae-bibimbap.name: Mountain Herb Bibimbap (Sanchae Bibimbap)
steps: Cut the gondre, chwinamul, fiddlehead fern, and bellflower root into easy-to-eat sizes and gently toss them with soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and perilla oil 1 tbsp.
Coat a pan with cooking oil 1 tbsp and separately stir-fry each herb over medium heat for 3 minutes each.
Arrange the cooked rice and herbs in a bowl and top with gochujang 2 tbsp, perilla oil 1 tbsp, and sesame seeds.
Mix evenly before eating.
tips: Season and stir-fry each herb separately to bring out their unique flavors.
Serving it with soybean paste stew goes well together.

sangchu-geotjeori.desc: A tangy fresh salad that tastes best when tossed right before eating.
sangchu-geotjeori.name: Fresh Lettuce Salad (Sangchu Geotjeori)
steps: Wash leaf lettuce, shake off the water, and tear it by hand into bite-sized pieces. Cut the onion into thin strips.
In a bowl, mix Korean red pepper flakes 1tbsp, soy sauce 1tbsp, vinegar 1tbsp, sugar 1/2tbsp, and minced garlic to make the seasoning sauce.
Add leaf lettuce and onion, and toss gently so they don't wilt.
Add sesame oil 1tsp and sesame seeds, mix one more time, and serve immediately.
tips: Shake off the water from leaf lettuce so the seasoning doesn't become watery.
It tastes the crispiest when eaten within 5 minutes after tossing.

sausage-bujim.desc: Lunchbox side dish made with egg-coated sausage.
sausage-bujim.name: Pan-Fried Sausage (Sausage-bujim)
steps: Cut the sausage diagonally into 3 pieces, coat with 3 tbsp flour, and shake off excess.
Beat 2 egg with 1/4 tsp salt and coat the sausage.
Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a pan and pan-fry over low heat for 2 minutes on each side until golden.
Let steam escape slightly and place into a lunchbox.
tips: Making light score marks on them makes kids like them even more.
Serve with ketchup on the side.

sausage-kimchi-bokkeum.desc: An easy pub-style snack made by stir-frying sausage and kimchi together.
sausage-kimchi-bokkeum.name: Stir-fried Sausage and Kimchi (Sausage Kimchi Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the sausage diagonally, slice the kimchi into 2 cm pieces, cut the onion into thin strips, and slice thinly the green onion.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over medium heat, and stir-fry the kimchi and onion for 3 minutes until the kimchi becomes translucent.
Add the sausage and sugar 1/2 tsp, and stir-fry for 3 minutes. Just make sure the sausage gets a light golden brown color.
Add the green onion, stir-fry for 1 minute, and finish with sesame oil and sesame seeds.
tips: Serving it with tofu makes it a tofu-kimchi style dish.
The sausage is salty, so you don't need to add extra salt.

sausage-veg-bokkeum.desc: A lunchbox side dish loved by both children and adults.
sausage-veg-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Sausage and Vegetables (Sausage-veg-bokkeum)
steps: Make 3 to 4 slits in the sausage or cut it diagonally, and cut the onion, bell pepper, and carrot into 1cm sizes.
In a pan heated over medium heat, drizzle cooking oil 1tbsp and stir-fry the carrot and onion for 1 minute.
Add the sausage and stir-fry for 2 minutes, and once the surface turns golden, add the bell pepper and stir-fry for 1 minute more.
Add the ketchup 2tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1tsp, and black pepper, stir-fry over low heat for 1 minute, and turn off the heat once the sauce coats everything evenly.
tips: Blanching the sausage in boiling water for 30 seconds reduces grease and additives.
You can also stir-fry it spicyly using 1tsp of gochujang instead of ketchup.

seafood-tomato-spaghetti.desc: Tomato spaghetti made with shrimp and squid.
seafood-tomato-spaghetti.name: Seafood Tomato Spaghetti
steps: Boil 1.5L of water with 1 tsp of salt, and cook spaghetti for 1 minute less than the package instructions. Reserve 1 cup (200 ml) of pasta water.
Cut shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces and mince onion.
Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a pan, sauté minced garlic and onion for 1 minute, then add seafood and cook for 2 minutes.
Add pasta sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, then toss in the cooked spaghetti and 3 tbsp of pasta water for 1 minute.
tips: Adding pasta water helps the sauce cling to the spaghetti.
Do not overcook seafood or it will get tough, so sauté briefly.

seasoned-bean-sprouts.desc: A basic side dish made simply by blanching and seasoning.
seasoned-bean-sprouts.name: Seasoned Soybean Sprouts (Kongnamul-muchim)
steps: Pour water 100ml into a pot, add the soybean sprout, cover with a lid, and boil over medium heat for 5~6 minutes. Do not open the lid while boiling.
Remove to a colander, rinse in cold water to cool, and then squeeze out the moisture firmly with both hands.
In a bowl, add the soybean sprout, minced garlic, salt 1/2 tsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, green onion, and Korean red pepper flakes, then toss gently with your hands.
Finish by sprinkling with sesame seeds.
tips: You must squeeze out the moisture firmly so the seasoning doesn't separate.
Seasoning with 1 tsp (about 5ml) of soy sauce instead of salt will make the color darker.

seasoned-spinach.desc: The most basic seasoned vegetable made by blanching.
seasoned-spinach.name: Seasoned Spinach (Sigeumchi-namul)
steps: Scrape off dirt from the root end of the spinach with the tip of a knife, split them into a cross shape, and rinse 3 times in cold water.
Add a little salt to 1 L of boiling water, put the spinach in root-first, and blanch for 30 seconds to 1 minute. Take it out as soon as the color turns to a vivid green.
Rinse once in cold water, squeeze out the water firmly with both hands, and cut into 4~5 cm lengths.
Add minced garlic, 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, 1/3 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp sesame oil, toss lightly, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching for too long makes it mushy and loses nutrients. Keep it under 1 minute.
Tossing with 1 tsp (about 6 g) of soybean paste makes a savory soybean paste seasoned dish.

seolleongtang.desc: A milky-white ox bone soup simmered long and deep with beef.
seolleongtang.name: Ox Bone Soup (Seolleongtang)
steps: Soak the beef in cold water for 1 hour to draw out the blood, blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes, and rinse.
Put water 3 L, beef, green onion 1/2 stalk, and minced garlic in a pot, bring to a boil over high heat, simmer over medium-low heat for 2 hours, take out the beef, and slice thinly.
Boil thin wheat noodles, drain, and season the broth with salt 1.5 tsp and black pepper.
Place cooked rice, thin wheat noodles, and beef in a bowl, pour hot broth over them, and top with slice thinly green onion.
tips: Skim off the foam and fat in between.
Serving with kkakdugi juice goes very well with seolleongtang.

seoul-bulgogi-jeongol.desc: Seoul-style bulgogi cooked with a shallow, flavorful broth.
seoul-bulgogi-jeongol.name: Seoul-style Bulgogi Hot Pot (Seoul Bulgogi Jeongol)
steps: Mix soy sauce 3 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and sesame oil, and marinate the beef for 20 minutes. Soak the glass noodles for 30 minutes.
Layer onion and mushroom in a hot pot and place the beef on top.
Pour water 500 ml and simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add glass noodles and green onion and boil for 5 more minutes.
tips: It is Seoul-style only when there is a shallow amount of broth.
Stir-fry rice in the leftover broth to eat.

seoul-sujebi.desc: Hand-torn noodle soup with Korean zucchini and potatoes in anchovy broth.
seoul-sujebi.name: Seoul-Style Hand-Torn Noodle Soup (Seoul Sujebi)
steps: Mix flour with 6 tbsp (90 ml) water and a little salt, knead the dough, and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Boil anchovy and kombu in 1 l water for 10 minutes, remove them, and add potato to boil for 5 minutes.
Tear the dough thinly into the pot and boil with Korean zucchini for 6 minutes.
Season with 1 tbsp soup soy sauce and 1/2 tsp salt.
tips: The longer the dough rests in the refrigerator, the chewier it gets.
Serve with kimchi.

seoul-udeok-haejangguk.desc: A comforting Cheongjin-dong style hangover soup made with ox blood and dried radish greens.
seoul-udeok-haejangguk.name: Seoul-Style Hangover Soup with Dried Radish Greens (Seoul-sik Ugeoji Haejangguk)
steps: Drain the blood from the beef, boil in 1.5L of water for 40 minutes, shred it, and cut the soaked dried radish greens into 4cm pieces.
Toss the dried radish greens with 1 tbsp of doenjang and minced garlic.
Add the dried radish greens, beef, remaining doenjang, and Korean red pepper flakes into the broth and boil for 20 minutes.
Blanch ox blood, add it in, boil for 5 minutes, and top with 1 tbsp of soup soy sauce and green onion.
tips: Add ox blood at the very end and do not boil it for too long.
It is a warm soup that is great for curing hangovers.

shabu-shabu.desc: A dish of thinly sliced beef and vegetables cooked in broth and dipped in sauce.
shabu-shabu.name: Shabu-Shabu
steps: Put water 1L and kombu in a pot, and just before it boils (about 80 degrees), remove the kombu to make the broth.
Cut napa cabbage, mushroom, tofu, and green onion into bite-sized pieces and arrange them on a plate.
Mix 3 tbsp of soy sauce, 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tsp of sugar, and finely crushed mixed nuts to make the sauce.
When the broth boils, add napa cabbage and tofu and cook for 5 minutes, then add beef slice by slice, swish for 10 seconds to cook, and dip in the sauce.
tips: Beef gets tough if cooked too long. Remove it as soon as the color changes.
Finish by adding kalguksu noodles or rice to the remaining broth.

shrimp-broccoli-bokkeum.desc: A high-protein stir-fry seasoned with just half a tablespoon of oyster sauce.
shrimp-broccoli-bokkeum.name: Shrimp and Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Thaw the shrimp, wipe off the moisture with a paper towel, and sprinkle with black pepper. Cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute.
Heat a pan over medium heat, add 1 tbsp of cooking oil, and stir-fry the minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry for 1 minute and 30 seconds on each side, and once they turn pink, add the broccoli.
Add 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce and 2 tbsp (30 ml) of water, stir-fry for 1 minute, and turn off the heat once it gets glossy.
tips: Shrimp gets tough if cooked too long, so take them out as soon as their color changes.
Oyster sauce is salty, so taste it and adjust accordingly.

shrimp-fried-rice.desc: A Chinese-style fried rice loaded with plump shrimp.
shrimp-fried-rice.name: Shrimp Fried Rice (Saewu Bokkeumbap)
steps: Thaw the shrimp, pat dry, and cut in half. Slice thinly the green onion and mince finely the carrot. Beat the egg with a pinch of salt.
Heat a pan over high heat, coat with 1 tbsp of cooking oil, add the egg, stir vigorously to make scrambled eggs, and set aside.
Coat with the remaining 1 tbsp of cooking oil, stir-fry the green onion for 30 seconds, and carrot and shrimp for 1 minute and 30 seconds until the shrimp turn pink.
Add cooked rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes while pressing down with a spatula to separate the grains nicely.
Add 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, 1/4 tsp of salt, and black pepper, mix for 1 minute, add the egg, and stir-fry one more time.
Drizzle with 1 tsp of sesame oil to finish.
tips: Using cold cooked rice makes the grains fluffier.
Stir-frying briefly over high heat keeps the shrimp tender.

sigeumchi-doenjang-guk.desc: Savory soup simmered with spinach and doenjang.
sigeumchi-doenjang-guk.name: Spinach Doenjang Soup (Sigeumchi Doenjang Guk)
steps: Trim the roots of the spinach, wash, and cut into 5 cm lengths.
Pour 500 ml of water into a pot, dissolve 1.5 tbsp of doenjang, and bring to a boil.
When it comes to a boil, add the tofu and minced garlic and boil for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and green onion and boil for just 2 minutes.
tips: Spinach changes color if boiled too long, so add it at the end.
Simmering a handful of anchovies together makes the broth deep.

sigeumchi-gyeran-mal.desc: A vibrant rolled omelet made with spinach.
sigeumchi-gyeran-mal.name: Spinach Rolled Omelet (Sigeumchi Gyeran-malli)
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 20 seconds, rinse in cold water, squeeze out the moisture, and slice thinly.
Mix 1/4 tsp salt and the spinach into 4 egg.
Coat a pan over low heat with cooking oil, pour in the egg mixture in 3 divided portions, and roll it up.
Let it cool and slice into thick pieces.
tips: You must squeeze the spinach dry so the rolled omelet does not break.
Rolling it slowly over low heat keeps the inside moist.

simple-pancake.name: Pancake
steps: In a bowl, mix 1 cup of flour, 1 tbsp of sugar, and 1/4 tsp of salt.
Add 1 egg and 150 ml of milk, and mix lightly until some lumps remain.
Melt butter in a pan over low heat and ladle the batter in.
When bubbles rise to the surface, flip and cook for 1 minute 30 seconds more.
tips: Stirring for too long will make it chewy.
You must cook it slowly over low heat for it to cook through to the center.

siraegi-guk.desc: A savory dried radish greens soup flavored with doenjang and perilla.
siraegi-guk.name: Dried Radish Greens Soup (Siraegi-guk)
steps: Cut the boiled and soaked dried radish greens into 4 cm lengths and season them with 1 tbsp of doenjang, minced garlic, and 1 tbsp of perilla oil.
Boil the anchovy in 1 L of water for 8 minutes and remove them.
Add the dried radish greens and the remaining 1 tbsp of doenjang to the broth and boil for 20 minutes.
Add 3 tbsp of perilla seed powder and green onion and boil for 5 minutes.
tips: Dried radish greens must be boiled and soaked thoroughly to become tender.
Add the perilla at the end so the aroma stays fresh.

siraegi-jjigae.desc: Dried radish greens braised in a seasoned doenjang sauce.
siraegi-jjigae.name: Braised Dried Radish Greens (Siraegi Jijim)
steps: Cut the soaked boiled dried radish greens into 3cm pieces, and toss them well with 1 tbsp doenjang, minced garlic, and 1 tbsp perilla oil.
Put the anchovy in 400ml of water, boil for 8 minutes, and take them out.
Put the dried radish greens, the broth, and the remaining 1 tbsp doenjang in a pot, and boil over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Add 3 tbsp perilla seed powder and simmer for 5 more minutes.
tips: Tossing the dried radish greens in the seasoning beforehand helps the flavors absorb.
Adding mackerel or Spanish mackerel makes it heartier.

soft-tofu-stew.desc: A spicy and soft one-pot meal.
soft-tofu-stew.name: Soft Tofu Stew (Sundubu Jjigae)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips and slice thinly the green onion. Prepare the soft tofu in its package without cutting it.
Coat a pot with 1 tbsp of cooking oil and fry the green onion and pork for 2 minutes on low heat to release the aroma.
Add Korean red pepper flakes and fry for only 30 seconds on low heat to make chili oil. High heat will make it bitter.
Add 150 ml of water, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, and minced garlic, and when it comes to a boil, drop in chunks of soft tofu.
Simmer for 5 minutes on medium heat and season with 1/3 tsp of salt. Crack an egg in the center, cover with a lid, and simmer for 1 minute more.
tips: Do not stir the soft tofu; just press it gently with a spoon to break it up.
Adding clams or shrimp turns it into seafood soft tofu stew.

soy-egg-rice.desc: A comforting one-bowl meal ready in 5 minutes when your fridge is empty.
soy-egg-rice.name: Soy Sauce Egg Rice (Ganjang Gyeran Bap)
steps: Warm the cooked rice in the microwave for 1 minute and transfer it to a bowl.

Heat 1 tsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, crack in the egg, let it sit for 30 seconds, then reduce to low heat and cook for 1 minute and 30 seconds more. A sunny-side-up or soft-set egg with firm whites and a slightly runny yolk is best.
Place 2 fried egg on top of the cooked rice, then drizzle with 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1 tsp of sesame oil.
Crush roasted seaweed over the top and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Break the yolk and mix everything together to eat.
tips: If the soy sauce tastes too salty, pairing it with 2 egg will mellow out the seasoning.
Melting 5 g of butter into the cooked rice before mixing instead of sesame oil turns this into rich, nutty butter soy sauce rice.

soy-kongguksu.desc: A quick 5-minute kongguksu made with unsweetened soy milk instead of whole soybeans.
soy-kongguksu.name: Soy Milk Cold Noodles (Kongguksu)
steps: Combine chilled soy milk 400 ml, mixed nuts 1 tbsp, and sesame seeds 1 tbsp in a blender, blend until smooth, season with salt 1/2 tsp, and keep in the refrigerator to chill.
Cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Add thin wheat noodles to boiling water 2 L and boil for 3 min. Rinse thoroughly in cold water and drain well.
Place thin wheat noodles in a bowl, pour the cold soy milk broth over them, and top with cucumber.
tips: Make sure the soy milk is well chilled. Adding ice is also good.
Blending nuts enhances the nutty flavor of the soy milk broth.

spam-egg-rice.desc: A satisfying meal made with just Spam and eggs.
spam-egg-rice.name: Spam and Egg Rice Bowl (Spam-Geran-Deopbap)
steps: Slice the Spam into 1 cm thickness.
Coat a pan heated over medium heat with 1 tsp of cooking oil and pan-fry the Spam until golden brown for 2 minutes on each side, using the oil rendered from the Spam to cook the egg as well.
Remove the Spam to a plate, crack the egg into the same pan, and cook over medium heat for 1 minute 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
Place the Spam and fried egg over the cooked rice, and drizzle with 1 tsp of soy sauce, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Spam is salty, so use very little soy sauce.
Blanching the Spam in boiling water for 10 seconds after pan-frying reduces the sodium.

spam-gui.desc: Crispy pan-fried Spam glazed with oligosaccharide syrup.
spam-gui.name: Pan-Fried Spam (Spam-gui)
steps: Cut the Spam to 0.7cm thickness, blanch in boiling water for 10 seconds to reduce sodium, and wipe away the moisture with a paper towel.
Heat a pan over medium-low heat, then lightly spread cooking oil 1tsp using a paper towel.
Place the Spam on top and pan-fry slowly for 2 minutes on the front and 2 minutes on the back. It is done when the edges are crispy and golden.
Brush or gently dab oligosaccharide syrup with a spoon, pan-fry for 30 seconds more, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: If the heat is too high, only the outside will burn. Pan-fry slowly over medium-low heat.
Eating it with rice and eggs makes a simple meal.

spam-mayo-bowl.desc: A rice bowl topped with sweet and salty Spam and mayonnaise.
spam-mayo-bowl.name: Spam Mayo Rice Bowl (Spam Mayo Deopbap)
steps: Cut Spam into a thickness of 1 cm, and mix the sauce (1 tsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of water).
Coat a pan heated over medium heat with 1 tsp of cooking oil and pan-fry Spam until golden on both sides for 2 minutes each.
Pour the sauce and simmer for 1 minute while spooning it over the Spam. When the sauce is mostly reduced and the Spam is glossy, turn off the heat.
Cook egg in the same pan for 1 minute and 30 seconds and set aside.
Place Spam and egg on top of cooked rice, drizzle 1 tbsp of mayonnaise in a zigzag pattern, and top with roasted seaweed and sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching Spam in boiling water for 10 seconds reduces the sodium.
Mixing 1/2 tsp (about 3g) of gochujang into mayonnaise creates a spicy mayo sauce.

spicy-pork.name: Spicy Pork Stir-Fry (Jeyuk Bokkeum)
steps: Mix 1.5 tbsp of gochujang, 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of sugar, 1 tbsp of minced garlic, 1 tbsp of sesame oil, and black pepper to make a sauce, then coat 300 g of pork and marinate for 15 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips about 0.5cm thick, and slice thinly the green onion.

Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan heated over high heat, spread out the pork and sear for 2 minutes, then stir-fry for 5 minutes while turning it over, once the outside turns red and liquid starts to form.
Add the onion and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes longer until the onion becomes translucent, then add the green onion and stir-fry for 1 minute.
If there is too much liquid, stir-fry for 1 minute longer over high heat as if reducing it to make it glossy.
tips: Adding 1 tbsp (21g) of oligosaccharide to the marinade gives it a nice shine.
Either pork belly or pork shoulder works great; if there is too much fat, wipe it off with a paper towel.

spinach-egg-bokkeum.desc: A simple side dish of spinach and egg stir-fried with garlic flavor.
spinach-egg-bokkeum.name: Spinach Egg Stir-Fry (Sigeumchi Gyeran Bokkeum)
steps: Trim the roots of the spinach, wash it, and cut it into 5cm lengths. Beat the egg with a pinch of salt.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1/2 tbsp (about 7ml) of cooking oil, scramble the egg, and set it aside.
In the remaining oil, stir-fry the minced garlic for 20 seconds, add the spinach, stir-fry for 1 minute, and season with 1/4 tsp of salt.
Add the egg, mix for 30 seconds, and finish.
tips: Turn off the heat as soon as the spinach wilts. Stir-frying it too long will create water.
Adding a few drops of sesame oil makes it nutty.

squid-jeon.desc: Savory squid pancake made with chewy squid.
squid-jeon.name: Squid Pancake (Squid-jeon)
steps: Peel the squid and mince finely. Slice thinly the green onion and mince the Cheongyang chili.
Mix 5 tbsp Korean pancake mix, egg, and 4 tbsp water, then mix in squid, green onion, and Cheongyang chili.
Heat cooking oil in a pan, drop spoonfuls of the mixture, and pan-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes on each side.
Serve on a plate with soy sauce with vinegar on the side.
tips: Pat the squid dry with a paper towel so the batter is not too watery.
Cooking too long will make it chewy.

ssalguksu-bokkeum.desc: Pad Thai-style stir-fried rice noodles with mung bean sprout, egg, and shrimp.
ssalguksu-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Rice Noodles
steps: Soak the rice noodles in 1 L of lukewarm water for 20 minutes, then drain in a colander. Pat the shrimp dry and cut the onion into thin strips. Crush the mixed nuts coarsely.
Mix 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, 1 tsp of sugar, and 1 tbsp of vinegar to make the sauce.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1 tbsp of cooking oil, stir-fry the shrimp and onion for 1 minute 30 seconds, push them to one side, crack the egg, and scramble.
Add the rice noodles and sauce, stir-fry for 2 minutes, and once the noodles become translucent, add the mung bean sprout and stir-fry for 30 more seconds.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with mixed nuts.
tips: Soaking the rice noodles too long will make them break during stir-frying. 20 minutes is enough.
If the noodles stick to the pan, add 1 tbsp (15 ml) of water at a time to loosen them.

ssukgat-dubu-muchim.desc: A mild and aromatic seasoned tofu dish with crown daisy.
ssukgat-dubu-muchim.name: Crown Daisy Tofu Salad (Ssukgat Dubu-muchim)
steps: Blanch the crown daisy in boiling water for only 10 seconds, rinse in cold water, squeeze out the water, and cut into 3 cm lengths.
Blanch the tofu in boiling water for 3 minutes, wrap in a cotton cloth to squeeze out all the water firmly, and mash it.
Mix the mashed tofu with sesame oil 1 tbsp, salt 1/3 tsp, minced garlic, and sesame seeds.
Add the crown daisy and toss gently.
tips: You must squeeze the tofu completely to keep it from getting soggy.
Do not let the blanched crown daisy sit for too long; season it right away.

steamed-egg.desc: Tender, silky steamed egg made easily in the microwave or a pot without an earthenware bowl.
steamed-egg.name: Steamed Egg (Gyeran Jjim)
steps: Crack 3 egg into a bowl and whisk with chopsticks until no stringy white clumps remain. Stir in 150 ml of water and 1/3 tsp of salt, then pass the mixture through a fine sieve for extra silkiness.
Pour the egg mixture into a heatproof bowl (about 14 cm in diameter) and skim off any surface bubbles with a spoon. Top with the green onion.

Microwave method: Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a lid, microwave at 700W for 2 minutes and 30 seconds, stir once, and microwave for 1 minute more. It is done when the center is set and no longer jiggles.
Stovetop pot method: Pour water 2 cm deep into a pot, bring to a boil, reduce the heat to low, set the bowl inside, cover with a lid, and steam for 12 minutes.
Drizzle a few drops of sesame oil over the top and serve immediately.
tips: Swapping the water for anchovy broth or kelp broth (150 ml) boosts the umami flavor.
A rough 1:1 volume ratio of egg to water strikes the ideal balance between firm and silky.

stir-fried-potato.desc: A simple everyday side dish made by cutting potatoes into thin strips and stir-frying them.
stir-fried-potato.name: Stir-Fried Potatoes (Gamja-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the potato into 3mm thick strips and soak in cold water for 5 minutes to remove starch. Drain thoroughly in a colander. Cut the onion and carrot into thin strips as well.
Heat a pan over medium heat with 1 tbsp of cooking oil, and stir-fry the onion and carrot first for 1 minute.
Add the potato and stir-fry over medium heat for 4~5 minutes. It is done when the potatoes become translucent and the edges look slightly cooked.
Season with 1/3 tsp of salt, stir-fry for 1 more minute, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Removing the starch thoroughly prevents them from becoming sticky and keeps them crisp.
Stir-frying for too long will make them mushy, so turn off the heat while the potato is still slightly firm.

stir-fried-zucchini.desc: A clean and light side dish stir-fried with onion.
stir-fried-zucchini.name: Stir-Fried Korean Zucchini (Hobak-bokkeum)
steps: Cut the Korean zucchini into half-moon shapes 0.5cm thick and cut the onion into thin strips.
Heat a pan over high heat, add cooking oil 1 tbsp, and stir-fry the onion for 30 seconds.
Add the Korean zucchini and minced garlic and stir-fry over high heat for 2~3 minutes. You can stop when the edges become slightly translucent.
Season with salt 1/3 tsp, stir-fry for 30 seconds more, and then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Stir-frying for too long will release moisture and make it mushy. Stir-fry briefly over high heat.
Seasoning with 1/2 tsp (about 3g) of salted fermented shrimp adds more umami flavor.

strawberry-pancake.name: Strawberry Pancake
steps: Add 1 cup flour, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 egg, and 150 ml milk, and mix leaving some lumps.
Melt the butter in a pan over low heat and pour the batter one ladle at a time.
When bubbles rise, flip and cook for 1 minute 30 seconds.
Stack on a plate and top with sliced strawberry.
tips: Cook slowly over low heat so it cooks through to the center.
Serve with heavy cream or yogurt.

strawberry-sandwich.desc: Sweet sandwich filled with strawberry and heavy cream.
strawberry-sandwich.name: Strawberry Cream Sandwich
steps: Add 1 tbsp sugar to 100 ml of heavy cream and whip until stiff peaks form.
Trim the crusts of the sandwich bread, remove the stems of the strawberry, and cut in half.
Spread the heavy cream on 2 slices of sandwich bread and arrange the strawberry neatly.
Cover with heavy cream, cover with the remaining sandwich bread, wrap in plastic wrap, set in the refrigerator for 20 minutes, and cut in half.
tips: The heavy cream whips up well when it is cold.
Wrapping it in plastic wrap and chilling it makes the cross section neat.

strawberry-yogurt-bowl.desc: Yogurt bowl topped with strawberry and oatmeal.
strawberry-yogurt-bowl.name: Strawberry Yogurt Bowl
steps: Remove the stems from the strawberry, wash, and cut in half.
Put the yogurt in a bowl and sprinkle the oatmeal.
Top with the strawberry and drizzle 1 tsp honey.
Scoop and eat right away with a spoon.
tips: Wash the strawberry right before eating so they do not get mushy.
You can use frozen strawberry.

sukju-egg-bokkeum.desc: A combination of mung bean sprouts and eggs ready in just 5 minutes.
sukju-egg-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Mung Bean Sprouts and Eggs
steps: Wash the mung bean sprout, drain, and slice thinly the green onion. Beat the egg with a pinch of salt.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1/2 tbsp (about 7ml) of cooking oil, scramble the egg, and set aside.
In the remaining oil, stir-fry the green onion for 20 seconds, add the mung bean sprout, stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute, and season with 1/3 tsp of salt.
Add back the egg, mix for 20 seconds, and sprinkle with black pepper.
tips: Stir-frying quickly over high heat keeps the mung bean sprout crunchy.
Adding 1/2 tsp of oyster sauce gives it a Chinese-style flavor.

sukju-namul.desc: Basic seasoned sprouts blanched while keeping the crispness.
sukju-namul.name: Seasoned Mung Bean Sprouts (Sukju Namul Muchim)
steps: Rinse the mung bean sprouts in cold water and drain them in a colander. Slice the green onion thinly.
Boil 1L of water in a pot, add the mung bean sprouts, and blanch them uncovered for 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Rinse them in cold water immediately and squeeze out the water firmly.
In a bowl, lightly toss the mung bean sprouts, green onion, minced garlic, 1/3 tsp of salt, and 1 tsp of sesame oil, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Blanching mung bean sprouts too long makes them mushy and smell fishy. Do not exceed 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Leaving them too long after seasoning creates water, so season them right before eating.

sukju-pork-bokkeum.desc: High-heat stir-fry blending the aroma of mung bean sprouts and pork.
sukju-pork-bokkeum.name: Pork and Mung Bean Sprout Stir-Fry (Dwaejigogi Sukju Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the pork into bite-sized pieces and sprinkle with black pepper. Cut the onion into thin strips and slice the green onion thinly. Wash the mung bean sprouts and drain the water.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1 tbsp of cooking oil, stir-fry the minced garlic and green onion for 20 seconds, then add the pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the onion and stir-fry for 1 minute, then add the mung bean sprouts and stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of oyster sauce, stir-fry for 30 seconds more, and turn off the heat immediately.
tips: Add the mung bean sprouts at the end and stir-fry briefly to prevent water from forming.
If the pan is small, stir-fry in two batches.

sunchang-gochujang-bulgogi.desc: Spicy pork bulgogi marinated in gochujang seasoning.
sunchang-gochujang-bulgogi.name: Sunchang Gochujang Pork Bulgogi (Sunchang Gochujang Bulgogi)
steps: Mix gochujang 3 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and sesame oil to make the seasoning.
Coat the pork in the seasoning and marinate for 30 minutes.
Cut the onion into thin strips and slice the green onion diagonally.
Stir-fry the pork and onion in a heated pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the green onion, and stir-fry for 1 more minute.
tips: High heat will burn the seasoning, so stir-fry over medium heat.
It tastes great when wrapped in lettuce.

sundae-bokkeum.desc: Korean blood sausage stir-fried with cabbage and perilla leaves in a spicy sauce.
sundae-bokkeum.name: Stir-Fried Korean Blood Sausage (Sundae Bokkeum)
steps: Cut the Korean blood sausage into 1.5cm thickness, cut the cabbage and onion into thin strips, and cut the perilla leaf in half.
Mix gochujang 1 tbsp, Korean red pepper flakes 1 tbsp, soy sauce 1 tbsp, and sugar 1 tbsp to make the sauce.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan over high heat and stir-fry the onion and cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add the Korean blood sausage and sauce, stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the perilla leaf and perilla seed powder and stir-fry for 1 minute more.
tips: Steaming the Korean blood sausage slightly beforehand makes it even softer.
Adding glass noodles or rice cakes is also great.

sundae-guk.desc: A milky-white broth soup made with pork and Korean blood sausage.
sundae-guk.name: Korean Blood Sausage Soup (Sundae Guk)
steps: Soak the pork in cold water for 15 minutes to draw out the blood, put it into water 1L of boiling water, boil for 25 minutes, take it out, and slice into bite-sized pieces while keeping the broth.
Slice the Korean blood sausage thickly, cut the garlic chive into 3cm lengths, and slice the green onion thinly.
Add the Korean blood sausage, pork, minced garlic, and perilla seed powder 2 tbsp to the broth and boil for 8 minutes.
Season with salt 1 tsp and top with the green onion, garlic chive, and black pepper.
tips: The broth used to boil the pork determines the flavor of the soup.
Seasoning with salted fermented shrimp makes the broth taste even more refreshing.

sundubu-egg-tang.desc: A mild soft tofu and egg soup without spicy seasoning.
sundubu-egg-tang.name: Soft Tofu and Egg Soup (Sundubu Gyeran Tang)
steps: Put 300ml water and 5g anchovy in a pot, and when it starts to boil, simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes and remove the anchovy.
Scoop in large pieces of soft tofu, add 1 tsp soy sauce and 1/3 tsp salt, and boil for 3 minutes.
Crack in 1 egg, do not stir, and cook for 1 minute.
Add sliced thinly green onion and Cheongyang chili, boil for 30 seconds more, and turn off the heat.
tips: You should scoop the soft tofu in large chunks with a spoon so it stays soft and tender.
If you want a spicy kick, add 1/2 tsp (about 1.5g) red pepper powder.

suwon-tongdak.name: Suwon-style Whole Fried Chicken (Suwon Tongdak)
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and marinate with salt 1 tsp, black pepper, and minced garlic for 30 minutes.
Wipe away excess moisture and evenly coat with flour 6 tbsp.
Fry in 170 degree oil for 12 minutes, take them out, and let cool for 5 minutes.
Fry for 3 more minutes in 180 degree oil and drain the oil.
tips: Frying twice ensures the inside cooks through and the outside stays crispy.
Serving with radish reduces the greasy feeling.

suwon-wang-galbi.desc: Suwon king ribs marinated in a sweet soy sauce and grilled.
suwon-wang-galbi.name: Suwon Wang Galbi
steps: Soak the pork in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood and make score cuts.
Blend the Korean pear and onion, then mix with soy sauce 5 tbsp, sugar 2 tbsp, minced garlic 2 tbsp, mirin, sesame oil, and black pepper to make the marinade.
Coat the pork in the marinade and refrigerate to marinate for at least 4 hours.
Grill in a pan or oven at 200 degrees over medium heat for 8 minutes on each side.
tips: It tastes even better when marinated overnight.
Trim off any charred parts with kitchen shears before eating.

suyuk.desc: Boiled pork belly cooked with doenjang and ginger to remove gamey odors.
suyuk.name: Boiled Pork Slices (Suyuk)
steps: In a pot, add water 1.5L, doenjang 1 tbsp, green onion, ginger, and mirin 2 tbsp, and bring to a boil.
When boiling, add the pork, boil over high heat for 5 minutes, then reduce to medium heat and boil for 45 minutes.
Pierce with a chopstick, and if it goes through easily, take it out and let it cool for 15 minutes.
Slice thickly against the grain.
tips: Slicing while hot will make it fall apart, so let it cool before slicing.
Enjoy dipped in salted shrimp sauce or ssamjang.

sweet-potato-chicken-salad.desc: A hearty salad of sweet potato and chicken breast tossed in a yogurt dressing.
sweet-potato-chicken-salad.name: Sweet Potato Chicken Salad (Goguma Dakgaseumsal Saelleodeu)
steps: Wash the sweet potato with the skin on, cut into 1.5cm thickness, and cook in the microwave for 4 minutes.
Boil water 500ml in a pot, add chicken breast, cook on high heat for 2 minutes, turn off the heat, cover with a lid, leave for 12 minutes, then let cool and shred along the grain.
Tear iceberg lettuce and cut tomato into bite-sized pieces.
Mix yogurt 2 tbsp, vinegar 1 tsp, salt 1/4 tsp, and black pepper to make a dressing, and toss with all ingredients.
tips: Sweet potatoes are calorie-dense, so keep it around 150g.
Replacing the dressing with lemon juice makes it more refreshing.

tamago-don.desc: Rice bowl topped with beaten egg simmered in a sweet soy broth.
tamago-don.name: Tamago-don
steps: Cut onion into thin strips and slice thinly green onion. Beat egg 2 eggs and set aside.
In a small pan, boil water 80ml, soy sauce 1 tbsp, mirin 1 tbsp, and sugar 1 tsp, add onion, and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in egg around the pan, cover with a lid, cook for 30 seconds until soft-boiled, and turn off the heat.
Put cooked rice in a bowl, top with the mixture, and garnish with green onion.
tips: Do not cook the egg all the way through; turn off the heat when it looks soft and curdled.
Adding chicken or pork turns it into oyakodon or katsudon.

tamagoyaki.desc: Thick, layered Japanese rolled omelet with a sweet and savory flavor.
tamagoyaki.name: Japanese Rolled Omelet (Tamagoyaki)
steps: In a bowl, beat 4 egg and whisk in 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tsp soy sauce, 1 pinch salt, and 3 tbsp (45 ml) water until smooth. Sifting through a fine mesh strainer once makes it even softer.
Heat a square pan or small frying pan over medium-low heat and lightly coat it with cooking oil using a paper towel.
Pour in 1/3 of the egg mixture, pop any bubbles that form on the surface, and once the edges are set, roll it up tightly from the end.
Push the rolled egg to the edge of the pan, oil the empty space, and pour in another 1/3 of the egg mixture, letting some flow underneath the rolled egg. Roll it up the same way.
Roll one last time with the remaining egg mixture and gently shape it by rolling it over low heat for 30 seconds.
Let it cool slightly and cut into 2 cm thickness.
tips: Rolling slowly over low heat prevents the outside from burning while keeping the inside moist.
Wrapping it in a bamboo sushi mat or plastic wrap for 5 minutes helps it hold a firm shape.

tangsuyuk.desc: Crispy fried pork served with a sweet and sour sauce.
tangsuyuk.name: Sweet and Sour Pork (Tangsuyuk)
steps: Cut pork into the thickness of a thumb and season with salt 1/3tsp and black pepper.
Mix starch 6tbsp and water 100ml in a bowl, let it sit for 30 minutes, then pour off the water on top and keep only the settled starch batter. Mix in egg 1.
Coat pork in the batter and fry in 170-degree oil (pour cooking oil into a pan to a depth of 2 cm and heat) for 4 minutes, take out, and fry again at 180 degrees for 1 more minute to make it crispy.
Boil water 200ml, sugar 3tbsp, vinegar 3tbsp, and soy sauce 2tbsp in a pot, add carrot and onion, and boil for 2 minutes. Dissolve starch 2tbsp in water 2tbsp to thicken, and add cucumber.
Pour the sauce over the fried pork and eat immediately, or serve the sauce on the side.
tips: The settled starch batter is the secret to crispiness.
Frying twice keeps it from getting soggy.

tartar-egg-sandwich.desc: Egg sandwich with tartar sauce containing pickled cucumber.
tartar-egg-sandwich.name: Tartar Egg Sandwich
steps: Boil egg for 10 minutes, peel, and mash. Finely mince pickled cucumber and onion.
Mix mashed egg with 2 tbsp mayonnaise, pickled cucumber, onion, 1/4 tsp salt, and black pepper.
Place on 2 slices of sandwich bread, cover with the remaining bread, and cut in half.
Wrapping it in plastic wrap makes it great for a lunchbox.
tips: Soak onion in water for 5 minutes to remove the spicy taste.
Toasting the sandwich bread keeps it from getting soggy.

tofu-egg-jeon.desc: A tofu pancake coated thinly with flour to use less oil.
tofu-egg-jeon.name: Pan-Fried Tofu with Egg (Dubu Gyeran-jeon)
steps: Cut tofu into 1 cm thick slices, place on a paper towel, and drain moisture for 5 minutes. Sprinkle salt 1/4 tsp.
Beat egg 2 finely. Lightly coat tofu with flour 1 tbsp and shake off excess.
In a pan heated over medium-low heat, grease with cooking oil 1 tbsp, dip tofu in the egg mixture, place it in the pan, and pan-fry for 3 minutes on each side until golden.
Mix soy sauce 1 tbsp and vinegar 1/2 tbsp to serve alongside.
tips: If the heat is too high, the egg coating will burn first, so maintain medium-low heat.
Wiping the oil off the cooked pancakes with a paper towel lowers the calories further.

tofu-egg-roll.desc: An egg roll made fluffy and lower in calories by mixing in tofu.
tofu-egg-roll.name: Tofu Egg Roll (Dubu Gyeran-mari)
steps: Squeeze out moisture from tofu using cotton cloth or paper towel and mash finely. Mince finely carrot and green onion.
In a bowl, mix well egg 3, mashed tofu, carrot, green onion, and salt 1/3 tsp.
Lightly coat a square pan heated on low heat with cooking oil using a paper towel, pour 1/3 of the egg mixture, and roll it up when the edges are cooked.
Push the rolled egg to the edge of the pan, grease with oil, pour 1/3 of the egg mixture, and repeat rolling once more.
Let it cool slightly and cut into 2 cm thick slices.
tips: Because tofu is added, it tears more easily than regular egg rolls, so roll slowly on low heat.
Wrapping it in a bamboo mat for 5 minutes makes the shape firm.

tofu-egg-soup.desc: A clean soup made by dissolving tofu and egg in anchovy broth.
tofu-egg-soup.name: Tofu and Egg Soup (Dubu Gyeran-guk)
steps: Put water 600ml and anchovy 10g in a pot, boil on high heat, and when it starts to boil, reduce to medium heat, simmer for 7 minutes, and remove the anchovy.
Cut tofu into 1.5 cm thick squares and slice diagonally green onion. Beat egg 2.
Add soy sauce 1 tbsp and salt 1/4 tsp to the broth, bring to a boil, add tofu, and boil for 3 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg in a thin stream, leave it unstirred for 30 seconds. Add green onion and black pepper, then turn off the heat.
tips: If you stir the egg immediately, the broth becomes cloudy. Wait 30 seconds and stir only once.
Stir-frying anchovy in a dry pan for 1 minute before using reduces the fishy smell.

tofu-egg-steam.desc: An egg steamed dish made smoother and lower in calories by adding soft tofu.
tofu-egg-steam.name: Steamed Egg with Soft Tofu (Sundubu Gyeran-jjim)
steps: Place soft tofu 175g in a bowl and mash finely with a spoon. Slice thinly green onion.
Add egg 2, salt 1/3 tsp, and water 100ml, mix well, and strain once through a sieve.
Put it in a heat-resistant bowl and top with green onion. Pour water 400ml into a pot, put the bowl inside, and cover with a lid.
When it starts to boil, reduce the heat to low, steam for 12 minutes, pierce with a chopstick to check if clear water comes out, and drizzle sesame oil 1/2 tsp.
tips: If the heat is too high while steaming, the surface will crack, so keep it on low heat.
Covering the bowl with plastic wrap prevents water droplets from falling.

tofu-ganjang-gui.desc: Tofu pan-fried until golden and coated in a savory soy sauce.
tofu-ganjang-gui.name: Pan-Fried Tofu with Soy Sauce (Tofu Ganjang Gui)
steps: Cut tofu into 1cm thickness and pat dry with paper towels.
Coat a pan over medium heat with cooking oil 1 tbsp and pan-fry tofu for 3 minutes on each side until golden.
Mix soy sauce 2 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, minced garlic, and water 3 tbsp, pour into the pan, and simmer for 1 minute.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Patting the water dry prevents oil from splattering and makes it crispy.
Add the sauce at the end so it doesn't burn.

tofu-kimchi.desc: A great combination for both drinks snacks and rice side dishes.
tofu-kimchi.name: Tofu and Kimchi (Tofu-Kimchi)
steps: Cut the tofu into 1cm thickness, blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes to keep it warm (microwave on a plate for 2 minutes also works). Cut the kimchi into 4cm lengths.
Heat cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes until the outside turns white, then add the kimchi and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes.
Add the green onion, stir-fry for 1 minute, and finish by adding sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Arrange the tofu in a circle on a plate and place the stir-fried kimchi in the center.
tips: If the kimchi is too sour, try adding 1/2 tsp (about 2g) of sugar.
You can also pan-fry the tofu until golden brown to serve with it.

tofu-kimchi-jeon.desc: A soft kimchi pancake made with mashed tofu.
tofu-kimchi-jeon.name: Tofu Kimchi Pancake (Tofu Kimchi-jeon)
steps: Finely chop the kimchi, wrap the tofu in cheesecloth, squeeze out the moisture, and mash it.
Mix 5 tbsp Korean pancake mix, egg, and 100 ml water, then add the kimchi and tofu and mix well.
Coat a heated pan with cooking oil, spread the batter thin, and pan-fry over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Transfer to a plate and serve with soy sauce on the side.
tips: Adding tofu makes it tender and mild.
Adding a little kimchi juice seasons it just right.

tofu-salad.desc: A refreshing tofu salad with tomato and cucumber.
tofu-salad.name: Tofu Salad (Dubu Salade)
steps: Blanch the tofu in boiling water for 1 minute or heat it in the microwave for 1 minute to cool, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into 2cm cubes.
Cut the tomato into bite-sized pieces, slice the cucumber into 0.5cm thick half-moons, and cut the onion into thin strips and soak in cold water for 5 minutes before draining.
In a bowl, mix soy sauce 1 tbsp, vinegar 1 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Place the tofu and vegetables on a plate, drizzle the dressing over them, and top with sesame seeds.
tips: You must drain the tofu well so the dressing does not become watery.
Adding a handful of nuts (about 15g) makes it nuttier and more savory.

tofu-steak.desc: Pan-fried steaks made from mashed tofu mixed with vegetables.
tofu-steak.name: Tofu Steak (Dubu Steak)
steps: Wrap the tofu in a cotton cloth or paper towels and press firmly to remove as much moisture as possible, then put it in a bowl and mash it. Mince the onion and carrot finely.
Add the minced vegetables, egg 1, Korean pancake mix 2 tbsp, salt 1/3 tsp, and black pepper to the mashed tofu and knead well to make a dough.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and shape them into round, flat patties 7cm in diameter and 2cm thick.
Heat cooking oil 2 tbsp in a pan over medium heat and pan-fry the patties until golden brown, about 4 minutes on each side, then transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, add soy sauce 2 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, water 3 tbsp, and minced garlic, boil for 1 minute to make the sauce, and pour it over the steaks.
tips: You must squeeze out the tofu moisture thoroughly so the patties do not fall apart.
Mixing in 3 tbsp (about 12g) of breadcrumbs makes them firmer.

tomato-egg.desc: The classic Chinese restaurant side dish made at home.
tomato-egg.name: Stir-fried Tomato and Egg (Tomato-Gyeran-Bokkeum)
steps: Remove the stems from the tomato, cut it into bite-sized pieces, and slice the green onion thinly. Beat 3 eggs and mix with a pinch of salt.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, pour in the eggs, and when the edges start to set, stir roughly to make soft scrambled eggs and set aside.

Add 1 more tbsp of cooking oil, toss in the green onion and tomato, and stir-fry over medium heat for 2 minutes. When the tomato softens and releases its juices, add 1 tsp of sugar and 1/3 tsp of salt.
Put the eggs back in, mix gently for just 30 seconds, and turn off the heat.
tips: The key is for the eggs to blend with the tomato juice like a sauce.
Using cherry tomatoes makes it even sweeter.

tomato-egg-soup.desc: A warm soup made by simmering tomatoes thoroughly and swirling in beaten eggs.
tomato-egg-soup.name: Tomato Egg Soup
steps: Dice the tomato and finely mince the onion.
Drizzle 1 tsp of cooking oil in a pot, stir-fry the onion for 1 minute and the tomato for 2 minutes, and mash them.
Pour in 300 ml of water, bring to a boil, and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Beat the egg, drizzle it in thinly, stir once after 30 seconds, and season with 1/3 tsp of salt and black pepper.
tips: If the tomato skin bothers you, blanch it in boiling water for 10 seconds and peel it.
Drizzling a few drops of olive oil at the end enhances the flavor.

tomato-marinade.desc: Sweet and tangy marinated tomato salad.
tomato-marinade.name: Marinated Cherry Tomatoes (Bangul Tomato Marinade)
steps: Remove the stems from the tomato, blanch in boiling water for 10 seconds, plunge into cold water, and peel off the skins.
Mix olive oil 2 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, sugar 1 tbsp, salt 1/4 tsp, and black pepper.
Add the tomato, toss well, and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Serve chilled on a plate.
tips: Peeling the skins allows the seasoning to soak all the way inside.
It can be stored in the fridge and eaten for up to 3 days.

tomato-spaghetti.desc: Basic tomato spaghetti made with store-bought pasta sauce.
tomato-spaghetti.name: Tomato Spaghetti
steps: Pour 1 cup water into a pot and boil over high heat, then add 2 tsp salt when it comes to a boil.
Add spaghetti and cook for 1 minute less than the time written on the package (usually 6 to 7 minutes). Set aside 1/2 cup (100ml) of the cooking water and drain the spaghetti in a colander.
Cut onion into 0.5cm fine pieces and cut bacon into 1cm widths.
Heat a pan over medium heat, coat with 1 tbsp cooking oil, and stir-fry minced garlic for 30 seconds to release the aroma, then add onion for 2 minutes and bacon for 1 more minute.
Pour 250g pasta sauce and the reserved 100ml water, then simmer over low heat for 3 minutes to reduce the sauce.
Add spaghetti and stir-fry for 1 minute so the sauce coats the noodles, then sprinkle with black pepper. Tear cheese finely with your hands and place it on top to finish.
tips: The water contains starch, which helps the sauce cling well to the spaghetti.
The spaghetti cooks for 1 more minute in the sauce, so you should remove it when it looks slightly underdone to prevent it from getting mushy.

tonjiru.desc: Japanese-style soup simmered with pork and root vegetables in doenjang.
tonjiru.name: Tonjiru
steps: Slice Korean radish and carrot thinly into ginkgo leaf shapes, cut burdock root diagonally and soak in water, and cut pork into bite-sized pieces.
Heat 1 tsp of sesame oil in a pot and sauté pork and vegetables for 3 minutes.
Pour 800ml of water, boil for 15 minutes, add tofu, and boil for 3 more minutes.
Dissolve 2 tbsp of doenjang and top with green onion.
tips: Dissolve doenjang at the end to preserve its aroma.
Leftover soup tastes even better the next day.

tortilla-pizza.desc: Crispy tortilla pizza made in a single skillet.
tortilla-pizza.name: Tortilla Pizza
steps: Cut onion into thin strips, cut bell pepper into 0.5cm widths, and cut ham in half.
Lightly coat a pan with 1 tsp cooking oil using a paper towel and heat over low heat. Place 1 flour tortilla on top.
Spread 2 tbsp pasta sauce over the flour tortilla, leaving a 1cm border around the edge, tear and place 2 slices of cheese on top, then add ham, onion, and bell pepper.
Cover with a lid and cook over low heat for 4 minutes. It's done when the cheese is melted and the bottom is golden.
Cook one more flour tortilla using the same method and cut into 6 wedges.
tips: You can also bake it in an air fryer at 180 degrees for 5 minutes.
If you don't have store-bought sauce, you can substitute 2 tbsp (about 30g) ketchup.

tsuyu-egg-udon.desc: A quick 5-minute udon that only requires tsuyu.
tsuyu-egg-udon.name: Tsuyu Egg Udon
steps: Put 400 ml water and 2 tbsp tsuyu in a pot and bring to a boil.
When the broth boils, add udon noodle and boil for 2 minutes to loosen them up.
Crack in egg, cover with a lid, and let sit for 1 minute.
Top with slice thinly green onion and sesame seeds.
tips: Saltyness varies by tsuyu concentration, so taste and adjust with water.
You can also top with dried seaweed flakes or fish cakes.

tteok-mandu-guk.desc: A hearty soup made by boiling sliced rice cakes and dumplings together.
tteok-mandu-guk.name: Rice Cake and Dumpling Soup (Tteok Mandu Guk)
steps: Soak the sliced rice cake in cold water for 10 minutes and drain.
Put water 700 ml, minced garlic, and soup soy sauce 1 tbsp in a pot and bring to a boil.
When it boils, add the sliced rice cake and dumpling, cook for 7 minutes, and once the sliced rice cake floats, pour in the beaten egg.
Add the green onion, drizzle with sesame oil 1 tsp, and top with crushed roasted seaweed.
tips: Soaking the sliced rice cake makes it cook faster and keeps the broth clear.
Pour the beaten egg in a circle and do not stir so it stays fluffy.

tteokbokki.name: Spicy Rice Cakes (Tteokbokki)
steps: Soak the rice cake in cold water for 10 minutes to soften it (thaw frozen rice cakes), cut the fish cake into bite-sized pieces, and slice thinly the green onion.
Put 400 ml of water, 2 tbsp of gochujang, 1 tbsp of Korean red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp of sugar, and 1 tbsp of soy sauce into a pot, dissolve them, and bring to a boil.
When it boils, add the rice cake and fish cake, and simmer over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes while stirring, until the broth thickens and the rice cake is soft and cooked.
Add the green onion and boil for 1 to 2 more minutes.
tips: Adding 1 tbsp (21 g) of oligosaccharide at the end gives it a nice shine.
Adding boiled eggs and ramen noodles (1/2 pack) makes it a hearty meal.

tteokguk.desc: A bowl of soup made with sliced rice cake in a beef broth.
tteokguk.name: Rice Cake Soup (Tteokguk)
steps: Soak the sliced rice cake in cold water for 15 min (thaw if frozen). Beat the egg by mixing the yolk and white, and slice the green onion thinly.
Drizzle 1 tsp of sesame oil in a pot, stir-fry the beef for 2 min, then pour 900ml of water and boil. When it comes to a boil, skim the foam and simmer over medium heat for 15 min.
Season the broth with 2 tbsp of soy sauce, minced garlic, and 1/3 tsp of salt.
Add the sliced rice cake and boil for 5 min until the sliced rice cake floats.
Egg garnish: Drizzle 1 tsp of cooking oil in a pan, cook the beaten egg thinly over low heat, let it cool, and cut into thin strips.
Serve the Tteokguk in a bowl and top with the egg garnish, green onion, and crushed roasted seaweed.
tips: Boiling the sliced rice cake too long will make it mushy, so turn off the heat as soon as it floats.
Adding 4~5 dumplings turns it into Tteok-mandu-guk.

tuna-bibimbap.desc: A hearty bowl of rice mixed with tuna, vegetables, and gochujang.
tuna-bibimbap.name: Tuna Bibimbap (Chamchi Bibimbap)
steps: Drain the oil from the canned tuna, and cut the leaf lettuce, cucumber, and carrot into thin strips.
Put cooked rice in a bowl and top with the vegetables and canned tuna.
Add gochujang 2 tbsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and sesame seeds, then mix everything together.
If it tastes too bland, add soy sauce to adjust the seasoning.
tips: Press the canned tuna in a strainer to remove excess oil so it isn't fishy.
Adding a fried egg on top makes it even more filling.

tuna-jeon.desc: Soft pan-fried patties made with canned tuna.
tuna-jeon.name: Tuna Patties (Tuna-jeon)
steps: Place the canned tuna in a mesh strainer and press with a spoon to completely drain the oil, then mince the onion finely.
In a bowl, mix canned tuna, the onion, 2 egg, 3 tbsp Korean pancake mix, 1 pinch salt, and black pepper evenly.
Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in a pan over medium heat, scoop the batter with a spoon, and drop it into round, flat shapes (6cm in diameter).
Pan-fry for 2 minutes 30 seconds on the front and 2 minutes on the back until golden, then place on a paper towel to drain excess oil.
tips: If the batter is too wet, add 1 tbsp Korean pancake mix at a time.
Mincing 1/2 Cheongyang chili and adding it gives a spicy kick.

tuna-kimchi-fried-rice.desc: Kimchi fried rice enhanced with the savory flavor of canned tuna.
tuna-kimchi-fried-rice.name: Tuna Kimchi Fried Rice (Chamchi Kimchi Bokkeumbap)
steps: Squeeze the liquid out of kimchi and cut it into 1 cm pieces, and drain the canned tuna in a sieve. Heat the cooked rice and break it up.
Coat a pan heated over medium heat with 1 tbsp of cooking oil and fry kimchi for 3 minutes. It is ready when the edges of kimchi become translucent and the sour smell dissipates.
Add canned tuna and fry for 1 minute while breaking it into small pieces with a spoon.
Add cooked rice and fry for 2 minutes while pressing and breaking it apart with a spatula, then drizzle 1 tsp of soy sauce around the edge of the pan and stir-fry for 30 seconds more.
Turn off the heat, and mix in 1 tsp of sesame oil, sesame seeds, and crushed roasted seaweed.
tips: Using 1 tsp (5 ml) of canned tuna oil instead of cooking oil makes it even more savory.
Putting a slice of cheese on top, covering it with a lid, and leaving it for 30 seconds makes cheese fried rice.

tuna-kimchi-stew.desc: A deep, flavorful stew made effortlessly without pork.
tuna-kimchi-stew.name: Tuna Kimchi Stew (Chamchi Kimchi Jjigae)
steps: Cut the kimchi into 5 cm lengths, slice the onion thinly, slice the green onion diagonally, and cut the tofu into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Drain only half of the oil from the canned tuna using a strainer (keeping some oil provides savory umami).
Add the kimchi and canned tuna to a pot and stir-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes. It is ready when red-tinted oil starts releasing from the kimchi.
Pour in 400 ml of water, and once it comes to a boil, add the onion, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 10 minutes. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface with a spoon.
Stir in 1 tsp of Korean red pepper flakes and 1 tsp of minced garlic, then taste. If it tastes bland, add 1/2 tbsp (about 8 ml) of soy sauce or a pinch (about 0.5 g) of salt.
Add the tofu and green onion, simmer for 5 minutes more, then turn off the heat.
tips: If the kimchi is extremely sour, add 1/2 tsp (about 2 g) of sugar to balance the acidity.
Because canned tuna is already salty, adjust the final seasoning at the very end.

tuna-lettuce-salad.desc: A tangy 5-minute salad made by draining the oil from the tuna.
tuna-lettuce-salad.name: Tuna Iceberg Lettuce Salad
steps: Place the canned tuna in a sieve to drain the oil and flake it with a fork.
Tear the iceberg lettuce by hand, cut the tomato into wedges, cut the onion into thin strips, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, and drain the water.
Mix 1 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tsp of soy sauce, 1 tsp of oligosaccharide syrup, 1 tsp of sesame oil, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Lay the vegetables on a plate, top with the canned tuna, and drizzle with the dressing.
tips: Soaking the onion in water removes the spicy flavor.
Adding a boiled egg makes it a hearty meal.

tuna-mayo-bowl.desc: A satisfying, hearty rice bowl made with a single can of tuna.
tuna-mayo-bowl.name: Tuna Mayo Rice Bowl (Chamchi Mayo Deopbap)
steps: Place the canned tuna in a strainer and press down firmly with a spoon to drain all the oil completely.
In a bowl, combine the canned tuna, 1 tbsp of mayonnaise, 1 tsp of soy sauce, and black pepper, then mix well.
To make a fried egg, heat 1 tsp of cooking oil in a pan over medium heat and fry for 1 minute and 30 seconds to 2 minutes.
Spoon the tuna mayo over the cooked rice, then top with the fried egg, crushed roasted seaweed, and sesame seeds.
tips: If it feels too rich, mix in 2 tbsp (about 20 g) of minced onion.
If you prefer less mayonnaise, you can use just 1 tsp (about 4 g).

tuna-miyeok-guk.desc: An easy seaweed soup flavored with canned tuna.
tuna-miyeok-guk.name: Tuna Seaweed Soup (Tuna Miyeok Guk)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 10 minutes, rinse in water, and cut into 5cm pieces.
Drizzle sesame oil 1 tbsp in a pot and sauté the dried seaweed and minced garlic over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Pour water 600 ml, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the canned tuna drained of oil and soup soy sauce 1 tbsp, and boil for another 5 minutes.
tips: Drain the oil from the canned tuna so the broth is not greasy.
Sautéing the dried seaweed makes the broth milky and savory.

tuna-sandwich.desc: A sandwich filled with tuna mayo and vegetables.
tuna-sandwich.name: Tuna Sandwich
steps: Drain the oil from canned tuna and mix with 2 tbsp mayonnaise and black pepper.
Toast sandwich bread in a dry pan for 1 minute on each side.
Place iceberg lettuce, tomato, and tuna mayo on 2 slices of sandwich bread.
Cover with the remaining sandwich bread and cut in half.
tips: Pat the tomato dry so the bread doesn't get soggy.
Adding minced onion adds a nice crunch.

ueong-jorim.desc: A savory side dish of burdock root that gets nuttier the more you chew.
ueong-jorim.name: Braised Burdock Root (Ueong-jorim)
steps: Scrape the burdock root skin off with the back of a knife, cut into 5 cm long thin strips, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, and drain. Cut the carrot into thin strips as well.
Heat cooking oil 1 tbsp in a pan, stir-fry the burdock root over medium heat for 3 minutes, then add the carrot and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in water 150 ml and soy sauce 2 tbsp, cover with a lid, and braise over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Add oligosaccharide syrup 1.5 tbsp, simmer for 3 minutes until glossy, and finish by drizzling with sesame oil and sprinkling with sesame seeds.
tips: Burdock root browns easily, so soak it in water as soon as you slice it.
Open the lid while braising to let the moisture evaporate before finishing.

wando-jeonbok-miyeok-guk.desc: Nourishing seaweed soup boiled with abalone and dried seaweed.
wando-jeonbok-miyeok-guk.name: Wando Abalone Seaweed Soup (Wando Jeonbok Miyeok-guk)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 10 minutes, rinse, cut into 5cm pieces, and scrub the abalone with a brush to separate the flesh from the organs, then slice the flesh thinly.
Drizzle 1 tbsp sesame oil in a pot, and sauté the abalone flesh, organs, and dried seaweed over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Pour in 800ml of water and, once it comes to a boil, boil for 15 minutes.
Season with minced garlic, 1 tbsp soup soy sauce, and 1/3 tsp salt, and boil for 5 more minutes.
tips: Sautéing the abalone organs together makes the broth rich and savory.
Since abalone can get tough if boiled for too long, you can also add it later.

wolnam-ssam.desc: Fresh spring rolls wrapped in rice paper with shrimp and vegetables.
wolnam-ssam.name: Fresh Spring Rolls (Wolnam Ssam)
steps: Boil the shrimp in boiling water for 2 min and slice in half, then cut into thin strips the bell pepper, carrot, and cucumber.
Mix soy sauce 2 tbsp, vinegar 2 tbsp, sugar 2 tbsp, and water 3 tbsp to make the dipping sauce.
Dip the rice paper in lukewarm water for 5 sec, lay it flat on a plate, and place leaf lettuce, vegetables, and shrimp on top to roll up tightly.
Dip in the sauce and enjoy.
tips: Soaking it in water for too long will tear it, so 5 sec is enough.
Using peanut sauce or sweet chili sauce is also great.

yakgwa.desc: Traditional fried pastries made with a dough of honey and sesame oil.
yakgwa.name: Traditional Korean Honey Pastry (Yakgwa)
steps: Add 4 tbsp of sesame oil to flour, rub with your hands until the oil is absorbed, and sift once.
Mix 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of honey, ginger, and 4 tbsp of water, pour it into the flour, and lightly gather and knead into a single ball of dough.
Roll the dough to a 1cm thickness, cut into squares, and poke holes with a fork.
Fry in 130°C cooking oil for 8 minutes, take them out, and submerge them in a syrup made by mixing 4 tbsp of honey and 1 tbsp of water for 30 minutes.
tips: Do not knead the dough; gather and press it together so the flaky layers remain intact.
Fry slowly at a low temperature to cook all the way through to the center.

yaki-udon.desc: Japanese-style stir-fried udon noodles tossed in a savory soy sauce.
yaki-udon.name: Stir-Fried Udon Noodles (Yaki Udon)
steps: Blanch the udon noodle in boiling water for 1 minute and drain in a colander, or microwave frozen noodles for 2 minutes to thaw and separate.
Cut the cabbage into 3 cm widths, cut the onion into 1 cm widths, cut the carrot into thin strips, and cut the pork into bite-sized pieces.
Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp (30 ml) water, and black pepper to make the sauce.
Heat a pan over high heat, add 1 tbsp cooking oil, and stir-fry the pork for 2 minutes, the carrot and onion for 1 minute, and the cabbage for 1 minute.
Add the udon noodle, pour in the sauce, and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes until the noodles are loosened.
Transfer to a bowl and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: If the noodles stick together, add 1 tbsp (15 ml) more water to help loosen them.
Topping with a fried egg makes it more filling.

yakisoba.desc: Japanese-style stir-fried noodles with pork and cabbage.
yakisoba.name: Yakisoba
steps: Blanch the ramen in boiling water for 1 minute and drain. Cut the cabbage and onion into thin strips and cut the pork into bite-sized pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan over high heat and stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes.
Add the onion and cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the ramen.
Add 1 tbsp of soy sauce, 1 tbsp of ketchup, 1 tbsp of oyster sauce, and black pepper, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
tips: Blanch the ramen only briefly so it doesn't get mushy when stir-frying.
It is also great topped with bonito flakes or a fried egg.

yaksik.desc: Traditional sweet rice dish steamed with glutinous rice, chestnuts, and mixed nuts.
yaksik.name: Sweet Rice Cake (Yaksik)
steps: Soak the glutinous rice for 3 hours, drain, and steam in a steamer for 30 minutes.
Add 2 tbsp of soy sauce, 4 tbsp of sugar, 2 tbsp of sesame oil, and 200 ml of water to the steamed glutinous rice, mix evenly, and add the chestnut and mixed nuts.
Place in a bowl and steam again in the steamer for 30 minutes.
Let cool slightly and cut into bite-sized pieces.
tips: Mix while hot so the sugar and soy sauce absorb evenly.
Adding jujubes and pine nuts gives it a more traditional flavor.

yangnyeom-chicken.desc: Crispy fried chicken tossed in a sweet and spicy sauce.
yangnyeom-chicken.name: Korean Fried Chicken with Sweet & Spicy Sauce (Yangnyeom Chicken)
steps: Marinate the chicken with salt 1/2 tsp and black pepper for 10 minutes, then coat with starch 4 tbsp and flour 2 tbsp.
Fry in cooking oil at 170°C for 8 minutes, take it out, let it cool for 3 minutes, then fry again at 180°C for 2 minutes to make it extra crispy.
Simmer ketchup 4 tbsp, gochujang 1 tbsp, oligosaccharide syrup 3 tbsp, and minced garlic in a pan on low heat for 2 minutes.
Add the fried chicken and toss quickly.
tips: Frying twice keeps it crispy longer.
Making it in an air fryer at 200°C for 20 minutes uses less oil.

yangpa-jeon.desc: Pan-fried thin strips of sweet onion.
yangpa-jeon.name: Pan-fried Onion (Yangpa-jeon)
steps: Cut the onion into thin strips.
Mix Korean pancake mix 5 tbsp, egg, water 4 tbsp, and salt 1/4 tsp, then add the onion and toss.
Add cooking oil to a pan over medium heat, spread the batter thin, and pan-fry until crispy for 3 minutes on each side.
Plate and serve with soy sauce dipping sauce.
tips: The batter should be thick enough to barely hold the onions together for a crispy texture.
The sweetness of the onion pairs well with the soy sauce.

yeolmu-bibimbap.desc: A refreshing summer delicacy of cooked rice mixed with crunchy young summer radish greens and gochujang.
yeolmu-bibimbap.name: Young Radish Greens Bibimbap (Yeolmu Bibimbap)
steps: Trim the roots of young summer radish greens, wash, cut into 5 cm lengths, blanch in boiling water for 20 sec, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out the moisture.
Fry egg sunny-side up in a pan greased with cooking oil 1 tsp.
Put cooked rice in a bowl and top with young summer radish greens and egg.
Add gochujang 2 tbsp, sesame oil 1 tbsp, and sesame seeds, then mix well.
tips: Blanching young summer radish greens reduces the grassy raw taste.
It is also great served with ice water like a cold soup rice dish.

yeolmu-kimchi.desc: A cool and refreshing young summer radish greens kimchi enjoyed in summer.
yeolmu-kimchi.name: Young Radish Greens Kimchi (Yeolmu-kimchi)
steps: Cut young summer radish greens into 5 cm lengths, sprinkle salt 3 tbsp evenly, marinate for 40 min, rinse once under running water, and drain.
Dissolve flour 2 tbsp in water 200 ml, simmer over medium-low heat while stirring until thick, and let it cool.
Mix the remaining water 500 ml, flour paste, blended onion, Korean red pepper flakes 5 tbsp, fish sauce 3 tbsp, minced garlic, and sugar to make the broth seasoning.
Add the seasoning to young summer radish greens, toss gently, and place in a container.
Ferment at room temperature for a day and store in the refrigerator.
tips: Handle young summer radish greens gently as rubbing them too much will create a grassy smell.
Serving it over noodles makes delicious yeolmu noodles.

yeongcheon-kalguksu.desc: A knife-cut noodle soup with Korean zucchini and potato in an anchovy broth.
yeongcheon-kalguksu.name: Anchovy Knife-Cut Noodle Soup (Gyeongsang-style Kalguksu)
steps: Put anchovy and kombu in 1.2 L of water, boil for 15 minutes, and take them out.
Cut potato into half-moons and cut Korean zucchini into thin strips.
Add potato and minced garlic to the broth, boil for 5 minutes, shake off excess flour from knife-cut wheat noodles, add them, and boil for 5 minutes.
Add Korean zucchini, boil for 3 more minutes, season with 2 tbsp of soup soy sauce, and top with green onion.
tips: It tastes clean when served with seasoned soy sauce on the side.
Shaking off the noodle flour keeps the broth clear.

yeongeun-chapssal-bap.desc: Nutritious rice cooked with lotus root, chestnut, and mixed nuts.
yeongeun-chapssal-bap.name: Lotus Root and Glutinous Rice Nut Rice (Yeongeun Chapssal-bap)
steps: Soak the uncooked rice and glutinous rice for 30 minutes, peel the lotus root and cut it into ginkgo leaf shapes, and cut the chestnut in half.
Put the uncooked rice, glutinous rice, 300 ml of water, 1 tbsp of soy sauce, and 1/3 tsp of salt in a pot, and top with the lotus root, chestnut, and mixed nuts.
Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce to low heat for 15 minutes, turn off the heat, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Add 1 tbsp of sesame oil and mix.
tips: Soaking the lotus root in vinegar water helps prevent discoloration.
Mixing in glutinous rice makes it chewy and gives it that nutritious rice feel.

yeongeun-jeon.name: Pan-fried Lotus Root (Yeongeun-jeon)
steps: Peel the lotus root, slice 5mm thick, blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes, and pat dry.
Mix Korean pancake mix 5 tbsp, egg 1, water 3 tbsp, and salt 1/4 tsp to make batter.
Add cooking oil to a pan, coat the lotus root in the batter, and pan-fry over medium heat for 3 minutes on each side.
Plate and serve with soy sauce dipping sauce.
tips: Blanching before pan-frying helps it cook thoroughly to the center.
Blanching in water with a drop of vinegar keeps it white.

yeongeun-jorim.desc: A sweet soy-braised lotus root dish that maintains a crunchy texture.
yeongeun-jorim.name: Braised Lotus Root (Yeongeun-jorim)
steps: Peel the lotus root, slice it 0.5 cm thick, and soak it in 500 ml of water mixed with vinegar 1 tbsp for 10 minutes to prevent browning.
Blanch the lotus root in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain in a colander.
Add cooking oil 1 tsp to a pan, stir-fry the lotus root for 1 minute, then add water 150 ml and soy sauce 2 tbsp to boil.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, add oligosaccharide syrup 1 tbsp, simmer for 3 more minutes until glossy, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Soaking it in vinegar water prevents the lotus root from turning black.
It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

yogurt-oat-bowl.desc: A bowl of yogurt made in 3 minutes without heat.
yogurt-oat-bowl.name: Yogurt Oatmeal Bowl (Yogurt Oteumil Bol)
steps: Put yogurt 150g in a bowl.
Top with oatmeal 20g and let it sit for 3 minutes to soften slightly.
Coarsely crush mixed nuts 1 tbsp and put on top.
Drizzle with oligosaccharide syrup 1 tsp, mix, and eat.
tips: Roasting the oatmeal in a dry pan for 1 minute makes it nuttier.
If it lacks sweetness, serve with a slice of apple or banana.

yubu-chobap.desc: Lunchbox rice pockets wrapped in sweet and sour fried tofu pouches.
yubu-chobap.name: Tofu Skin Rice Pockets (Yubu-chobap)
steps: Mix the cooked rice with 2 tbsp of vinegar, 1 tbsp of sugar, and 1/2 tsp of salt, and let it cool.
Finely mince the carrot, fry in a dry pan for 1 minute, and mix into the cooked rice along with the sesame seeds.
Squeeze the moisture out of the fried tofu pouches, open the ends, shape the cooked rice into bite-sized portions, and fill them 80% full.
Fold the openings closed and arrange on a plate.
tips: Blanching the fried tofu pouches to remove excess oil makes them cleaner.
They will burst if stuffed too full, so only fill them 80%.

yubu-udon.desc: Warm tsuyu udon topped with fried tofu pouches.
yubu-udon.name: Fried Tofu Udon (Yubu Udon)
steps: Combine water 400ml and tsuyu 3 tbsp in a pot and bring to a boil.
Blanch the udon noodle in boiling water for 1 min and place it in a bowl.
Pour the broth and top with fried tofu pouch, slice thinly green onion, and crushed roasted seaweed.
Enjoy immediately while hot.
tips: Let the fried tofu pouch soak in the broth for a moment to absorb the flavor.
Add more water if the tsuyu is too concentrated.

yukgaejang-style.desc: A spicy beef soup loaded with mung bean sprout and fiddlehead fern.
yukgaejang-style.name: Spicy Beef Soup (Yukgaejang)
steps: Soak beef in cold water for 15 minutes to remove blood, put it in 1.2L of water and boil over medium heat for 30 minutes, then take it out and shred along the grain. Keep the broth as is.
Cut green onion into 8cm lengths and halve them, and cut fiddlehead fern to 5cm.
In a pan, stir-fry 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp Korean red pepper flakes, and 1 tbsp minced garlic over low heat for 1 minute to make chili oil.
Add the shredded beef, fiddlehead fern, and green onion, toss for 2 minutes, transfer everything to the broth, add 2 tbsp soup soy sauce, and boil for 15 minutes.
Add mung bean sprout and boil for just 3 more minutes.
tips: Stir-frying Korean red pepper flakes in oil first makes the broth deep and spicy.
Add mung bean sprout at the end so they stay crisp.

yukjeon.desc: Tender beef slices coated in flour and egg, then pan-fried.
yukjeon.name: Pan-Fried Beef Slices (Yukjeon)
steps: Pat the beef dry with paper towels and season with 1/4 tsp of salt and black pepper.
Lightly coat with flour and dip into beaten egg (2 eggs).
Heat a pan over medium heat, add 2 tbsp of cooking oil, and pan-fry for 1 minute and 30 seconds on each side.
Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce made by mixing 1 tbsp of soy sauce and 1/2 tbsp of vinegar.
tips: Thin meat cooks quickly, so do not overcook it.
Keep the heat at medium to prevent the egg coating from burning.

zucchini-egg-bokkeum.desc: Simple stir-fried Korean zucchini and eggs seasoned only with salt.
zucchini-egg-bokkeum.name: Zucchini and Egg Stir-Fry (Aehobak Gyeran Bokkeum)
steps: Cut Korean zucchini into half-moon shapes 0.5cm thick, and cut onion into thin strips. Beat egg with a pinch of salt.
In a pan heated over high heat, drizzle cooking oil 1/2 tbsp (about 7ml), add egg, stir vigorously to make scrambled eggs, and set aside.
Using the remaining oil, sauté onion for 30 seconds and Korean zucchini for 2 minutes while seasoning with salt 1/3 tsp.
Put the egg back in, toss for 30 seconds, and finish.
tips: Stir-fry Korean zucchini briefly over high heat so it doesn't release water.
Adding 1/2 tsp of salted fermented shrimp adds an extra savory depth.

zucchini-jeon.desc: A traditional holiday side dish made by coating Korean zucchini in egg and pan-frying it.
zucchini-jeon.name: Korean Zucchini Pancake (Hobak-jeon)
steps: Cut the Korean zucchini into 0.7cm-thick round slices, sprinkle with salt 1 pinch, let sit for 5 minutes, and then wipe away the moisture with a paper towel.
Beat the egg 2 and mix in salt a little.
Lightly coat both sides of the Korean zucchini with Korean pancake mix and shake off the excess gently.
Heat a pan over medium heat, add cooking oil 3 tbsp, coat the Korean zucchini in egg, and place them in the pan.
Pan-fry the front side for 2~3 minutes and the back side for 2 minutes until golden brown, then transfer to a paper towel to drain the oil.
tips: If you don't have Korean pancake mix, mix 50g of flour with 1/3 tsp of salt to use instead.
Too high of a heat will burn the egg coating, so be sure to keep it on medium heat.
